/* atax.c: this file is part of PolyBench/C */

#include <stdio.h>
#include <unistd.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <math.h>

/* Include polybench common header. */
#include <polybench.h>

/* Include benchmark-specific header. */
#include "atax.h"


/* Array initialization. */
static
void init_array (int m, int n,
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(A,M,N,m,n),
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(x,N,n))
{
  int i, j;
  DATA_TYPE fn;
  fn = (DATA_TYPE)n;

  for (i = 0; i < n; i++)
      x[i] = 1 + (i / fn);
  for (i = 0; i < m; i++)
    for (j = 0; j < n; j++)
      A[i][j] = (DATA_TYPE) ((i+j) % n) / (5*m);
}


/* DCE code. Must scan the entire live-out data.
   Can be used also to check the correctness of the output. */
static
void print_array(int n,
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(y,N,n))

{
  int i;

  POLYBENCH_DUMP_START;
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_BEGIN("y");
  for (i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    if (i % 20 == 0) fprintf (POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, "\n");
    fprintf (POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, DATA_PRINTF_MODIFIER, y[i]);
  }
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_END("y");
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_FINISH;
}


/* Main computational kernel. The whole function will be timed,
   including the call and return. */
static
void kernel_atax[[gnu::flatten, gnu::noinline]](int m, int n,
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(A,M,N,m,n),
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(x,N,n),
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(y,N,n),
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(tmp,M,m))
{
  int i, j;

#pragma scop
  for (i = 0; i < _PB_N; i++)
    y[i] = 0;
  for (i = 0; i < _PB_M; i++)
    {
      tmp[i] = SCALAR_VAL(0.0);
      for (j = 0; j < _PB_N; j++)
	tmp[i] = tmp[i] + A[i][j] * x[j];
      for (j = 0; j < _PB_N; j++)
	y[j] = y[j] + A[i][j] * tmp[i];
    }
#pragma endscop

}


int main(int argc, char** argv)
{
  /* Retrieve problem size. */
  int m = M;
  int n = N;

  /* Variable declaration/allocation. */
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(A, DATA_TYPE, M, N, m, n);
  POLYBENCH_1D_ARRAY_DECL(x, DATA_TYPE, N, n);
  POLYBENCH_1D_ARRAY_DECL(y, DATA_TYPE, N, n);
  POLYBENCH_1D_ARRAY_DECL(tmp, DATA_TYPE, M, m);

  /* Initialize array(s). */
  init_array (m, n, POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A), POLYBENCH_ARRAY(x));

  /* Start timer. */
  polybench_start_instruments;

  /* Run kernel. */
  kernel_atax (m, n,
	       POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A),
	       POLYBENCH_ARRAY(x),
	       POLYBENCH_ARRAY(y),
	       POLYBENCH_ARRAY(tmp));

  /* Stop and print timer. */
  polybench_stop_instruments;
  polybench_print_instruments;

  /* Prevent dead-code elimination. All live-out data must be printed
     by the function call in argument. */
  polybench_prevent_dce(print_array(n, POLYBENCH_ARRAY(y)));

  /* Be clean. */
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(A);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(x);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(y);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(tmp);

  return 0;
}

domain:
    # Problem sizes (compile-time constants from atax.h)
    i: dim in [0, M)        # row index of A and tmp
    j: dim in [0, N)        # column / vector index of A, x, y

data:
    # Row-major matrix A: A[i, j] stored at base_A + (i * N + j)
    A[i, j]: in DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j

    # Vectors (1D, contiguous)
    x[j]:    in    DATA_TYPE = (j) -> j
    y[j]:    out   DATA_TYPE = (j) -> j
    tmp[i]:  out   DATA_TYPE = (i) -> i
        # tmp is logically an output of kernel_atax, but is only used
        # to compute y and is not read after the kernel in this benchmark.

parameters:
    # Tuning parameters (supplied based on hardware; not affecting semantics)
    I_BLOCK:   int  # tile size along i (rows) for better cache usage
    J_BLOCK:   int  # tile size along j (columns) for better cache/SIMD usage
    VEC_WIDTH: int  # SIMD width (e.g., 8 for AVX2 double, 16 for AVX-512 float)
    I_UNROLL:  int  # unroll factor along i inside tiles
    T:         int  # maximum number of worker threads (≤ hardware threads)

computation:
    # Stage 0: initialize y to zero (matches the first loop in kernel_atax)
    S_init_y:
        for j:
            y[j] = 0

    # Stage 1: tmp = A * x
    #   tmp[i] = sum_j A[i, j] * x[j]
    # This is a standard row-major matrix-vector product.
    S_tmp:
        for i:
            tmp[i] = sum(j, A[i, j] * x[j])

    # Stage 2: y = y + A^T * tmp
    #   y[j] = y[j] + sum_i A[i, j] * tmp[i]
    # Combined with S_init_y this implements y = A^T * (A * x).
    S_y:
        for i:
            for j:
                y[j] = y[j] + A[i, j] * tmp[i]

dependencies:
    # y must be zeroed before it is used as an accumulation target.
    for j in [0, N), i in [0, M):
        S_init_y(j) -> S_y(i, j)

    # For each row i, tmp[i] must be fully computed before it is used in S_y.
    for i in [0, M), j in [0, N):
        S_tmp(i) -> S_y(i, j)

    # y[j] is a reduction over i: different i-iterations of S_y that update
    # the same y[j] must respect reduction dependencies, but can be turned
    # into a parallel reduction.
    for j in [0, N), i in [0, M-1]:
        S_y(i, j) -> S_y(i + 1, j)

optimization:
    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # New directive: fuse(S1, S2, DIM)
    #   Conceptually merges loops over DIM for statements S1 and S2 when
    #   they share the same iteration space. For each DIM value v,
    #   S1(v) executes before S2(v); different v iterations remain
    #   reorderable subject to dependencies.
    #------------------------------------------------------------

    # 1) Fuse tmp computation and y update by row.
    #    Implementation: for each i, compute tmp[i] (dot product) and then
    #    immediately update y using that tmp[i]. This matches the original
    #    C schedule, keeps tmp[i] in registers, and shortens its live range.
    fuse(S_tmp, S_y, i)

    # 2) Tile (block) the i and j dimensions to improve cache reuse of A and y.
    #    - In S_tmp, tiling j helps when N is large by operating on x in chunks.
    #    - In S_y, tiling both i and j improves spatial locality in A and y.
    block(i, iB, I_BLOCK)   # outer tile index iB, inner index i within tile
    block(j, jB, J_BLOCK)   # outer tile index jB, inner index j within tile

    # 3) Ensure inner loops iterate over j (contiguous dimension).
    #    A is row-major: A[i, j] has j as the fastest-varying index.
    #    x[j] and y[j] are also contiguous. This favors vectorization.
    #    hoist(iB) / hoist(jB) indicate that tile loops are placed as
    #    outer as possible, leaving j as the innermost loop.
    hoist(iB)
    hoist(jB)
    # After tiling, the core compute structure is:
    #   for iB
    #     for jB
    #       for i in tile(iB)
    #         for j in tile(jB)
    #           ...  (dot product or y update)

    # 4) Vectorize inner loops over j.
    #    Both the tmp[i] dot product and the y[j] update become
    #    SIMD-friendly: they stream through A[i, j] and x[j] or y[j].
    vectorize(j, VEC_WIDTH)

    # 5) Unroll inner i loops inside tiles to expose ILP and reduce control
    #    overhead, especially in the y-update where each j iteration performs
    #    a small number of independent multiply-adds for consecutive rows.
    unroll(i, I_UNROLL)

    # 6) Parallelize across tiles of the row dimension i.
    #    - For S_tmp: different i-iterations are completely independent.
    #    - For S_y: y[j] is a reduction over i; implement parallelization
    #      with per-thread private y buffers of size N and a final reduction:
    #          * Each thread t maintains y_private[t][j] initialized to 0.
    #          * Within its (iB, i) tile range, the thread updates
    #                y_private[t][j] += A[i, j] * tmp[i]
    #          * After all threads finish, reduce:
    #                y[j] = sum_t y_private[t][j]
    #      The extra memory T * N * sizeof(DATA_TYPE) is kept within
    #      the allowed < 50% overhead of the original footprint.
    parallelize(iB)
--- END OF MODEL: atax-01 ---

domain:
    # Problem-size dimensions
    i: dim in [0, M)  # row index of A and tmp
    j: dim in [0, N)  # column index of A, and index into x and y

    # Logical thread dimension used only in the optimized parallel schedule
    t: dim in [0, T)

data:
    # Matrix A: size M x N, stored in row-major order
    A[i, j]: in DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j

    # Input vector x: length N
    x[j]: in DATA_TYPE = (j) -> j

    # Output vector y: length N
    # In the C kernel, y is fully overwritten, but we keep it as inout to
    # allow composition with surrounding code if needed.
    y[j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (j) -> j

    # Temporary vector tmp: length M, holds tmp = A * x (row-wise dot products)
    tmp[i]: out DATA_TYPE = (i) -> i

    # Optional per-thread reduction buffer for y, used only in the
    # parallelized optimized schedule (not visible at the external interface).
    y_priv[t, j]: scratch DATA_TYPE = (t, j) -> t * N + j

parameters:
    # Problem sizes
    M: int  # number of rows of A; length of tmp
    N: int  # number of columns of A; length of x and y

    # Machine- / kernel-tuning parameters
    T: int         # number of worker threads, 1 <= T <= 64
    BI: int        # tile size in i (rows), e.g., 32 or 64
    BJ: int        # tile size in j (cols), e.g., 256 or 512
    VLEN: int      # SIMD vector width in elements (4 for double-AVX2, 8 for float-AVX2, etc.)
    FACTOR_J: int  # unroll factor for the inner j loop, typically 2–4

    #DATA_TYPE: floating-point type (float or double).
    #           We assume "+" is effectively associative for reductions.

computation:
    # Stage 0: initialize y to zero.
    # Corresponds exactly to:
    #   for (i = 0; i < _PB_N; i++) y[i] = 0;
    S_init_y:
        for j in [0, N):
            y[j] = 0

    # Stage 1 + 2: for each row i,
    #   - compute tmp[i] = sum_j A[i, j] * x[j]
    #   - then accumulate y[j] += A[i, j] * tmp[i]
    #
    # This is a direct, structured transcription of kernel_atax:
    #
    #   for (i = 0; i < _PB_M; i++) {
    #     tmp[i] = 0;
    #     for (j = 0; j < _PB_N; j++)
    #       tmp[i] += A[i][j] * x[j];
    #     for (j = 0; j < _PB_N; j++)
    #       y[j] += A[i][j] * tmp[i];
    #   }
    #
    for i in [0, M):

        S_tmp_init:
            tmp[i] = 0

        # S_tmp_accum(i, *) is a dot product between row i of A and x.
        S_tmp_accum:
            for j in [0, N):
                tmp[i] = tmp[i] + A[i, j] * x[j]

        # S_y_accum(i, *) adds the contribution of row i to all y[j].
        S_y_accum:
            for j in [0, N):
                y[j] = y[j] + A[i, j] * tmp[i]

dependencies:
    # tmp[i] is accumulated as a reduction over j in S_tmp_accum.
    for i in [0, M), j1 in [0, N), j2 in [0, N) with j1 < j2:
        S_tmp_accum(i, j1) -> S_tmp_accum(i, j2)

    # tmp[i] must be fully initialized and accumulated before it is used in S_y_accum.
    for i in [0, M):
        S_tmp_init(i) -> S_tmp_accum(i, 0)
        S_tmp_accum(i, N-1) -> S_y_accum(i, 0)

    # y[j] is updated across j and across i in S_y_accum. This is a reduction
    # on y[j] with respect to the addition operator.
    for i in [0, M), j1 in [0, N), j2 in [0, N) with j1 < j2:
        S_y_accum(i, j1) -> S_y_accum(i, j2)
    for i1 in [0, M), i2 in [0, M) with i1 < i2, j in [0, N):
        S_y_accum(i1, j) -> S_y_accum(i2, j)

    # Different rows i1 != i2 have no dependencies through tmp:
    # tmp[i1] and tmp[i2] are independent.

optimization:
    # High-level algebraic view (for reasoning about reductions and parallelism):
    #
    #   tmp[i] = sum(j in [0, N), A[i, j] * x[j])          # tmp = A * x
    #   y[j]   = sum(i in [0, M), A[i, j] * tmp[i])        # y = A^T * tmp
    #
    # This is equivalent to the loop structure above (modulo floating-point
    # round-off) and makes clear that:
    #   - S_tmp_accum is a reduction over j for each i;
    #   - S_y_accum is a reduction over i for each j.

    # 1. Scalarization of tmp[i]
    #    tmp[i] is only used within the i-th iteration of the outer loop.
    #    Implement tmp[i] as a scalar register 't' scoped inside the i-loop
    #    (and store t to tmp[i] once at the end if tmp is needed as an output).
    #    This removes repeated loads/stores of tmp[i] inside S_y_accum.
    #scalarize(tmp[i])

    # 2. Blocking (tiling) in i and j
    #    We tile both the row dimension i and the column dimension j to improve
    #    cache locality and to expose coarse-grain work units for parallelism.
    #
    #    i = Ii * BI + ii, with Ii the tile index and ii the intra-tile row index
    #    j = J  * BJ + jj, with J  the tile index and jj the intra-tile column index
    block(i, Ii, BI)
    block(j, J, BJ)

    # Execute tiles in (Ii, J) order, i.e., row tiles outer, then column tiles.
    # This preserves the natural row-major streaming of A[i, j] and of y[j].
    hoist(Ii)
    hoist(J)

    # 3. Parallelization over tiles of rows (Ii)
    #    Different rows of A are independent in S_tmp_accum, and S_y_accum
    #    updates y in a way that is a reduction over the i dimension.
    #    We therefore:
    #      - parallelize the outer tile dimension Ii, and
    #      - treat updates to y[j] as a parallel reduction along i.
    parallelize(Ii)

    #    Custom reduction realization:
    #      - Instead of writing directly to the shared y[j] in S_y_accum,
    #        each thread t accumulates into its own private buffer y_priv[t, j].
    #      - After all Ii tiles have been processed in parallel, we compute:
    #
    #           for j in [0, N):
    #               y[j] = sum(t in [0, T), y_priv[t, j])
    #
    #      - This removes write conflicts on y[j] and preserves the mathematical
    #        reduction semantics y[j] = sum_i A[i, j] * tmp[i].
    #
    #    Memory constraint:
    #      - The additional storage is T * N * sizeof(DATA_TYPE).
    #      - To satisfy the "less than 50% extra memory" requirement relative
    #        to the original footprint M*N + M + 2*N, choose T such that
    #
    #            T * N <= 0.5 * (M * N + M + 2 * N)
    #
    #        which is easily satisfied for typical PolyBench settings.
    #
    #parallel_reduction(Ii, y[j], +) using y_priv[t, j]

    # 4. SIMD vectorization and unrolling over the inner contiguous dimension j
    #    Both inner loops S_tmp_accum and S_y_accum access:
    #      - A[i, j] row-major (j is contiguous),
    #      - x[j] and y[j] as contiguous vectors.
    #    This makes dimension j ideal for SIMD vectorization and unrolling.
    vectorize(j, VLEN)     # apply SIMD over jj inside each BJ tile
    unroll(j, FACTOR_J)    # software-unroll jj to increase ILP and hide latency

    # 5. Optional: fuse y-initialization with the reduction
    #    Since y is overwritten by a reduction from 0, we can conceptually
    #    replace S_init_y + S_y_accum with a single reduction assignment:
    #
    #        for j in [0, N):
    #            y[j] = sum(i in [0, M), A[i, j] * tmp[i])
    #
    #    The actual schedule remains row-major (i outer, j inner) to keep
    #    A[i, j] accesses contiguous, but this view lets the compiler elide
    #    a separate zeroing pass over y.
    #fuse(S_init_y, S_y_accum) as
    #    for j in [0, N):
    #        y[j] = sum(i in [0, M), A[i, j] * tmp[i])

    # 6. Optional: alignment and constant-size assumptions for code generation
    #    - Assume A, x, y, tmp are aligned to cache-line (64-byte) boundaries
    #      to enable aligned SIMD loads/stores.
    #    - Treat M and N as compile-time constants when possible to enable
    #      more aggressive unrolling and vectorization.
    #assume_aligned(A, x, y, tmp, 64)
--- END OF MODEL: atax-02 ---

domain:
    # Problem dimensions (matching PolyBench's m, n)
    i: dim in [0, M)        # rows of A, length m
    j: dim in [0, N)        # columns of A / indices of y,x, length n
    k: dim in [0, N)        # separate column index for the tmp-reduction

data:
    # Row-major M x N matrix A
    A[i, j]: in DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j

    # Input vector x (length N)
    x[j]: in DATA_TYPE = j

    # Temporary vector tmp (length M), not part of live-out
    tmp[i]: tmp DATA_TYPE = i

    # Output vector y (length N)
    y[j]: out DATA_TYPE = j

parameters:
    # Problem sizes (runtime, but treated as symbolic here)
    M: int
    N: int

    # Tuning parameters (all positive integers, chosen for the target CPU/cache)
    T_J:  int   # tile size for j (y/x/A’s column dimension) in both inner loops
    T_K:  int   # tile size for k (A-x dot-product dimension) if separated from T_J

    V_J:  int   # SIMD width (or multiple thereof) for j-loop vectorization
    V_K:  int   # SIMD width (or multiple thereof) for k-loop vectorization

    U_J:  int   # unroll factor for inner j-loops
    U_K:  int   # unroll factor for inner k-loops

computation:
    # Initialize y to 0 (matches the first loop in kernel_atax)
    S_init_y:
        for j in [0, N):
            y[j] = 0

    # Main kernel: for each row i
    #   1. tmp[i] = A[i,*] · x
    #   2. y[*]  += A[i,*] * tmp[i]
    #
    # This is exactly the original two inner loops, just with different
    # names (k vs j) for the inner indices.
    S_outer:
        for i in [0, M):
            S_tmp_init:
                tmp[i] = 0

            S_tmp_acc:
                for k in [0, N):
                    tmp[i] = tmp[i] + A[i, k] * x[k]

            S_y_acc:
                for j in [0, N):
                    y[j] = y[j] + A[i, j] * tmp[i]

dependencies:
    # y must be fully initialized before any accumulation
    for j in [0, N), i in [0, M):
        S_init_y(j) -> S_y_acc(i, j)

    # tmp[i] is reduced along k: init -> chain of accumulations -> final value
    for i in [0, M):
        S_tmp_init(i) -> S_tmp_acc(i, 0)
    for i in [0, M), k in [0, N-1):
        S_tmp_acc(i, k) -> S_tmp_acc(i, k+1)

    # y-updates for a given (i, j) can start only after tmp[i] is fully computed
    for i in [0, M), j in [0, N):
        S_tmp_acc(i, N-1) -> S_y_acc(i, j)

    # y[j] is a reduction across i: updates at (i, j) depend on previous (i-1, j)
    for j in [0, N), i in [0, M-1):
        S_y_acc(i, j) -> S_y_acc(i+1, j)

optimization:
    #------------------------------
    # 1. Declare reductions
    #------------------------------
    # tmp[i] is the result of a reduction over k
    reduction(tmp[i], k)
    # y[j] is the result of a reduction over i
    reduction(y[j], i)
    # These declarations tell the optimizer that:
    #   - the operations on tmp[i] across k and on y[j] across i are
    #     associative/commutative reductions and may be re-associated
    #     and parallelized, as long as the final sums are preserved.

    #------------------------------
    # 2. Parallelization
    #------------------------------
    # Parallelize the outer i-loop (rows of A).
    # Because y[j] is declared as a reduction over i, different i-iterations
    # can execute concurrently, combining their contributions to y[j] via a
    # reduction mechanism (e.g., per-thread partial y vectors plus a final
    # combine, or appropriate atomics).
    parallelize(i)

    # Optionally also parallelize y-initialization, though its cost is small.
    parallelize(j)  # applies to S_init_y

    #------------------------------
    # 3. Cache tiling / blocking
    #------------------------------
    # Both inner loops (over k and j) stream across the second dimension of A,
    # which is contiguous in memory (row-major layout). We tile that dimension
    # to keep active segments of A, x, and y in L1/L2 cache.
    #
    # For the tmp-accumulation loop: i (outer) × k (inner)
    block(k, K, T_K)
    hoist(K)        # hoist the tile loop K just under the i-loop

    # For the y-accumulation loop: i (outer) × j (inner)
    block(j, J, T_J)
    hoist(J)        # hoist the tile loop J just under the i-loop

    # The resulting scheduled structure is conceptually:
    #   for i in tiles / parallel:
    #     tmp[i] = 0
    #     for K in tiles of k:
    #       for k in K-tile (vectorized):
    #         tmp[i] += A[i,k] * x[k]
    #     for J in tiles of j:
    #       for j in J-tile (vectorized):
    #         y[j] += A[i,j] * tmp[i]
    #
    # This preserves the original per-row reuse of A[i,*]:
    # each row is read twice (once for tmp, once for y) in close succession,
    # maximizing cache reuse of that row.

    #------------------------------
    # 4. Vectorization and unrolling
    #------------------------------
    # Vectorize the innermost loops over the contiguous dimension of A.
    # V_K and V_J should be chosen to match or be a multiple of the hardware
    # SIMD width (e.g., 4, 8, or 16 depending on DATA_TYPE and ISA).
    vectorize(k, V_K)
    unroll(k, U_K)

    vectorize(j, V_J)
    unroll(j, U_J)

    # The combination of blocking, vectorization, and unrolling encourages
    # the compiler to generate wide SIMD loads/stores on x and y and
    # unit-stride accesses on rows of A, while the outer i-parallelism
    # exploits all cores.

    #------------------------------
    # 5. Notes on data layout and memory usage
    #------------------------------
    # - A remains row-major: (i, j) -> i * N + j, which is ideal for both
    #   inner loops that traverse j/k as the innermost dimension.
    # - No additional large data structures beyond the existing tmp and y
    #   are introduced by this model; reductions over y[j] are logical and
    #   can be implemented with bounded per-thread scratch space, keeping
    #   extra memory well within the 50% overhead constraint.
    # - The high-level mathematical effect is y = A^T * (A * x), and all
    #   transformations respect the original kernel’s semantics.
--- END OF MODEL: atax-03 ---

--- START OF MODEL: atax-04 ---
domain:
    i: dim in [0, M)        # row index
    j: dim in [0, N)        # column / vector index

data:
    A[i, j]: in DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j
        # Dense MxN matrix, row-major as in the C code: A[i][j].
    x[j]: in DATA_TYPE = (j) -> j
        # Input vector of length N.
    y[j]: out DATA_TYPE = (j) -> j
        # Output vector of length N; kernel overwrites it (initial contents unused).
    tmp[i]: temp DATA_TYPE = (i) -> i
        # Temporary vector of length M, holds (A * x).

parameters:
    TI: int  # tile size for i (rows), e.g., 64–256 depending on LLC size
    TJ: int  # tile size for j (columns), e.g., 128–512 for L1/L2 cache
    VF: int  # SIMD width (elements per vector register), e.g., 8 for AVX2 doubles
    T:  int  # maximum parallel workers/threads, e.g., 32–64 on the target machine

computation:
    # y is fully overwritten; initialize it explicitly to zero.
    init_y:
        for j in [0, N):
            Y_INIT: y[j] = 0

    # First matrix-vector product: tmp = A * x
    #   tmp[i] = sum_j A[i, j] * x[j]
    compute_tmp:
        for i in [0, M):
            TMP_DEF: tmp[i] = sum(j in [0, N), A[i, j] * x[j])

    # Second matrix-vector product: y += A^T * tmp
    #   y[j] = y[j] + sum_i A[i, j] * tmp[i]
    # Overall: y = A^T * (A * x).
    update_y:
        for j in [0, N):
            Y_ACC: y[j] = y[j] + sum(i in [0, M), A[i, j] * tmp[i])

dependencies:
    # init_y must complete before any accumulation into y.
    for j in [0, N):
        Y_INIT(j) -> Y_ACC(j)

    # Each tmp[i] must be computed before any use of tmp[i] in the y-update.
    for i in [0, M), j in [0, N):
        TMP_DEF(i) -> Y_ACC(j)

    # Within TMP_DEF, the sum over j is a pure reduction:
    #   tmp[i] = Σ_j A[i,j]*x[j]
    # so different j-iterations only depend on tmp[i] through '+',
    # and may be freely reordered and vectorized.
    # Within Y_ACC, the sum over i is also a pure reduction:
    #   y[j] += Σ_i A[i,j]*tmp[i]
    # so different i-iterations only interact through '+', enabling
    # reduction-based parallelization.

optimization:
    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # 1. Row-wise fusion to reuse A[i, *] and tmp[i] (core layout optimization)
    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # fuse(F, G, dim) := transform computations F and G so that the reduction in G
    # along 'dim' is evaluated incrementally immediately after F(dim) is computed.
    #
    # Here, we fuse 'compute_tmp' and the reduction in 'update_y' along i.
    # This yields the row-wise structure of the original C kernel:
    #
    #   for i:
    #     tmp[i] = 0;
    #     for j: tmp[i] += A[i,j] * x[j];
    #     for j: y[j] += A[i,j] * tmp[i];
    #
    # Ensures each row A[i, *] is loaded once and reused from cache for both
    # tmp[i] and contributions to y.
    fuse(compute_tmp, update_y, i)

    # Ensure i remains the outermost loop after fusion so that the
    # memory access to A is row-major contiguous.
    hoist(i)

    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # 2. Cache-blocking in j for x and y
    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # Work on j-tiles of size TJ so that:
    #   - chunks of x[TJ] and y[TJ] fit comfortably in L1/L2,
    #   - inner loops can be vectorized effectively.
    block(j, J, TJ)

    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # 3. Coarse-grain blocking in i to form parallel tasks
    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # Block rows into tiles of size TI. Each i-tile (I) carries enough work to
    # amortize threading overhead and benefits from reuse of x[J] within the tile.
    block(i, I, TI)

    # Conceptual fused/blocked structure after 1–3:
    #
    #   for I in tiles of i:          # outer row tiles
    #     for J in tiles of j:        # inner column tiles
    #       # tmp[i] accumulation over j in J
    #       for i in I:
    #         for j in J:
    #           tmp[i] += A[i,j] * x[j]
    #
    #       # y[j] accumulation over i in I
    #       for i in I:
    #         for j in J:
    #           y[j] += A[i,j] * tmp[i]

    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # 4. Parallelization over i-tiles with reduction on y
    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # parallelize(DIM) := run iterations of DIM across T workers, subject
    # to dependencies. Here, DIM = I. The y-update is a reduction over i,
    # so tiles of I are independent modulo summation into y.
    #
    # Implementation strategy (privatized reduction on y):
    #   - For each worker w and each active j-tile J, allocate a private
    #     buffer y_private[w, J] initialized to 0.
    #   - Within worker w, update y_private[w, j] instead of y[j].
    #   - After all I-tiles complete, reduce:
    #         y[j] = Σ_w y_private[w, j]
    #
    # Memory overhead: O(T * TJ) elements of DATA_TYPE, which is well below
    # 50% of the original footprint dominated by A[M,N].
    parallelize(I)

    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # 5. SIMD vectorization and unrolling in j
    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # Vectorize over the innermost j-tile loop for both tmp and y updates.
    # This aligns with the row-major layout of A and the contiguous layout of x,y.
    vectorize(J, VF)

    # Small unrolling factor improves ILP and reduces loop overhead.
    unroll(J, 4)

    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # 6. Optional: light unrolling in i inside each tile
    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # Unroll by 2 rows to expose more ILP without blowing up register pressure
    # or harming cache behavior (each row of A still fits in L1).
    unroll(i, 2)
--- END OF MODEL: atax-04 ---

--- START OF MODEL: atax-05 ---
domain:
    i: dim in [0, M)              # rows of A, length of tmp

#include <stdio.h>
#include <unistd.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <math.h>

/* Include polybench common header. */
#include <polybench.h>

/* Include benchmark-specific header. */
#include "bicg.h"


/* Array initialization. */
static
void init_array (int m, int n,
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(A,N,M,n,m),
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(r,N,n),
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(p,M,m))
{
  int i, j;

  for (i = 0; i < m; i++)
    p[i] = (DATA_TYPE)(i % m) / m;
  for (i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    r[i] = (DATA_TYPE)(i % n) / n;
    for (j = 0; j < m; j++)
      A[i][j] = (DATA_TYPE) (i*(j+1) % n)/n;
  }
}


/* DCE code. Must scan the entire live-out data.
   Can be used also to check the correctness of the output. */
static
void print_array(int m, int n,
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(s,M,m),
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(q,N,n))

{
  int i;

  POLYBENCH_DUMP_START;
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_BEGIN("s");
  for (i = 0; i < m; i++) {
    if (i % 20 == 0) fprintf (POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, "\n");
    fprintf (POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, DATA_PRINTF_MODIFIER, s[i]);
  }
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_END("s");
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_BEGIN("q");
  for (i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    if (i % 20 == 0) fprintf (POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, "\n");
    fprintf (POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, DATA_PRINTF_MODIFIER, q[i]);
  }
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_END("q");
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_FINISH;
}


/* Main computational kernel. The whole function will be timed,
   including the call and return. */
static
void kernel_bicg[[gnu::flatten, gnu::noinline]](int m, int n,
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(A,N,M,n,m),
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(s,M,m),
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(q,N,n),
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(p,M,m),
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(r,N,n))
{
  int i, j;

#pragma scop
  for (i = 0; i < _PB_M; i++)
    s[i] = 0;
  for (i = 0; i < _PB_N; i++)
    {
      q[i] = SCALAR_VAL(0.0);
      for (j = 0; j < _PB_M; j++)
	{
	  s[j] = s[j] + r[i] * A[i][j];
	  q[i] = q[i] + A[i][j] * p[j];
	}
    }
#pragma endscop

}


int main(int argc, char** argv)
{
  /* Retrieve problem size. */
  int n = N;
  int m = M;

  /* Variable declaration/allocation. */
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(A, DATA_TYPE, N, M, n, m);
  POLYBENCH_1D_ARRAY_DECL(s, DATA_TYPE, M, m);
  POLYBENCH_1D_ARRAY_DECL(q, DATA_TYPE, N, n);
  POLYBENCH_1D_ARRAY_DECL(p, DATA_TYPE, M, m);
  POLYBENCH_1D_ARRAY_DECL(r, DATA_TYPE, N, n);

  /* Initialize array(s). */
  init_array (m, n,
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A),
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(r),
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(p));

  /* Start timer. */
  polybench_start_instruments;

  /* Run kernel. */
  kernel_bicg (m, n,
	       POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A),
	       POLYBENCH_ARRAY(s),
	       POLYBENCH_ARRAY(q),
	       POLYBENCH_ARRAY(p),
	       POLYBENCH_ARRAY(r));

  /* Stop and print timer. */
  polybench_stop_instruments;
  polybench_print_instruments;

  /* Prevent dead-code elimination. All live-out data must be printed
     by the function call in argument. */
  polybench_prevent_dce(print_array(m, n, POLYBENCH_ARRAY(s), POLYBENCH_ARRAY(q)));

  /* Be clean. */
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(A);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(s);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(q);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(p);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(r);

  return 0;
}

    # q[i] is an addition reduction over the j-dimension
    for i in [0, N), j1 in [0, M), j2 in [j1 + 1, M):
        UPDATE_SQ(i, j1) -> UPDATE_SQ(i, j2)

    # Updates must see the zero-initialized values of s[j] and q[i]
    for j in [0, M), i in [0, N):
        INIT_S(j) -> UPDATE_SQ(i, j)
    for i in [0, N), j in [0, M):
        INIT_Q(i) -> UPDATE_SQ(i, j)

optimization:
    # -----------------------------
    # 1. Cache blocking over rows and columns of A
    # -----------------------------
    # Block the 2D (i, j) iteration space so that we operate on tiles
    # of A of size TI x TJ.  This improves spatial and temporal locality
    # of p[j] and s[j] (reused across many rows) and of A itself.
    block(i, I, TI)   # i = I * TI + i_inner
    block(j, J, TJ)   # j = J * TJ + j_inner

    # Hoist the tile loops to form a tiled nest of the form:
    #   for I in tiles of i:
    #     for J in tiles of j:
    #       for i in I-tile:
    #         for j in J-tile:
    #           ...
    hoist(I)
    hoist(J)

    # -----------------------------
    # 2. Parallelism
    # -----------------------------
    # Parallelize across row tiles I.
    # Each tile I works on a disjoint subset of rows of A and q[i].
    # s[j] is a reduction over i, so updates from different I-tiles
    # can be combined with a reduction (e.g., thread-private s[j]
    # partial sums per tile, then merged).  This keeps additional
    # memory bounded (O(M) per worker) and can be tuned so that the
    # overhead remains well below 50% of the size of A.
    parallelize(I)  # with reduction_add on s[j] over i

    # The simple initialization loops are also parallelizable:
    parallelize(INIT_S.j)
    parallelize(MAIN.i)  # for INIT_Q, if executed outside the tiled nest

    # -----------------------------
    # 3. Vectorization and unrolling
    # -----------------------------
    # Vectorize along the innermost column dimension within each J-tile.
    # This exploits the fact that A[i, j], p[j], and s[j] are contiguous
    # in memory when j varies fastest.
    #
    # After blocking, the innermost dimension is the inner j within a J-tile.
    vectorize(j, VEC)

    # Unroll the innermost j-loop to increase instruction-level parallelism
    # and help the compiler schedule FMA operations efficiently.
    unroll(j, U)

    # -----------------------------
    # 4. Scalar replacement (register tiling)
    # -----------------------------
    # Keep r[i] and q[i] in registers across the inner j-loop.  In C this
    # corresponds to:
    #   DATA_TYPE ri = r[i];
    #   DATA_TYPE qi = 0;
    #   for (j ...) { ... use ri, qi ... }
    #   q[i] = qi;
    #
    # This avoids repeated loads/stores of q[i] and r[i] in the j-loop.
    scalarize({r[i], q[i]}, j)
    # scalarize(VAR_SET, DIMENSION):
    #   Replace repeated memory accesses to the given loop-invariant scalars
    #   inside loops over DIMENSION by register-resident temporaries.
--- END OF MODEL: bicg-03 ---

    VEC_WIDTH: int # SIMD width used along j

    # Initialize s and q exactly as in the C code
    S_INIT:
        for j in [0, M):

    Q_INIT:
        for i in [0, N):
            q[i] = 0

    #   s[j] = sum_i r[i] * A[i,j]       (s = A^T * r)
    #   q[i] = sum_j A[i,j] * p[j]       (q = A * p)
    # The loops are fused so that each A[i,j] load is reused for both sums.
    CORE:
        for i, j:
            s[j] = s[j] + r[i] * A[i, j]
            q[i] = q[i] + A[i, j] * p[j]

    # s and q must be initialized before they are used in CORE.

        Q_INIT(i) -> CORE(i, j)

    #-------------------------------
    # 1. Expose reductions explicitly
    #-------------------------------
    # s[j] is mathematically a sum over i:
    #   s[j] = sum_{i=0..N-1} r[i] * A[i,j]
    # Declaring it as a reduction along i allows parallelization and reassociation.
    reduction(s[j], i)   # '+' reduction along i

    # q[i] is mathematically a sum over j:
    #   q[i] = sum_{j=0..M-1} A[i,j] * p[j]
    # This is a scalar reduction inside the i-iteration and will be kept in a register.
    reduction(q[i], j)   # '+' reduction along j

    # 2. Cache blocking (tiling)
    #-------------------------------
    # Tile the 2D CORE loop so that:
    #   - inner tiles of j fit p[j] and s[j] segments into L1/L2 cache,
    #   - outer tiles of i give good work chunks for threads.
    #
    # Resulting structure (conceptually):
    #   for I in 0..N step TILE_I:
    #     for J in 0..M step TILE_J:
    #       for i in I..min(I+TILE_I, N):
    #         for j in J..min(J+TILE_J, M):
    #           ... CORE body ...

    block(j, J, TILE_J)   # J: outer tile index for columns
    hoist(I)              # move I to the outermost possible level
    hoist(J)              # keep J just inside I for rectangular tiles

    # 3. Parallelization
    #-------------------------------
    # Parallelize across row tiles I:
    #   - Each thread processes a distinct block of rows.
    #   - q[i] writes are thread-local (no sharing of the same i).
    #   - s[j] updates across different I-tiles form a reduction along i, as declared above.

    #   The reduction(s[j], i) can be realized with one temporary s_private[thread][j]

    #   bound relative to the dominant A[N][M] for typical PolyBench sizes.
    parallelize(I)

    # 4. SIMD and unrolling on the innermost loop
    #-------------------------------

    #       q[i] += A[i,j] * p[j]

    # (Modeled as a comment; typically performed automatically by compilers.)
    # - Hoist r[i] out of the inner j-loop and keep it in a register:

domain:
    i: dim in [0, N)     # row index of A, q, r
    j: dim in [0, M)     # column index of A, s, p

data:
    # A is stored row-major as in the original C code: A[i][j] == A[i*M + j].
    A[i, j]: in DATA_TYPE   = (i, j) -> i * M + j

    # Input vectors.
    p[j]:    in DATA_TYPE   = (j)    -> j         # length M
    r[i]:    in DATA_TYPE   = (i)    -> i         # length N

    # Output vectors (fully overwritten by the kernel).
    s[j]: out DATA_TYPE     = (j)    -> j         # length M, s = A^T * r
    q[i]: out DATA_TYPE     = (i)    -> i         # length N, q = A * p

parameters:
    N:  int  # number of rows of A, length of q and r
    M:  int  # number of columns of A, length of s and p

    # Tunable tiling and SIMD parameters.
    TI: int  # tile size along i (rows), chosen for good L2/LLC locality
    TJ: int  # tile size along j (cols), chosen so A tile + p[j] fit in L1/L2
    V:  int  # SIMD vector length along j (e.g., 4 for AVX2 double, 8 for AVX2 float)
    U:  int  # unroll factor for j within a SIMD vector (e.g., 2–4)

    # Upper bound on the number of parallel partitions along i.
    # Implementation uses per-thread private partial sums for s[j] and
    # reduces them at the end. To keep the extra storage below 50% of
    # the size of A, we enforce:
    #   1 <= T <= min(MAX_THREADS, floor(N / 2))
    # so that a T x M temporary array of partial s never exceeds 0.5 * N*M.
    T:  int  # logical max number of threads/partitions along i

computation:
    # BiCG kernel computes two matrix-vector products:
    #   q = A * p        (size N)
    #   s = A^T * r      (size M)
    #
    # The original C code fuses the two so that each A[i][j] is loaded once
    # and used in both dot-products.

    # s[j] = (A^T * r)[j] = sum over rows i of r[i] * A[i, j]
    S_REDUCTION:
      for j in [0, M):
        s[j] = sum(i, r[i] * A[i, j])

    # q[i] = (A * p)[i] = sum over columns j of A[i, j] * p[j]
    Q_REDUCTION:
      for i in [0, N):
        q[i] = sum(j, A[i, j] * p[j])

dependencies:
    # S_REDUCTION and Q_REDUCTION:
    # - read A, r, p
    # - write disjoint outputs s and q
    # Therefore there are no flow or anti-dependencies between them,
    # and they may be executed in any order or fused into a single loop nest.

optimization:
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # 1. Fuse the two reductions over A
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # Fuse S_REDUCTION and Q_REDUCTION so that a single traversal of A
    # computes both s and q:
    #   for i:
    #     q[i] = sum_j A[i,j] * p[j]
    #     for all j in the same traversal:
    #       s[j] accumulates r[i] * A[i,j]
    #
    # This matches the original C kernel and roughly halves the memory
    # traffic to A compared to computing s and q in separate passes.
    fuse(S_REDUCTION, Q_REDUCTION)

    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # 2. Tile the (i, j) iteration space for cache locality
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # Block along the row (i) and column (j) dimensions of A in the
    # fused loop nest. TI is chosen so that:
    #   - a tile of q[i] and r[i] and the corresponding rows of A
    #     fit comfortably in L2/L3,
    # and TJ is chosen so that:
    #   - a tile of A[i, j] over j together with p[j] fits in L1/L2.
    #
    # Conceptually this yields:
    #   for I in tiles of i with size TI:
    #     for J in tiles of j with size TJ:
    #       for i in I:
    #         for j in J:
    #           use A[i,j], p[j], r[i]
    block(i, I, TI)
    block(j, J, TJ)

    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # 3. Parallelize over tiles of i with a reduction on s
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # Parallelize the outer tile loop I across up to T worker threads.
    # Each worker t accumulates its own private partial sums for s[j]
    # over the subset of rows i assigned to it:
    #
    #   s_private[t][j] += r[i] * A[i,j]   for i in tile subset of t
    #   q[i]            += A[i,j] * p[j]   for those i
    #
    # After all tiles have been processed, a final reduction over t
    # combines s_private[t][j] into the global s[j]:
    #
    #   s[j] = sum_t s_private[t][j]
    #
    # The number of threads actually used obeys:
    #   1 <= threads_used <= T <= min(MAX_THREADS, floor(N/2))
    # so that the extra storage for s_private (threads_used x M) never
    # exceeds 50% of the size of A (N x M).
    parallelize(I)

    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # 4. Exploit SIMD and ILP along j
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # Vectorize the innermost j-loop so that:
    #   - A[i, j:j+V-1] and p[j:j+V-1] are loaded in SIMD registers,
    #   - q[i] is kept in a scalar register and updated via FMA where
    #     available,
    #   - r[i] is hoisted out of the j-loop into a scalar register and
    #     multiplied with the SIMD A[i, j:j+V-1] to update s[j:j+V-1].
    #
    # Unrolling by U within the vectorized loop further increases ILP
    # and reduces loop overhead.
    vectorize(j, V)
    unroll(j, U)

#include <stdio.h>
#include <unistd.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <math.h>

/* Include polybench common header. */
#include <polybench.h>

/* Include benchmark-specific header. */
#include "bicg.h"


/* Array initialization. */
static
void init_array (int m, int n,
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(A,N,M,n,m),
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(r,N,n),
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(p,M,m))
{
  int i, j;

  for (i = 0; i < m; i++)
    p[i] = (DATA_TYPE)(i % m) / m;
  for (i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    r[i] = (DATA_TYPE)(i % n) / n;
    for (j = 0; j < m; j++)
      A[i][j] = (DATA_TYPE) (i*(j+1) % n)/n;
  }
}


/* DCE code. Must scan the entire live-out data.
   Can be used also to check the correctness of the output. */
static
void print_array(int m, int n,
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(s,M,m),
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(q,N,n))

{
  int i;

  POLYBENCH_DUMP_START;
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_BEGIN("s");
  for (i = 0; i < m; i++) {
    if (i % 20 == 0) fprintf (POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, "\n");
    fprintf (POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, DATA_PRINTF_MODIFIER, s[i]);
  }
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_END("s");
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_BEGIN("q");
  for (i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    if (i % 20 == 0) fprintf (POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, "\n");
    fprintf (POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, DATA_PRINTF_MODIFIER, q[i]);
  }
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_END("q");
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_FINISH;
}


/* Main computational kernel. The whole function will be timed,
   including the call and return. */
static
void kernel_bicg[[gnu::flatten, gnu::noinline]](int m, int n,
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(A,N,M,n,m),
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(s,M,m),
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(q,N,n),
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(p,M,m),
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(r,N,n))
{
  int i, j;

#pragma scop
  for (i = 0; i < _PB_M; i++)
    s[i] = 0;
  for (i = 0; i < _PB_N; i++)
    {
      q[i] = SCALAR_VAL(0.0);
      for (j = 0; j < _PB_M; j++)
	{
	  s[j] = s[j] + r[i] * A[i][j];
	  q[i] = q[i] + A[i][j] * p[j];
	}
    }
#pragma endscop

}


int main(int argc, char** argv)
{
  /* Retrieve problem size. */
  int n = N;
  int m = M;

  /* Variable declaration/allocation. */
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(A, DATA_TYPE, N, M, n, m);
  POLYBENCH_1D_ARRAY_DECL(s, DATA_TYPE, M, m);
  POLYBENCH_1D_ARRAY_DECL(q, DATA_TYPE, N, n);
  POLYBENCH_1D_ARRAY_DECL(p, DATA_TYPE, M, m);
  POLYBENCH_1D_ARRAY_DECL(r, DATA_TYPE, N, n);

  /* Initialize array(s). */
  init_array (m, n,
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A),
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(r),
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(p));

  /* Start timer. */
  polybench_start_instruments;

  /* Run kernel. */
  kernel_bicg (m, n,
	       POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A),
	       POLYBENCH_ARRAY(s),
	       POLYBENCH_ARRAY(q),
	       POLYBENCH_ARRAY(p),
	       POLYBENCH_ARRAY(r));

  /* Stop and print timer. */
  polybench_stop_instruments;
  polybench_print_instruments;

  /* Prevent dead-code elimination. All live-out data must be printed
     by the function call in argument. */
  polybench_prevent_dce(print_array(m, n, POLYBENCH_ARRAY(s), POLYBENCH_ARRAY(q)));

  /* Be clean. */
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(A);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(s);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(q);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(p);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(r);

  return 0;
}

    # can be parallelized with appropriate privatization and final combination.

    block(j, J, T_J)   # J indexes tiles of columns of width T_J

    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # Within the inner (i,j) loop:
    #   - r[i] and q[i] are invariant w.r.t. j and should be kept in registers.
    #   - A[i,j] is loaded once into a scalar a_ij and reused:
    #         a_ij = A[i,j]
    #         s[j] += a_ij * r[i]
    #         q[i] += a_ij * p[j]
    #
    # These are standard compiler optimizations; we document them here
    # to make the intended low-level structure explicit.

    # (No explicit directive; rely on scalar replacement and CSE in the backend.)
--- END OF MODEL: bicg-01 ---

--- START OF MODEL: bicg-02 ---
domain:
    # N: number of rows of A, length of r and q
    # M: number of columns of A, length of p and s
    i: dim in [0, N)        # row index of A, index for r and q
    j: dim in [0, M)        # column index of A, index for p and s

data:
    # Matrix A as in the C code: A[N][M], row-major.
    A[i, j]: in DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * M + j

    # Input vectors
    r[i]: in  DATA_TYPE = i    # length N
    p[j]: in  DATA_TYPE = j    # length M

    # Output vectors (completely overwritten by the kernel)
    s[j]: out DATA_TYPE = j    # length M
    q[i]: out DATA_TYPE = i    # length N

parameters:
    # Tunable blocking sizes (<= problem sizes, chosen w.r.t. cache)
    TI: int    # tile size for i (rows of A)
    TJ: int    # tile size for j (cols of A)

    # SIMD width in elements (e.g., 4 or 8 depending on DATA_TYPE and ISA)
    VW: int

    # Conceptual number of worker threads (<= 32 physical cores, or 64 HW threads)
    T:  int

computation:
    #-----------------------------------------
    # Phase 0: explicit zero-initialization
    #-----------------------------------------
    init_s:
        for j in [0, M):
            s[j] = 0

    init_q:
        for i in [0, N):
            q[i] = 0

    #-----------------------------------------
    # Phase 1: fused BiCG kernel
    #
    # Mathematically:
    #   s[j] = sum_i r[i] * A[i, j]   == (A^T * r)[j]
    #   q[i] = sum_j A[i, j] * p[j]   == (A * p)[i]
    #
    # We keep the operations fused in a single traversal of A so each
    # A[i, j] load feeds both updates (maximizing arithmetic per byte).
    #-----------------------------------------
    bicg:
        for i in [0, N):
            # Conceptually:
            #   ri = r[i]    # hoisted invariant for this i
            #   qi = q[i]    # scalar accumulator for this i
            for j in [0, M):
                update_s:
                    s[j] = s[j] + r[i] * A[i, j]
                update_q:
                    q[i] = q[i] + A[i, j] * p[j]
            # After the j-loop, qi would be written back to q[i]

dependencies:
    # s must be zero-initialized before any update in bicg
    for j in [0, M), i in [0, N):
        init_s(j) -> update_s(i, j)

    # q must be zero-initialized before any update in bicg
    for i in [0, N), j in [0, M):
        init_q(i) -> update_q(i, j)

    # s[j] is a reduction over i with operator '+':
    # for any fixed j, updates at different i are ordered by i.
    for j in [0, M), i1 in [0, N), i2 in [0, N):
        if i1 < i2:
            update_s(i1, j) -> update_s(i2, j)

    # q[i] is a reduction over j with operator '+':
    # for any fixed i, updates at different j are ordered by j.
    for i in [0, N), j1 in [0, M), j2 in [0, M):
        if j1 < j2:
            update_q(i, j1) -> update_q(i, j2)

optimization:
    #==============================================================
    # 1. Cache blocking / tiling
    #==============================================================
    # block(dim, tile_dim, tile_size):
    #   Split 'dim' into outer tile_dim and inner dim such that
    #   the loop over 'dim' is implemented as tiles of size tile_size.
    #
    # Resulting structure:
    #   for I in [0, ceil(N/TI)):
    #     for J in [0, ceil(M/TJ)):
    #       for i in tile I:
    #         for j in tile J:
    #           ...
    #
    # This improves locality for A, p, s, q and fits tiles into caches.
    block(i, I, TI)
    block(j, J, TJ)

    # Hoist tile loops I and J to the outermost level to form the 4-deep nest
    # I, J, i, j, matching the above structure.
    hoist(I)
    hoist(J)

    #==============================================================
    # 2. Parallelism
    #==============================================================
    # Custom directive:
    #   reduction(var, op, dim)
    #   - declares that all updates to 'var' along dimension 'dim'
    #     form an associative+commutative reduction with operator 'op'.
    #   - enables transformations (e.g., parallelization) that rely on
    #     privatization and later combination of partial results.
    reduction(s, +, i)

    # parallelize(dim):
    #   - run iterations of 'dim' concurrently.
    #   - here we parallelize over outer i-tiles (I), so each worker
    #     handles a subset of rows of A. Because s[j] is marked as
    #     a reduction over i, the implementation uses thread-local
    #     partial s-vectors and combines them at the end.
    parallelize(I)

    # Note: q[i] does not require a reduction annotation for this choice
    # of parallelism because each i (and hence each q[i]) is owned by
    # exactly one tile I and one worker.

    #==============================================================
    # 3. Vectorization and unrolling
    #==============================================================
    # The innermost j-loop has stride-1 access to A[i, j], p[j], and s[j].
    # Vectorizing j maps well to SIMD on x64 (AVX/AVX2/AVX-512).
    vectorize(j, VW)

    # Unroll the inner j-loop further to increase ILP and reduce branch
    # and loop-control overhead. The exact factor can be tuned.
    unroll(j, 4)

    #==============================================================
    # 4. Scalar replacement / invariant hoisting
    #==============================================================
    # Custom directive:
    #   hoist_invariant(expr, dim)
    #   - evaluate 'expr' once per iteration of the loop indexed by
    #     the outer dimension (here: i) and keep the result in a scalar
    #     register across the inner loop over 'dim'.
    #
    # r[i] is invariant across j; q[i] is naturally handled as a
    # scalar accumulator inside the j-loop.
    hoist_invariant(r[i], j)   # load r[i] once per i-iteration
    hoist_invariant(q[i], j)   # keep q[i] as a scalar accumulator

    # (Modern compilers will also typically common-subexpression A[i, j]
    #  so that its single load in each (i, j) iteration feeds both
    #  the s[j] and q[i] updates.)
--- END OF MODEL: bicg-02 ---

--- START OF MODEL: bicg-03 ---
# Optimized model for PolyBench/C BiCG kernel

domain:
    # Matrix A is N x M
    i: dim in [0, N)  # row index
    j: dim in [0, M)  # column index

data:
    # Row-major storage for A: A[i, j] is stored at base + (i * M + j)
    A[i, j]: in DATA_TYPE  = (i, j) -> i * M + j

    # 1D vectors, contiguous storage
    p[j]:     in  DATA_TYPE = (j) -> j        # length M
    r[i]:     in  DATA_TYPE = (i) -> i        # length N
    s[j]:   out  DATA_TYPE = (j) -> j        # length M, computes s = A^T * r
    q[i]:   out  DATA_TYPE = (i) -> i        # length N, computes q = A * p

parameters:
    # Problem sizes (match N, M from the C code)
    N: int
    M: int

    # Tuning parameters for cache blocking, vectorization and unrolling
    TI: int  # tile size for i (rows), e.g., chosen to fit a strip of rows in L2
    TJ: int  # tile size for j (cols), e.g., aligned to SIMD width and L1
    VEC: int # SIMD vector length in elements (e.g., 4 or 8 for doubles)
    U:   int # unroll factor for the innermost j-loop (e.g., 2–8)

computation:
    # 1. Initialize s to zero.
    INIT_S:
        for j in [0, M):
            s[j] = 0

    # 2. Initialize q to zero and perform the fused BiCG update.
    #
    #    This matches the original kernel:
    #      for (i = 0; i < N; ++i) {
    #        q[i] = 0;
    #        for (j = 0; j < M; ++j) {
    #          s[j] += r[i] * A[i][j];
    #          q[i] += A[i][j] * p[j];
    #        }
    #      }
    #
    MAIN:
        for i in [0, N):
            INIT_Q:
                q[i] = 0
            UPDATE_SQ:
                for j in [0, M):
                    s[j] = s[j] + r[i] * A[i, j]
                    q[i] = q[i] + A[i, j] * p[j]

dependencies:
    # s[j] is an addition reduction over the i-dimension
    for j in [0, M), i1 in [0, N), i2 in [i1 + 1, N):
        UPDATE_SQ(i1, j) -> UPDATE_SQ(i2, j)

    # q[i] is an addition reduction over the j-dimension
    for i in [0, N), j1 in [0, M), j2 in [j1 + 1, M):
        UPDATE_SQ(i, j1) -> UPDATE_SQ(i, j2)

    # Updates must see the zero-initialized values of s[j] and q[i]
    for j in [0, M), i in [0, N):
        INIT_S(j) -> UPDATE_SQ(i, j)
    for i in [0, N), j in [0, M):
        INIT_Q(i) -> UPDATE_SQ(i, j)

optimization:
    # -----------------------------
    # 1. Cache blocking over rows and columns of A
    # -----------------------------
    # Block the 2D (i, j) iteration space so that we operate on tiles
    # of A of size TI x TJ.  This improves spatial and temporal locality
    # of p[j] and s[j] (reused across many rows) and of A itself.
    block(i, I, TI)   # i = I * TI + i_inner
    block(j, J, TJ)   # j = J * TJ + j_inner

    # Hoist the tile loops to form a tiled nest of the form:
    #   for I in tiles of i:
    #     for J in tiles of j:
    #       for i in I-tile:
    #         for j in J-tile:
    #           ...
    hoist(I)
    hoist(J)

    # -----------------------------
    # 2. Parallelism
    # -----------------------------
    # Parallelize across row tiles I.
    # Each tile I works on a disjoint subset of rows of A and q[i].
    # s[j] is a reduction over i, so updates from different I-tiles
    # can be combined with a reduction (e.g., thread-private s[j]
    # partial sums per tile, then merged).  This keeps additional
    # memory bounded (O(M) per worker) and can be tuned so that the
    # overhead remains well below 50% of the size of A.
    parallelize(I)  # with reduction_add on s[j] over i

    # The simple initialization loops are also parallelizable:
    parallelize(INIT_S.j)
    parallelize(MAIN.i)  # for INIT_Q, if executed outside the tiled nest

    # -----------------------------
    # 3. Vectorization and unrolling
    # -----------------------------
    # Vectorize along the innermost column dimension within each J-tile.
    # This exploits the fact that A[i, j], p[j], and s[j] are contiguous
    # in memory when j varies fastest.
    #
    # After blocking, the innermost dimension is the inner j within a J-tile.
    vectorize(j, VEC)

    # Unroll the innermost j-loop to increase instruction-level parallelism
    # and help the compiler schedule FMA operations efficiently.
    unroll(j, U)

    # -----------------------------
    # 4. Scalar replacement (register tiling)
    # -----------------------------
    # Keep r[i] and q[i] in registers across the inner j-loop.  In C this
    # corresponds to:
    #   DATA_TYPE ri = r[i];
    #   DATA_TYPE qi = 0;
    #   for (j ...) { ... use ri, qi ... }
    #   q[i] = qi;
    #
    # This avoids repeated loads/stores of q[i] and r[i] in the j-loop.
    scalarize({r[i], q[i]}, j)
    # scalarize(VAR_SET, DIMENSION):
    #   Replace repeated memory accesses to the given loop-invariant scalars
    #   inside loops over DIMENSION by register-resident temporaries.
--- END OF MODEL: bicg-03 ---

--- START OF MODEL: bicg-04 ---
domain:
    i: dim in [0, N)          # row index of A, q, r
    j: dim in [0, M)          # column index of A, p, s

data:
    # Matrix A is stored row-major as in the C code: A[i][j]
    A[i, j]: in DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * M + j

    # Vectors over columns (length M)
    p[j]: in    DATA_TYPE = (j) -> j
    s[j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (j) -> j   # initialized inside the kernel, then written

    # Vectors over rows (length N)
    r[i]: in    DATA_TYPE = (i) -> i
    q[i]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i) -> i   # initialized inside the kernel, then written

parameters:
    # Problem sizes (compile-time in PolyBench, but modeled as parameters here)
    N: int
    M: int

    # Tuning parameters for performance (chosen per hardware)
    TILE_I: int    # tile size in i (rows), e.g., 64 or 128
    TILE_J: int    # tile size in j (cols), e.g., 256 or 512
    VEC_WIDTH: int # SIMD width used along j

computation:
    # Initialize s and q exactly as in the C code
    S_INIT:
        for j in [0, M):
            s[j] = 0

    Q_INIT:
        for i in [0, N):
            q[i] = 0

    # Fused BiCG kernel:
    #   s[j] = sum_i r[i] * A[i,j]       (s = A^T * r)
    #   q[i] = sum_j A[i,j] * p[j]       (q = A * p)
    # The loops are fused so that each A[i,j] load is reused for both sums.
    CORE:
        for i, j:
            s[j] = s[j] + r[i] * A[i, j]
            q[i] = q[i] + A[i, j] * p[j]

dependencies:
    # s and q must be initialized before they are used in CORE.
    for j in [0, M), i in [0, N):
        S_INIT(j) -> CORE(i, j)

    for i in [0, N), j in [0, M):
        Q_INIT(i) -> CORE(i, j)

optimization:
    #-------------------------------
    # 1. Expose reductions explicitly
    #-------------------------------
    # s[j] is mathematically a sum over i:
    #   s[j] = sum_{i=0..N-1} r[i] * A[i,j]
    # Declaring it as a reduction along i allows parallelization and reassociation.
    reduction(s[j], i)   # '+' reduction along i

    # q[i] is mathematically a sum over j:
    #   q[i] = sum_{j=0..M-1} A[i,j] * p[j]
    # This is a scalar reduction inside the i-iteration and will be kept in a register.
    reduction(q[i], j)   # '+' reduction along j

    #-------------------------------
    # 2. Cache blocking (tiling)
    #-------------------------------
    # Tile the 2D CORE loop so that:
    #   - inner tiles of j fit p[j] and s[j] segments into L1/L2 cache,
    #   - outer tiles of i give good work chunks for threads.
    #
    # Resulting structure (conceptually):
    #   for I in 0..N step TILE_I:
    #     for J in 0..M step TILE_J:
    #       for i in I..min(I+TILE_I, N):
    #         for j in J..min(J+TILE_J, M):
    #           ... CORE body ...
    block(i, I, TILE_I)   # I: outer tile index for rows
    block(j, J, TILE_J)   # J: outer tile index for columns
    hoist(I)              # move I to the outermost possible level
    hoist(J)              # keep J just inside I for rectangular tiles

    #-------------------------------
    # 3. Parallelization
    #-------------------------------
    # Parallelize across row tiles I:
    #   - Each thread processes a distinct block of rows.
    #   - q[i] writes are thread-local (no sharing of the same i).
    #   - s[j] updates across different I-tiles form a reduction along i, as declared above.
    #
    # Implementation note:
    #   The reduction(s[j], i) can be realized with one temporary s_private[thread][j]
    #   per worker, followed by a final accumulation into s[j]. This adds
    #   O(num_threads * M) extra storage, which is well below the 50% overhead
    #   bound relative to the dominant A[N][M] for typical PolyBench sizes.
    parallelize(I)

    #-------------------------------
    # 4. SIMD and unrolling on the innermost loop
    #-------------------------------
    # After tiling, the innermost loop is over j inside a fixed (i, I, J) context:
    #   for j in J..J+TILE_J:
    #       s[j] += r[i] * A[i,j]
    #       q[i] += A[i,j] * p[j]
    #
    # Accesses in j are unit-stride for A[i,j], p[j], and s[j], which is ideal for SIMD.
    vectorize(j, VEC_WIDTH)  # map j-iterations to vector lanes
    unroll(j, 4)             # unroll by 4 for additional ILP within each SIMD chunk

    #-------------------------------
    # 5. Scalar hoisting (implicit)
    #-------------------------------
    # (Modeled as a comment; typically performed automatically by compilers.)
    # - Hoist r[i] out of the inner j-loop and keep it in a register:
    #       ri = r[i];
    #       for j: s[j] += ri * A[i,j]; ...
    # - Keep q[i] as a scalar accumulator in a register across the inner j-loop,
    #   writing q[i] back to memory once per i (not per j).
    # These are standard loop-invariant code motion and scalar replacement
    # optimizations and do not require an explicit directive here.
--- END OF MODEL: bicg-04 ---

--- START OF MODEL: bicg-05 ---
domain:
    i: dim in [0, N)     # row index of A, q, r
    j: dim in [0, M)     # column index of A, s, p

data:
    # A is stored row-major as in the original C code: A[i][j] == A[i*M + j].
    A[i, j]: in DATA_TYPE   = (i, j) -> i * M + j

    # Input vectors.
    p[j]:    in DATA_TYPE   = (j)    -> j         # length M
    r[i]:    in DATA_TYPE   = (i)    -> i         # length N

    # Output vectors (fully overwritten by the kernel).
    s[j]: out DATA_TYPE     = (j)    -> j         # length M, s = A^T * r
    q[i]: out DATA_TYPE     = (i)    -> i         # length N, q = A * p

parameters:
    N:  int  # number of rows of A, length of q and r
    M:  int  # number of columns of A, length of s and p

    # Tunable tiling and SIMD parameters.
    TI: int  # tile size along i (rows), chosen for good L2/LLC locality
    TJ: int  # tile size along j (cols), chosen so A tile + p[j] fit in L1/L2
    V:  int  # SIMD vector length along j (e.g., 4 for AVX2 double, 8 for AVX2 float)
    U:  int  # unroll factor for j within a SIMD vector (e.g., 2–4)

    # Upper bound on the number of parallel partitions along i.
    # Implementation uses per-thread private partial sums for s[j] and
    # reduces them at the end. To keep the extra storage below 50% of
    # the size of A, we enforce:
    #   1 <= T <= min(MAX_THREADS, floor(N / 2))
    # so that a T x M temporary array of partial s never exceeds 0.5 * N*M.
    T:  int  # logical max number of threads/partitions along i

computation:
    # BiCG kernel computes two matrix-vector products:
    #   q = A * p        (size N)
    #   s = A^T * r      (size M)
    #
    # The original C code fuses the two so that each A[i][j] is loaded once
    # and used in both dot-products.

    # s[j] = (A^T * r)[j] = sum over rows i of r[i] * A[i, j]
    S_REDUCTION:
      for j in [0, M):
        s[j] = sum(i, r[i] * A[i, j])

    # q[i] = (A * p)[i] = sum over columns j of A[i, j] * p[j]
    Q_REDUCTION:
      for i in [0, N):
        q[i] = sum(j, A[i, j] * p[j])

dependencies:
    # S_REDUCTION and Q_REDUCTION:
    # - read A, r, p
    # - write disjoint outputs s and q
    # Therefore there are no flow or anti-dependencies between them,
    # and they may be executed in any order or fused into a single loop nest.

optimization:
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # 1. Fuse the two reductions over A
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # Fuse S_REDUCTION and Q_REDUCTION so that a single traversal of A
    # computes both s and q:
    #   for i:
    #     q[i] = sum_j A[i,j] * p[j]
    #     for all j in the same traversal:
    #       s[j] accumulates r[i] * A[i,j]
    #
    # This matches the original C kernel and roughly halves the memory
    # traffic to A compared to computing s and q in separate passes.
    fuse(S_REDUCTION, Q_REDUCTION)

    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # 2. Tile the (i, j) iteration space for cache locality
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # Block along the row (i) and column (j) dimensions of A in the
    # fused loop nest. TI is chosen so that:
    #   - a tile of q[i] and r[i] and the corresponding rows of A
    #     fit comfortably in L2/L3,
    # and TJ is chosen so that:
    #   - a tile of A[i, j] over j together with p[j] fits in L1/L2.
    #
    # Conceptually this yields:
    #   for I in tiles of i with size TI:
    #     for J in tiles of j with size TJ:
    #       for i in I:
    #         for j in J:
    #           use A[i,j], p[j], r[i]
    block(i, I, TI)
    block(j, J, TJ)

    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # 3. Parallelize over tiles of i with a reduction on s
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # Parallelize the outer tile loop I across up to T worker threads.
    # Each worker t accumulates its own private partial sums for s[j]
    # over the subset of rows i assigned to it:
    #
    #   s_private[t][j] += r[i] * A[i,j]   for i in tile subset of t
    #   q[i]            += A[i,j] * p[j]   for those i
    #
    # After all tiles have been processed, a final reduction over t
    # combines s_private[t][j] into the global s[j]:
    #
    #   s[j] = sum_t s_private[t][j]
    #
    # The number of threads actually used obeys:
    #   1 <= threads_used <= T <= min(MAX_THREADS, floor(N/2))
    # so that the extra storage for s_private (threads_used x M) never
    # exceeds 50% of the size of A (N x M).
    parallelize(I)

    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # 4. Exploit SIMD and ILP along j
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # Vectorize the innermost j-loop so that:
    #   - A[i, j:j+V-1] and p[j:j+V-1] are loaded in SIMD registers,
    #   - q[i] is kept in a scalar register and updated via FMA where
    #     available,
    #   - r[i] is hoisted out of the j-loop into a scalar register and
    #     multiplied with the SIMD A[i, j:j+V-1] to update s[j:j+V-1].
    #
    # Unrolling by U within the vectorized loop further increases ILP
    # and reduces loop overhead.
    vectorize(j, V)
    unroll(j, U)
--- END OF MODEL: bicg-05 ---

#include <stdio.h>

#include <string.h>
#include <math.h>

/* Include polybench common header. */
#include <polybench.h>

/* Include benchmark-specific header. */

/* Array initialization. */
static
void init_array (int m, int n,
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(A,N,M,n,m),
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(r,N,n),
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(p,M,m))
{
  int i, j;

  for (i = 0; i < m; i++)
    p[i] = (DATA_TYPE)(i % m) / m;
  for (i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    r[i] = (DATA_TYPE)(i % n) / n;
    for (j = 0; j < m; j++)
      A[i][j] = (DATA_TYPE) (i*(j+1) % n)/n;
  }
}


/* DCE code. Must scan the entire live-out data.
   Can be used also to check the correctness of the output. */
static
void print_array(int m, int n,
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(s,M,m),
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(q,N,n))

{
  int i;

  POLYBENCH_DUMP_START;
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_BEGIN("s");
  for (i = 0; i < m; i++) {
    if (i % 20 == 0) fprintf (POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, "\n");
    fprintf (POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, DATA_PRINTF_MODIFIER, s[i]);
  }
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_END("s");
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_BEGIN("q");
  for (i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    if (i % 20 == 0) fprintf (POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, "\n");
    fprintf (POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, DATA_PRINTF_MODIFIER, q[i]);
  }
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_END("q");
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_FINISH;
}


/* Main computational kernel. The whole function will be timed,
   including the call and return. */
static
void kernel_bicg[[gnu::flatten, gnu::noinline]](int m, int n,
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(A,N,M,n,m),
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(s,M,m),
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(q,N,n),
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(p,M,m),
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(r,N,n))
{
  int i, j;

#pragma scop
  for (i = 0; i < _PB_M; i++)
    s[i] = 0;
  for (i = 0; i < _PB_N; i++)
    {
      q[i] = SCALAR_VAL(0.0);
      for (j = 0; j < _PB_M; j++)
	{
	  s[j] = s[j] + r[i] * A[i][j];
	  q[i] = q[i] + A[i][j] * p[j];
	}
    }
#pragma endscop

}


int main(int argc, char** argv)
{
  /* Retrieve problem size. */
  int n = N;
  int m = M;

  /* Variable declaration/allocation. */
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(A, DATA_TYPE, N, M, n, m);
  POLYBENCH_1D_ARRAY_DECL(s, DATA_TYPE, M, m);
  POLYBENCH_1D_ARRAY_DECL(q, DATA_TYPE, N, n);
  POLYBENCH_1D_ARRAY_DECL(p, DATA_TYPE, M, m);
  POLYBENCH_1D_ARRAY_DECL(r, DATA_TYPE, N, n);

  /* Initialize array(s). */
  init_array (m, n,
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A),
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(r),
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(p));

  /* Start timer. */
  polybench_start_instruments;

  /* Run kernel. */
  kernel_bicg (m, n,
	       POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A),
	       POLYBENCH_ARRAY(s),
	       POLYBENCH_ARRAY(q),
	       POLYBENCH_ARRAY(p),
	       POLYBENCH_ARRAY(r));

  /* Stop and print timer. */
  polybench_stop_instruments;
  polybench_print_instruments;

  /* Prevent dead-code elimination. All live-out data must be printed
     by the function call in argument. */
  polybench_prevent_dce(print_array(m, n, POLYBENCH_ARRAY(s), POLYBENCH_ARRAY(q)));

  /* Be clean. */
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(A);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(s);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(q);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(p);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(r);

  return 0;
}

    j: dim in [0, M)     # column index of A, s, p

data:

    # Input vectors.
    p[j]:    in DATA_TYPE   = (j)    -> j         # length M
    r[i]:    in DATA_TYPE   = (i)    -> i         # length N

    s[j]: out DATA_TYPE     = (j)    -> j         # length M, s = A^T * r
    q[i]: out DATA_TYPE     = (i)    -> i         # length N, q = A * p

parameters:
    N:  int  # number of rows of A, length of q and r
    M:  int  # number of columns of A, length of s and p

    # Tunable tiling and SIMD parameters.
    TI: int  # tile size along i (rows), chosen for good L2/LLC locality
    TJ: int  # tile size along j (cols), chosen so A tile + p[j] fit in L1/L2
    V:  int  # SIMD vector length along j (e.g., 4 for AVX2 double, 8 for AVX2 float)
    U:  int  # unroll factor for j within a SIMD vector (e.g., 2–4)

    # Upper bound on the number of parallel partitions along i.
    # Implementation uses per-thread private partial sums for s[j] and
    # reduces them at the end. To keep the extra storage below 50% of
    # the size of A, we enforce:
    #   1 <= T <= min(MAX_THREADS, floor(N / 2))
    # so that a T x M temporary array of partial s never exceeds 0.5 * N*M.
    T:  int  # logical max number of threads/partitions along i

computation:
    # BiCG kernel computes two matrix-vector products:
    #   q = A * p        (size N)
    #   s = A^T * r      (size M)
    #
    # The original C code fuses the two so that each A[i][j] is loaded once
    # and used in both dot-products.

    # s[j] = (A^T * r)[j] = sum over rows i of r[i] * A[i, j]
    S_REDUCTION:
      for j in [0, M):
        s[j] = sum(i, r[i] * A[i, j])

    # q[i] = (A * p)[i] = sum over columns j of A[i, j] * p[j]
    Q_REDUCTION:
      for i in [0, N):
        q[i] = sum(j, A[i, j] * p[j])

dependencies:
    # S_REDUCTION and Q_REDUCTION:
    # - read A, r, p
    # - write disjoint outputs s and q
    # Therefore there are no flow or anti-dependencies between them,
    # and they may be executed in any order or fused into a single loop nest.

optimization:
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # 1. Fuse the two reductions over A
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # Fuse S_REDUCTION and Q_REDUCTION so that a single traversal of A
    # computes both s and q:
    #   for i:
    #     q[i] = sum_j A[i,j] * p[j]
    #     for all j in the same traversal:
    #       s[j] accumulates r[i] * A[i,j]
    #
    # This matches the original C kernel and roughly halves the memory
    # traffic to A compared to computing s and q in separate passes.
    fuse(S_REDUCTION, Q_REDUCTION)

    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # 2. Tile the (i, j) iteration space for cache locality
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # Block along the row (i) and column (j) dimensions of A in the
    # fused loop nest. TI is chosen so that:
    #   - a tile of q[i] and r[i] and the corresponding rows of A
    #     fit comfortably in L2/L3,
    # and TJ is chosen so that:
    #   - a tile of A[i, j] over j together with p[j] fits in L1/L2.
    #
    # Conceptually this yields:
    #   for I in tiles of i with size TI:
    #     for J in tiles of j with size TJ:
    #       for i in I:
    #         for j in J:
    #           use A[i,j], p[j], r[i]
    block(i, I, TI)
    block(j, J, TJ)

    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # 3. Parallelize over tiles of i with a reduction on s
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # Parallelize the outer tile loop I across up to T worker threads.
    # Each worker t accumulates its own private partial sums for s[j]
    # over the subset of rows i assigned to it:
    #
    #   s_private[t][j] += r[i] * A[i,j]   for i in tile subset of t
    #   q[i]            += A[i,j] * p[j]   for those i
    #
    # After all tiles have been processed, a final reduction over t
    # combines s_private[t][j] into the global s[j]:
    #
    #   s[j] = sum_t s_private[t][j]
    #
    # The number of threads actually used obeys:
    #   1 <= threads_used <= T <= min(MAX_THREADS, floor(N/2))
    # so that the extra storage for s_private (threads_used x M) never
    # exceeds 50% of the size of A (N x M).
    parallelize(I)

    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # 4. Exploit SIMD and ILP along j
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # Vectorize the innermost j-loop so that:
    #   - A[i, j:j+V-1] and p[j:j+V-1] are loaded in SIMD registers,
    #   - q[i] is kept in a scalar register and updated via FMA where
    #     available,
    #   - r[i] is hoisted out of the j-loop into a scalar register and
    #     multiplied with the SIMD A[i, j:j+V-1] to update s[j:j+V-1].
    #
    # Unrolling by U within the vectorized loop further increases ILP
    # and reduces loop overhead.
    vectorize(j, V)
    unroll(j, U)

#include <stdio.h>
#include <unistd.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <math.h>

/* Include polybench common header. */
#include <polybench.h>

/* Include benchmark-specific header. */
#include "bicg.h"


/* Array initialization. */
static
void init_array (int m, int n,
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(A,N,M,n,m),
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(r,N,n),
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(p,M,m))
{
  int i, j;

  for (i = 0; i < m; i++)
    p[i] = (DATA_TYPE)(i % m) / m;
  for (i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    r[i] = (DATA_TYPE)(i % n) / n;
    for (j = 0; j < m; j++)
      A[i][j] = (DATA_TYPE) (i*(j+1) % n)/n;
  }
}


/* DCE code. Must scan the entire live-out data.
   Can be used also to check the correctness of the output. */
static
void print_array(int m, int n,
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(s,M,m),
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(q,N,n))

{
  int i;

  POLYBENCH_DUMP_START;
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_BEGIN("s");
  for (i = 0; i < m; i++) {
    if (i % 20 == 0) fprintf (POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, "\n");
    fprintf (POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, DATA_PRINTF_MODIFIER, s[i]);
  }
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_END("s");
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_BEGIN("q");
  for (i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    if (i % 20 == 0) fprintf (POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, "\n");
    fprintf (POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, DATA_PRINTF_MODIFIER, q[i]);
  }
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_END("q");
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_FINISH;
}


/* Main computational kernel. The whole function will be timed,
   including the call and return. */
static
void kernel_bicg[[gnu::flatten, gnu::noinline]](int m, int n,
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(A,N,M,n,m),
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(s,M,m),
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(q,N,n),
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(p,M,m),
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(r,N,n))
{
  int i, j;

#pragma scop
  for (i = 0; i < _PB_M; i++)
    s[i] = 0;
  for (i = 0; i < _PB_N; i++)
    {
      q[i] = SCALAR_VAL(0.0);
      for (j = 0; j < _PB_M; j++)
	{
	  s[j] = s[j] + r[i] * A[i][j];
	  q[i] = q[i] + A[i][j] * p[j];
	}
    }
#pragma endscop

}


int main(int argc, char** argv)
{
  /* Retrieve problem size. */
  int n = N;
  int m = M;

  /* Variable declaration/allocation. */
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(A, DATA_TYPE, N, M, n, m);
  POLYBENCH_1D_ARRAY_DECL(s, DATA_TYPE, M, m);
  POLYBENCH_1D_ARRAY_DECL(q, DATA_TYPE, N, n);
  POLYBENCH_1D_ARRAY_DECL(p, DATA_TYPE, M, m);
  POLYBENCH_1D_ARRAY_DECL(r, DATA_TYPE, N, n);

  /* Initialize array(s). */
  init_array (m, n,
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A),
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(r),
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(p));

  /* Start timer. */
  polybench_start_instruments;

  /* Run kernel. */
  kernel_bicg (m, n,
	       POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A),
	       POLYBENCH_ARRAY(s),
	       POLYBENCH_ARRAY(q),
	       POLYBENCH_ARRAY(p),
	       POLYBENCH_ARRAY(r));

  /* Stop and print timer. */
  polybench_stop_instruments;
  polybench_print_instruments;

  /* Prevent dead-code elimination. All live-out data must be printed
     by the function call in argument. */
  polybench_prevent_dce(print_array(m, n, POLYBENCH_ARRAY(s), POLYBENCH_ARRAY(q)));

  /* Be clean. */
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(A);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(s);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(q);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(p);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(r);

  return 0;
}
