    r[i]:     in  DATA_TYPE = (i) -> i        # length N
    s[j]:   out  DATA_TYPE = (j) -> j        # length M, computes s = A^T * r
    q[i]:   out  DATA_TYPE = (i) -> i        # length N, computes q = A * p

parameters:
    # Problem sizes (match N, M from the C code)
    N: int
    M: int

    # Tuning parameters for cache blocking, vectorization and unrolling
    TI: int  # tile size for i (rows), e.g., chosen to fit a strip of rows in L2
    TJ: int  # tile size for j (cols), e.g., aligned to SIMD width and L1
    VEC: int # SIMD vector length in elements (e.g., 4 or 8 for doubles)
    U:   int # unroll factor for the innermost j-loop (e.g., 2–8)

computation:
    # 1. Initialize s to zero.
    INIT_S:
        for j in [0, M):
            s[j] = 0

    # 2. Initialize q to zero and perform the fused BiCG update.
    #
    #    This matches the original kernel:
    #      for (i = 0; i < N; ++i) {
    #        q[i] = 0;
    #        for (j = 0; j < M; ++j) {
    #          s[j] += r[i] * A[i][j];
    #          q[i] += A[i][j] * p[j];
    #        }
    #      }
    #
    MAIN:
        for i in [0, N):
            INIT_Q:
                q[i] = 0
            UPDATE_SQ:
                for j in [0, M):
                    s[j] = s[j] + r[i] * A[i, j]
                    q[i] = q[i] + A[i, j] * p[j]

dependencies:
    # s[j] is an addition reduction over the i-dimension
    for j in [0, M), i1 in [0, N), i2 in [i1 + 1, N):
        UPDATE_SQ(i1, j) -> UPDATE_SQ(i2, j)

    # q[i] is an addition reduction over the j-dimension
    for i in [0, N), j1 in [0, M), j2 in [j1 + 1, M):
        UPDATE_SQ(i, j1) -> UPDATE_SQ(i, j2)

    # Updates must see the zero-initialized values of s[j] and q[i]
    for j in [0, M), i in [0, N):
        INIT_S(j) -> UPDATE_SQ(i, j)
    for i in [0, N), j in [0, M):
        INIT_Q(i) -> UPDATE_SQ(i, j)

optimization:
    # -----------------------------
    # 1. Cache blocking over rows and columns of A
    # -----------------------------
    # Block the 2D (i, j) iteration space so that we operate on tiles
    # of A of size TI x TJ.  This improves spatial and temporal locality
    # of p[j] and s[j] (reused across many rows) and of A itself.
    block(i, I, TI)   # i = I * TI + i_inner
    block(j, J, TJ)   # j = J * TJ + j_inner

    # Hoist the tile loops to form a tiled nest of the form:
    #   for I in tiles of i:
    #     for J in tiles of j:
    #       for i in I-tile:
    #         for j in J-tile:
    #           ...
    hoist(I)
    hoist(J)

    # -----------------------------
    # 2. Parallelism
    # -----------------------------
    # Parallelize across row tiles I.
    # Each tile I works on a disjoint subset of rows of A and q[i].
    # s[j] is a reduction over i, so updates from different I-tiles
    # can be combined with a reduction (e.g., thread-private s[j]
    # partial sums per tile, then merged).  This keeps additional
    # memory bounded (O(M) per worker) and can be tuned so that the
    # overhead remains well below 50% of the size of A.
    parallelize(I)  # with reduction_add on s[j] over i

    # The simple initialization loops are also parallelizable:
    parallelize(INIT_S.j)
    parallelize(MAIN.i)  # for INIT_Q, if executed outside the tiled nest

    # -----------------------------
    # 3. Vectorization and unrolling
    # -----------------------------
    # Vectorize along the innermost column dimension within each J-tile.
    # This exploits the fact that A[i, j], p[j], and s[j] are contiguous
    # in memory when j varies fastest.
    #
    # After blocking, the innermost dimension is the inner j within a J-tile.
    vectorize(j, VEC)

    # Unroll the innermost j-loop to increase instruction-level parallelism
    # and help the compiler schedule FMA operations efficiently.
    unroll(j, U)

    # -----------------------------
    # 4. Scalar replacement (register tiling)
    # -----------------------------
    # Keep r[i] and q[i] in registers across the inner j-loop.  In C this
    # corresponds to:
    #   DATA_TYPE ri = r[i];
    #   DATA_TYPE qi = 0;
    #   for (j ...) { ... use ri, qi ... }
    #   q[i] = qi;
    #
    # This avoids repeated loads/stores of q[i] and r[i] in the j-loop.
    scalarize({r[i], q[i]}, j)
    # scalarize(VAR_SET, DIMENSION):
    #   Replace repeated memory accesses to the given loop-invariant scalars
    #   inside loops over DIMENSION by register-resident temporaries.
--- END OF MODEL: bicg-03 ---

domain:
    i: dim in [0, N)          # row index of A, q, r
    j: dim in [0, M)          # column index of A, p, s

data:
    # Matrix A is stored row-major as in the C code: A[i][j]
    A[i, j]: in DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * M + j

    # Vectors over columns (length M)
    p[j]: in    DATA_TYPE = (j) -> j
    s[j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (j) -> j   # initialized inside the kernel, then written

    # Vectors over rows (length N)
    r[i]: in    DATA_TYPE = (i) -> i
    q[i]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i) -> i   # initialized inside the kernel, then written

parameters:
    # Problem sizes (compile-time in PolyBench, but modeled as parameters here)
    N: int
    M: int

    # Tuning parameters for performance (chosen per hardware)
    TILE_I: int    # tile size in i (rows), e.g., 64 or 128
    TILE_J: int    # tile size in j (cols), e.g., 256 or 512
    VEC_WIDTH: int # SIMD width used along j

computation:
    # Initialize s and q exactly as in the C code
    S_INIT:
        for j in [0, M):
            s[j] = 0

    Q_INIT:
        for i in [0, N):
            q[i] = 0

    # Fused BiCG kernel:
    #   s[j] = sum_i r[i] * A[i,j]       (s = A^T * r)
    #   q[i] = sum_j A[i,j] * p[j]       (q = A * p)
    # The loops are fused so that each A[i,j] load is reused for both sums.
    CORE:
        for i, j:
            s[j] = s[j] + r[i] * A[i, j]
            q[i] = q[i] + A[i, j] * p[j]

dependencies:
    # s and q must be initialized before they are used in CORE.
    for j in [0, M), i in [0, N):
        S_INIT(j) -> CORE(i, j)

    for i in [0, N), j in [0, M):
        Q_INIT(i) -> CORE(i, j)

optimization:
    #-------------------------------
    # 1. Expose reductions explicitly
    #-------------------------------
    # s[j] is mathematically a sum over i:
    #   s[j] = sum_{i=0..N-1} r[i] * A[i,j]
    # Declaring it as a reduction along i allows parallelization and reassociation.
    reduction(s[j], i)   # '+' reduction along i

    # q[i] is mathematically a sum over j:
    #   q[i] = sum_{j=0..M-1} A[i,j] * p[j]
    # This is a scalar reduction inside the i-iteration and will be kept in a register.
    reduction(q[i], j)   # '+' reduction along j

    #-------------------------------
    # 2. Cache blocking (tiling)
    #-------------------------------
    # Tile the 2D CORE loop so that:
    #   - inner tiles of j fit p[j] and s[j] segments into L1/L2 cache,
    #   - outer tiles of i give good work chunks for threads.
    #
    # Resulting structure (conceptually):
    #   for I in 0..N step TILE_I:
    #     for J in 0..M step TILE_J:
    #       for i in I..min(I+TILE_I, N):
    #         for j in J..min(J+TILE_J, M):
    #           ... CORE body ...
    block(i, I, TILE_I)   # I: outer tile index for rows
    block(j, J, TILE_J)   # J: outer tile index for columns
    hoist(I)              # move I to the outermost possible level
    hoist(J)              # keep J just inside I for rectangular tiles

    #-------------------------------
    # 3. Parallelization
    #-------------------------------
    # Parallelize across row tiles I:
    #   - Each thread processes a distinct block of rows.
    #   - q[i] writes are thread-local (no sharing of the same i).
    #   - s[j] updates across different I-tiles form a reduction along i, as declared above.
    #
    # Implementation note:
    #   The reduction(s[j], i) can be realized with one temporary s_private[thread][j]
    #   per worker, followed by a final accumulation into s[j]. This adds
    #   O(num_threads * M) extra storage, which is well below the 50% overhead
    #   bound relative to the dominant A[N][M] for typical PolyBench sizes.
    parallelize(I)

    #-------------------------------
    # 4. SIMD and unrolling on the innermost loop
    #-------------------------------
    # After tiling, the innermost loop is over j inside a fixed (i, I, J) context:
    #   for j in J..J+TILE_J:
    #       s[j] += r[i] * A[i,j]
    #       q[i] += A[i,j] * p[j]
    #
    # Accesses in j are unit-stride for A[i,j], p[j], and s[j], which is ideal for SIMD.
    vectorize(j, VEC_WIDTH)  # map j-iterations to vector lanes
    unroll(j, 4)             # unroll by 4 for additional ILP within each SIMD chunk

    #-------------------------------
    # 5. Scalar hoisting (implicit)
    #-------------------------------
    # (Modeled as a comment; typically performed automatically by compilers.)
    # - Hoist r[i] out of the inner j-loop and keep it in a register:
    #       ri = r[i];
    #       for j: s[j] += ri * A[i,j]; ...
    # - Keep q[i] as a scalar accumulator in a register across the inner j-loop,
    #   writing q[i] back to memory once per i (not per j).
    # These are standard loop-invariant code motion and scalar replacement
    # optimizations and do not require an explicit directive here.

domain:
    i: dim in [0, N)     # row index of A, q, r
    j: dim in [0, M)     # column index of A, s, p

data:
    # A is stored row-major as in the original C code: A[i][j] == A[i*M + j].
    A[i, j]: in DATA_TYPE   = (i, j) -> i * M + j

    # Input vectors.
    p[j]:    in DATA_TYPE   = (j)    -> j         # length M
    r[i]:    in DATA_TYPE   = (i)    -> i         # length N

    # Output vectors (fully overwritten by the kernel).
    s[j]: out DATA_TYPE     = (j)    -> j         # length M, s = A^T * r
    q[i]: out DATA_TYPE     = (i)    -> i         # length N, q = A * p

parameters:
    N:  int  # number of rows of A, length of q and r
    M:  int  # number of columns of A, length of s and p

    # Tunable tiling and SIMD parameters.
    TI: int  # tile size along i (rows), chosen for good L2/LLC locality
    TJ: int  # tile size along j (cols), chosen so A tile + p[j] fit in L1/L2
    V:  int  # SIMD vector length along j (e.g., 4 for AVX2 double, 8 for AVX2 float)
    U:  int  # unroll factor for j within a SIMD vector (e.g., 2–4)

    # Upper bound on the number of parallel partitions along i.
    # Implementation uses per-thread private partial sums for s[j] and
    # reduces them at the end. To keep the extra storage below 50% of
    # the size of A, we enforce:
    #   1 <= T <= min(MAX_THREADS, floor(N / 2))
    # so that a T x M temporary array of partial s never exceeds 0.5 * N*M.
    T:  int  # logical max number of threads/partitions along i

computation:
    # BiCG kernel computes two matrix-vector products:
    #   q = A * p        (size N)
    #   s = A^T * r      (size M)
    #
    # The original C code fuses the two so that each A[i][j] is loaded once
    # and used in both dot-products.

    # s[j] = (A^T * r)[j] = sum over rows i of r[i] * A[i, j]
    S_REDUCTION:
      for j in [0, M):
        s[j] = sum(i, r[i] * A[i, j])

    # q[i] = (A * p)[i] = sum over columns j of A[i, j] * p[j]
    Q_REDUCTION:
      for i in [0, N):
        q[i] = sum(j, A[i, j] * p[j])

dependencies:
    # S_REDUCTION and Q_REDUCTION:
    # - read A, r, p
    # - write disjoint outputs s and q
    # Therefore there are no flow or anti-dependencies between them,
    # and they may be executed in any order or fused into a single loop nest.

optimization:
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # 1. Fuse the two reductions over A
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # Fuse S_REDUCTION and Q_REDUCTION so that a single traversal of A
    # computes both s and q:
    #   for i:
    #     q[i] = sum_j A[i,j] * p[j]
    #     for all j in the same traversal:
    #       s[j] accumulates r[i] * A[i,j]
    #
    # This matches the original C kernel and roughly halves the memory
    # traffic to A compared to computing s and q in separate passes.
    fuse(S_REDUCTION, Q_REDUCTION)

    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # 2. Tile the (i, j) iteration space for cache locality
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # Block along the row (i) and column (j) dimensions of A in the
    # fused loop nest. TI is chosen so that:
    #   - a tile of q[i] and r[i] and the corresponding rows of A
    #     fit comfortably in L2/L3,
    # and TJ is chosen so that:
    #   - a tile of A[i, j] over j together with p[j] fits in L1/L2.
    #
    # Conceptually this yields:
    #   for I in tiles of i with size TI:
    #     for J in tiles of j with size TJ:
    #       for i in I:
    #         for j in J:
    #           use A[i,j], p[j], r[i]
    block(i, I, TI)
    block(j, J, TJ)

    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # 3. Parallelize over tiles of i with a reduction on s
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # Parallelize the outer tile loop I across up to T worker threads.
    # Each worker t accumulates its own private partial sums for s[j]
    # over the subset of rows i assigned to it:
    #
    #   s_private[t][j] += r[i] * A[i,j]   for i in tile subset of t
    #   q[i]            += A[i,j] * p[j]   for those i
    #
    # After all tiles have been processed, a final reduction over t
    # combines s_private[t][j] into the global s[j]:
    #
    #   s[j] = sum_t s_private[t][j]
    #
    # The number of threads actually used obeys:
    #   1 <= threads_used <= T <= min(MAX_THREADS, floor(N/2))
    # so that the extra storage for s_private (threads_used x M) never
    # exceeds 50% of the size of A (N x M).
    parallelize(I)

    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # 4. Exploit SIMD and ILP along j
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # Vectorize the innermost j-loop so that:
    #   - A[i, j:j+V-1] and p[j:j+V-1] are loaded in SIMD registers,
    #   - q[i] is kept in a scalar register and updated via FMA where
    #     available,
    #   - r[i] is hoisted out of the j-loop into a scalar register and
    #     multiplied with the SIMD A[i, j:j+V-1] to update s[j:j+V-1].
    #
    # Unrolling by U within the vectorized loop further increases ILP
    # and reduces loop overhead.
    vectorize(j, V)
    unroll(j, U)

#include <stdio.h>
#include <unistd.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <math.h>

/* Include polybench common header. */
#include <polybench.h>

/* Include benchmark-specific header. */
#include "bicg.h"


/* Array initialization. */
static
void init_array (int m, int n,
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(A,N,M,n,m),
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(r,N,n),
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(p,M,m))
{
  int i, j;

  for (i = 0; i < m; i++)
    p[i] = (DATA_TYPE)(i % m) / m;
  for (i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    r[i] = (DATA_TYPE)(i % n) / n;
    for (j = 0; j < m; j++)
      A[i][j] = (DATA_TYPE) (i*(j+1) % n)/n;
  }
}


/* DCE code. Must scan the entire live-out data.
   Can be used also to check the correctness of the output. */
static
void print_array(int m, int n,
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(s,M,m),
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(q,N,n))

{
  int i;

  POLYBENCH_DUMP_START;
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_BEGIN("s");
  for (i = 0; i < m; i++) {
    if (i % 20 == 0) fprintf (POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, "\n");
    fprintf (POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, DATA_PRINTF_MODIFIER, s[i]);
  }
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_END("s");
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_BEGIN("q");
  for (i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    if (i % 20 == 0) fprintf (POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, "\n");
    fprintf (POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, DATA_PRINTF_MODIFIER, q[i]);
  }
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_END("q");
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_FINISH;
}


/* Main computational kernel. The whole function will be timed,
   including the call and return. */
static
void kernel_bicg[[gnu::flatten, gnu::noinline]](int m, int n,
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(A,N,M,n,m),
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(s,M,m),
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(q,N,n),
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(p,M,m),
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(r,N,n))
{
  int i, j;

#pragma scop
  for (i = 0; i < _PB_M; i++)
    s[i] = 0;
  for (i = 0; i < _PB_N; i++)
    {
      q[i] = SCALAR_VAL(0.0);
      for (j = 0; j < _PB_M; j++)
	{
	  s[j] = s[j] + r[i] * A[i][j];
	  q[i] = q[i] + A[i][j] * p[j];
	}
    }
#pragma endscop

}


int main(int argc, char** argv)
{
  /* Retrieve problem size. */
  int n = N;
  int m = M;

  /* Variable declaration/allocation. */
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(A, DATA_TYPE, N, M, n, m);
  POLYBENCH_1D_ARRAY_DECL(s, DATA_TYPE, M, m);
  POLYBENCH_1D_ARRAY_DECL(q, DATA_TYPE, N, n);
  POLYBENCH_1D_ARRAY_DECL(p, DATA_TYPE, M, m);
  POLYBENCH_1D_ARRAY_DECL(r, DATA_TYPE, N, n);

  /* Initialize array(s). */
  init_array (m, n,
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A),
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(r),
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(p));

  /* Start timer. */
  polybench_start_instruments;

  /* Run kernel. */
  kernel_bicg (m, n,
	       POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A),
	       POLYBENCH_ARRAY(s),
	       POLYBENCH_ARRAY(q),
	       POLYBENCH_ARRAY(p),
	       POLYBENCH_ARRAY(r));

  /* Stop and print timer. */
  polybench_stop_instruments;
  polybench_print_instruments;

  /* Prevent dead-code elimination. All live-out data must be printed
     by the function call in argument. */
  polybench_prevent_dce(print_array(m, n, POLYBENCH_ARRAY(s), POLYBENCH_ARRAY(q)));

  /* Be clean. */
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(A);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(s);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(q);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(p);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(r);

  return 0;
}

    # q[i] is a reduction over j:
    #   q[i] = Σ_j A[i,j] * p[j]

    # can be parallelized with appropriate privatization and final combination.

    for j in [0, M), i1 in [0, N), i2 in [0, N), i1 < i2:

    block(j, J, T_J)   # J indexes tiles of columns of width T_J

    # 3. Parallelization across tiles in the row dimension.
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # Each tile in I is independent for q[i] (rows of A), while s[j]
    # is a reduction over i. We parallelize over I and implement s[j]
    # as a reduction variable across tiles.
    #
    # A typical implementation:
    #   - Each worker gets a private buffer s_private[j] for its I-tiles.
    #   - After all tiles, s[j] = sum_over_I s_private_I[j].
    #
    # This preserves correctness and uses O(#threads * M) extra memory,
    # which is typically far below 50% of the A matrix footprint.

    parallelize(I)  # parallel row tiles with reduction on s[j] over I

    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # 4. Loop ordering within tiles for locality.
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # Inside each (I,J) tile, placing i outside j:
    #   for i in tile I:
    #     q[i] reduction over j in tile J
    #     r[i] reused across inner j
    #     A[i,j], p[j], s[j] streamed contiguously in j.
    #
    # This matches the original code’s access pattern and is friendly
    # to hardware prefetchers.

    interchange(i, j)  # ensure order: i outer, j inner within each tile

    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # 5. SIMD vectorization and unrolling along the contiguous j-dimension.
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # The j-dimension indexes contiguous elements:
    #   A[i, j]  -> i*M + j
    #   p[j], s[j] -> j
    #
    # Vectorizing and unrolling j exploits wide SIMD registers and
    # hides instruction latency while maintaining unit-stride access.

    vectorize(j, VEC_J)  # map j-iterations to SIMD lanes
    unroll(j, U_J)       # unroll j-loop within each SIMD chunk

    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # 6. Scalar hoisting and common subexpression elimination (CSE).
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # Within the inner (i,j) loop:
    #   - r[i] and q[i] are invariant w.r.t. j and should be kept in registers.
    #   - A[i,j] is loaded once into a scalar a_ij and reused:
    #         a_ij = A[i,j]
    #         s[j] += a_ij * r[i]
    #         q[i] += a_ij * p[j]
    #
    # These are standard compiler optimizations; we document them here
    # to make the intended low-level structure explicit.

    # (No explicit directive; rely on scalar replacement and CSE in the backend.)
--- END OF MODEL: bicg-01 ---

--- START OF MODEL: bicg-02 ---
domain:
    # N: number of rows of A, length of r and q
    # M: number of columns of A, length of p and s
    i: dim in [0, N)        # row index of A, index for r and q
    j: dim in [0, M)        # column index of A, index for p and s

data:
    # Matrix A as in the C code: A[N][M], row-major.
    A[i, j]: in DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * M + j

    # Input vectors
    r[i]: in  DATA_TYPE = i    # length N
    p[j]: in  DATA_TYPE = j    # length M

    # Output vectors (completely overwritten by the kernel)
    s[j]: out DATA_TYPE = j    # length M
    q[i]: out DATA_TYPE = i    # length N

parameters:
    # Tunable blocking sizes (<= problem sizes, chosen w.r.t. cache)
    TI: int    # tile size for i (rows of A)
    TJ: int    # tile size for j (cols of A)

    # SIMD width in elements (e.g., 4 or 8 depending on DATA_TYPE and ISA)
    VW: int

    # Conceptual number of worker threads (<= 32 physical cores, or 64 HW threads)
    T:  int

computation:
    #-----------------------------------------
    # Phase 0: explicit zero-initialization
    #-----------------------------------------
    init_s:
        for j in [0, M):
            s[j] = 0

    init_q:
        for i in [0, N):
            q[i] = 0

    #-----------------------------------------
    # Phase 1: fused BiCG kernel
    #
    # Mathematically:
    #   s[j] = sum_i r[i] * A[i, j]   == (A^T * r)[j]
    #   q[i] = sum_j A[i, j] * p[j]   == (A * p)[i]
    #
    # We keep the operations fused in a single traversal of A so each
    # A[i, j] load feeds both updates (maximizing arithmetic per byte).
    #-----------------------------------------
    bicg:
        for i in [0, N):
            # Conceptually:
            #   ri = r[i]    # hoisted invariant for this i
            #   qi = q[i]    # scalar accumulator for this i
            for j in [0, M):
                update_s:
                    s[j] = s[j] + r[i] * A[i, j]
                update_q:
                    q[i] = q[i] + A[i, j] * p[j]
            # After the j-loop, qi would be written back to q[i]

dependencies:
    # s must be zero-initialized before any update in bicg
    for j in [0, M), i in [0, N):
        init_s(j) -> update_s(i, j)

    # q must be zero-initialized before any update in bicg
    for i in [0, N), j in [0, M):
        init_q(i) -> update_q(i, j)

    # s[j] is a reduction over i with operator '+':
    # for any fixed j, updates at different i are ordered by i.
    for j in [0, M), i1 in [0, N), i2 in [0, N):
        if i1 < i2:
            update_s(i1, j) -> update_s(i2, j)

    # q[i] is a reduction over j with operator '+':
    # for any fixed i, updates at different j are ordered by j.
    for i in [0, N), j1 in [0, M), j2 in [0, M):
        if j1 < j2:
            update_q(i, j1) -> update_q(i, j2)

optimization:
    #==============================================================
    # 1. Cache blocking / tiling
    #==============================================================
    # block(dim, tile_dim, tile_size):
    #   Split 'dim' into outer tile_dim and inner dim such that
    #   the loop over 'dim' is implemented as tiles of size tile_size.
    #
    # Resulting structure:
    #   for I in [0, ceil(N/TI)):
    #     for J in [0, ceil(M/TJ)):
    #       for i in tile I:
    #         for j in tile J:
    #           ...
    #
    # This improves locality for A, p, s, q and fits tiles into caches.
    block(i, I, TI)
    block(j, J, TJ)

    # Hoist tile loops I and J to the outermost level to form the 4-deep nest
    # I, J, i, j, matching the above structure.
    hoist(I)
    hoist(J)

    #==============================================================
    # 2. Parallelism
    #==============================================================
    # Custom directive:
    #   reduction(var, op, dim)
    #   - declares that all updates to 'var' along dimension 'dim'
    #     form an associative+commutative reduction with operator 'op'.
    #   - enables transformations (e.g., parallelization) that rely on
    #     privatization and later combination of partial results.
    reduction(s, +, i)

    # parallelize(dim):
    #   - run iterations of 'dim' concurrently.
    #   - here we parallelize over outer i-tiles (I), so each worker
    #     handles a subset of rows of A. Because s[j] is marked as
    #     a reduction over i, the implementation uses thread-local
    #     partial s-vectors and combines them at the end.
    parallelize(I)

    # Note: q[i] does not require a reduction annotation for this choice
    # of parallelism because each i (and hence each q[i]) is owned by
    # exactly one tile I and one worker.

    #==============================================================
    # 3. Vectorization and unrolling
    #==============================================================
    # The innermost j-loop has stride-1 access to A[i, j], p[j], and s[j].
    # Vectorizing j maps well to SIMD on x64 (AVX/AVX2/AVX-512).
    vectorize(j, VW)

    # Unroll the inner j-loop further to increase ILP and reduce branch
    # and loop-control overhead. The exact factor can be tuned.
    unroll(j, 4)

    #==============================================================
    # 4. Scalar replacement / invariant hoisting
    #==============================================================
    # Custom directive:
    #   hoist_invariant(expr, dim)
    #   - evaluate 'expr' once per iteration of the loop indexed by
    #     the outer dimension (here: i) and keep the result in a scalar
    #     register across the inner loop over 'dim'.
    #
    # r[i] is invariant across j; q[i] is naturally handled as a
    # scalar accumulator inside the j-loop.
    hoist_invariant(r[i], j)   # load r[i] once per i-iteration
    hoist_invariant(q[i], j)   # keep q[i] as a scalar accumulator

    # (Modern compilers will also typically common-subexpression A[i, j]
    #  so that its single load in each (i, j) iteration feeds both
    #  the s[j] and q[i] updates.)
--- END OF MODEL: bicg-02 ---

--- START OF MODEL: bicg-03 ---
# Optimized model for PolyBench/C BiCG kernel

domain:
    # Matrix A is N x M
    i: dim in [0, N)  # row index
    j: dim in [0, M)  # column index

data:
    # Row-major storage for A: A[i, j] is stored at base + (i * M + j)
    A[i, j]: in DATA_TYPE  = (i, j) -> i * M + j

    # 1D vectors, contiguous storage
    p[j]:     in  DATA_TYPE = (j) -> j        # length M
    r[i]:     in  DATA_TYPE = (i) -> i        # length N
    s[j]:   out  DATA_TYPE = (j) -> j        # length M, computes s = A^T * r
    q[i]:   out  DATA_TYPE = (i) -> i        # length N, computes q = A * p

parameters:
    # Problem sizes (match N, M from the C code)
    N: int
    M: int

    # Tuning parameters for cache blocking, vectorization and unrolling
    TI: int  # tile size for i (rows), e.g., chosen to fit a strip of rows in L2
    TJ: int  # tile size for j (cols), e.g., aligned to SIMD width and L1
    VEC: int # SIMD vector length in elements (e.g., 4 or 8 for doubles)
    U:   int # unroll factor for the innermost j-loop (e.g., 2–8)

computation:
    # 1. Initialize s to zero.
    INIT_S:
        for j in [0, M):
            s[j] = 0

    # 2. Initialize q to zero and perform the fused BiCG update.
    #
    #    This matches the original kernel:
    #      for (i = 0; i < N; ++i) {
    #        q[i] = 0;
    #        for (j = 0; j < M; ++j) {
    #          s[j] += r[i] * A[i][j];
    #          q[i] += A[i][j] * p[j];
    #        }
    #      }
    #
    MAIN:
        for i in [0, N):
            INIT_Q:
                q[i] = 0
            UPDATE_SQ:
                for j in [0, M):
                    s[j] = s[j] + r[i] * A[i, j]
                    q[i] = q[i] + A[i, j] * p[j]

dependencies:
    # s[j] is an addition reduction over the i-dimension
    for j in [0, M), i1 in [0, N), i2 in [i1 + 1, N):
        UPDATE_SQ(i1, j) -> UPDATE_SQ(i2, j)

    # q[i] is an addition reduction over the j-dimension
    for i in [0, N), j1 in [0, M), j2 in [j1 + 1, M):
        UPDATE_SQ(i, j1) -> UPDATE_SQ(i, j2)

    # Updates must see the zero-initialized values of s[j] and q[i]
    for j in [0, M), i in [0, N):
        INIT_S(j) -> UPDATE_SQ(i, j)
    for i in [0, N), j in [0, M):
        INIT_Q(i) -> UPDATE_SQ(i, j)

optimization:
    # -----------------------------
    # 1. Cache blocking over rows and columns of A
    # -----------------------------
    # Block the 2D (i, j) iteration space so that we operate on tiles
    # of A of size TI x TJ.  This improves spatial and temporal locality
    # of p[j] and s[j] (reused across many rows) and of A itself.
    block(i, I, TI)   # i = I * TI + i_inner
    block(j, J, TJ)   # j = J * TJ + j_inner

    # Hoist the tile loops to form a tiled nest of the form:
    #   for I in tiles of i:
    #     for J in tiles of j:
    #       for i in I-tile:
    #         for j in J-tile:
    #           ...
    hoist(I)
    hoist(J)

    # -----------------------------
    # 2. Parallelism
    # -----------------------------
    # Parallelize across row tiles I.
    # Each tile I works on a disjoint subset of rows of A and q[i].
    # s[j] is a reduction over i, so updates from different I-tiles
    # can be combined with a reduction (e.g., thread-private s[j]
    # partial sums per tile, then merged).  This keeps additional
    # memory bounded (O(M) per worker) and can be tuned so that the
    # overhead remains well below 50% of the size of A.
    parallelize(I)  # with reduction_add on s[j] over i

    # The simple initialization loops are also parallelizable:
    parallelize(INIT_S.j)
    parallelize(MAIN.i)  # for INIT_Q, if executed outside the tiled nest

    # -----------------------------
    # 3. Vectorization and unrolling
    # -----------------------------
    # Vectorize along the innermost column dimension within each J-tile.
    # This exploits the fact that A[i, j], p[j], and s[j] are contiguous
    # in memory when j varies fastest.
    #
    # After blocking, the innermost dimension is the inner j within a J-tile.
    vectorize(j, VEC)

    # Unroll the innermost j-loop to increase instruction-level parallelism
    # and help the compiler schedule FMA operations efficiently.
    unroll(j, U)

    # -----------------------------
    # 4. Scalar replacement (register tiling)
    # -----------------------------
    # Keep r[i] and q[i] in registers across the inner j-loop.  In C this
    # corresponds to:
    #   DATA_TYPE ri = r[i];
    #   DATA_TYPE qi = 0;
    #   for (j ...) { ... use ri, qi ... }
    #   q[i] = qi;
    #
    # This avoids repeated loads/stores of q[i] and r[i] in the j-loop.
    scalarize({r[i], q[i]}, j)
    # scalarize(VAR_SET, DIMENSION):
    #   Replace repeated memory accesses to the given loop-invariant scalars
    #   inside loops over DIMENSION by register-resident temporaries.
--- END OF MODEL: bicg-03 ---

--- START OF MODEL: bicg-04 ---
domain:
    i: dim in [0, N)          # row index of A, q, r
    j: dim in [0, M)          # column index of A, p, s

data:
    # Matrix A is stored row-major as in the C code: A[i][j]
    A[i, j]: in DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * M + j

    # Vectors over columns (length M)
    p[j]: in    DATA_TYPE = (j) -> j
    s[j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (j) -> j   # initialized inside the kernel, then written

    # Vectors over rows (length N)
    r[i]: in    DATA_TYPE = (i) -> i
    q[i]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i) -> i   # initialized inside the kernel, then written

parameters:
    # Problem sizes (compile-time in PolyBench, but modeled as parameters here)
    N: int
    M: int

    # Tuning parameters for performance (chosen per hardware)
    TILE_I: int    # tile size in i (rows), e.g., 64 or 128
    TILE_J: int    # tile size in j (cols), e.g., 256 or 512
    VEC_WIDTH: int # SIMD width used along j

computation:
    # Initialize s and q exactly as in the C code
    S_INIT:
        for j in [0, M):
            s[j] = 0

    Q_INIT:
        for i in [0, N):
            q[i] = 0

    # Fused BiCG kernel:
    #   s[j] = sum_i r[i] * A[i,j]       (s = A^T * r)
    #   q[i] = sum_j A[i,j] * p[j]       (q = A * p)
    # The loops are fused so that each A[i,j] load is reused for both sums.
    CORE:
        for i, j:
            s[j] = s[j] + r[i] * A[i, j]
            q[i] = q[i] + A[i, j] * p[j]

dependencies:
    # s and q must be initialized before they are used in CORE.
    for j in [0, M), i in [0, N):
        S_INIT(j) -> CORE(i, j)

    for i in [0, N), j in [0, M):
        Q_INIT(i) -> CORE(i, j)

optimization:
    #-------------------------------
    # 1. Expose reductions explicitly
    #-------------------------------
    # s[j] is mathematically a sum over i:
    #   s[j] = sum_{i=0..N-1} r[i] * A[i,j]
    # Declaring it as a reduction along i allows parallelization and reassociation.
    reduction(s[j], i)   # '+' reduction along i

    # q[i] is mathematically a sum over j:
    #   q[i] = sum_{j=0..M-1} A[i,j] * p[j]
    # This is a scalar reduction inside the i-iteration and will be kept in a register.
    reduction(q[i], j)   # '+' reduction along j

    #-------------------------------
    # 2. Cache blocking (tiling)
    #-------------------------------
    # Tile the 2D CORE loop so that:
    #   - inner tiles of j fit p[j] and s[j] segments into L1/L2 cache,
    #   - outer tiles of i give good work chunks for threads.
    #
    # Resulting structure (conceptually):
    #   for I in 0..N step TILE_I:
    #     for J in 0..M step TILE_J:
    #       for i in I..min(I+TILE_I, N):
    #         for j in J..min(J+TILE_J, M):
    #           ... CORE body ...
    block(i, I, TILE_I)   # I: outer tile index for rows
    block(j, J, TILE_J)   # J: outer tile index for columns
    hoist(I)              # move I to the outermost possible level
    hoist(J)              # keep J just inside I for rectangular tiles

    #-------------------------------
    # 3. Parallelization
    #-------------------------------
    # Parallelize across row tiles I:
    #   - Each thread processes a distinct block of rows.
    #   - q[i] writes are thread-local (no sharing of the same i).
    #   - s[j] updates across different I-tiles form a reduction along i, as declared above.
    #
    # Implementation note:
    #   The reduction(s[j], i) can be realized with one temporary s_private[thread][j]
    #   per worker, followed by a final accumulation into s[j]. This adds
    #   O(num_threads * M) extra storage, which is well below the 50% overhead
    #   bound relative to the dominant A[N][M] for typical PolyBench sizes.
    parallelize(I)

    #-------------------------------
    # 4. SIMD and unrolling on the innermost loop
    #-------------------------------
    # After tiling, the innermost loop is over j inside a fixed (i, I, J) context:
    #   for j in J..J+TILE_J:
    #       s[j] += r[i] * A[i,j]
    #       q[i] += A[i,j] * p[j]
    #
    # Accesses in j are unit-stride for A[i,j], p[j], and s[j], which is ideal for SIMD.
    vectorize(j, VEC_WIDTH)  # map j-iterations to vector lanes
    unroll(j, 4)             # unroll by 4 for additional ILP within each SIMD chunk

    #-------------------------------
    # 5. Scalar hoisting (implicit)
    #-------------------------------
    # (Modeled as a comment; typically performed automatically by compilers.)
    # - Hoist r[i] out of the inner j-loop and keep it in a register:
    #       ri = r[i];
    #       for j: s[j] += ri * A[i,j]; ...
    # - Keep q[i] as a scalar accumulator in a register across the inner j-loop,
    #   writing q[i] back to memory once per i (not per j).
    # These are standard loop-invariant code motion and scalar replacement
    # optimizations and do not require an explicit directive here.
--- END OF MODEL: bicg-04 ---

--- START OF MODEL: bicg-05 ---
domain:
    i: dim in [0, N)     # row index of A, q, r
    j: dim in [0, M)     # column index of A, s, p

data:
    # A is stored row-major as in the original C code: A[i][j] == A[i*M + j].
    A[i, j]: in DATA_TYPE   = (i, j) -> i * M + j

    # Input vectors.
    p[j]:    in DATA_TYPE   = (j)    -> j         # length M
    r[i]:    in DATA_TYPE   = (i)    -> i         # length N

    # Output vectors (fully overwritten by the kernel).
    s[j]: out DATA_TYPE     = (j)    -> j         # length M, s = A^T * r
    q[i]: out DATA_TYPE     = (i)    -> i         # length N, q = A * p

parameters:
    N:  int  # number of rows of A, length of q and r
    M:  int  # number of columns of A, length of s and p

    # Tunable tiling and SIMD parameters.
    TI: int  # tile size along i (rows), chosen for good L2/LLC locality
    TJ: int  # tile size along j (cols), chosen so A tile + p[j] fit in L1/L2
    V:  int  # SIMD vector length along j (e.g., 4 for AVX2 double, 8 for AVX2 float)
    U:  int  # unroll factor for j within a SIMD vector (e.g., 2–4)

    # Upper bound on the number of parallel partitions along i.
    # Implementation uses per-thread private partial sums for s[j] and
    # reduces them at the end. To keep the extra storage below 50% of
    # the size of A, we enforce:
    #   1 <= T <= min(MAX_THREADS, floor(N / 2))
    # so that a T x M temporary array of partial s never exceeds 0.5 * N*M.
    T:  int  # logical max number of threads/partitions along i

computation:
    # BiCG kernel computes two matrix-vector products:
    #   q = A * p        (size N)
    #   s = A^T * r      (size M)
    #
    # The original C code fuses the two so that each A[i][j] is loaded once
    # and used in both dot-products.

    # s[j] = (A^T * r)[j] = sum over rows i of r[i] * A[i, j]
    S_REDUCTION:
      for j in [0, M):
        s[j] = sum(i, r[i] * A[i, j])

    # q[i] = (A * p)[i] = sum over columns j of A[i, j] * p[j]
    Q_REDUCTION:
      for i in [0, N):
        q[i] = sum(j, A[i, j] * p[j])

dependencies:
    # S_REDUCTION and Q_REDUCTION:
    # - read A, r, p
    # - write disjoint outputs s and q
    # Therefore there are no flow or anti-dependencies between them,
    # and they may be executed in any order or fused into a single loop nest.

optimization:
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # 1. Fuse the two reductions over A
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # Fuse S_REDUCTION and Q_REDUCTION so that a single traversal of A
    # computes both s and q:
    #   for i:
    #     q[i] = sum_j A[i,j] * p[j]
    #     for all j in the same traversal:
    #       s[j] accumulates r[i] * A[i,j]
    #
    # This matches the original C kernel and roughly halves the memory
    # traffic to A compared to computing s and q in separate passes.
    fuse(S_REDUCTION, Q_REDUCTION)

    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # 2. Tile the (i, j) iteration space for cache locality
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # Block along the row (i) and column (j) dimensions of A in the
    # fused loop nest. TI is chosen so that:
    #   - a tile of q[i] and r[i] and the corresponding rows of A
    #     fit comfortably in L2/L3,
    # and TJ is chosen so that:
    #   - a tile of A[i, j] over j together with p[j] fits in L1/L2.
    #
    # Conceptually this yields:
    #   for I in tiles of i with size TI:
    #     for J in tiles of j with size TJ:
    #       for i in I:
    #         for j in J:
    #           use A[i,j], p[j], r[i]
    block(i, I, TI)
    block(j, J, TJ)

    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # 3. Parallelize over tiles of i with a reduction on s
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # Parallelize the outer tile loop I across up to T worker threads.
    # Each worker t accumulates its own private partial sums for s[j]
    # over the subset of rows i assigned to it:
    #
    #   s_private[t][j] += r[i] * A[i,j]   for i in tile subset of t
    #   q[i]            += A[i,j] * p[j]   for those i
    #
    # After all tiles have been processed, a final reduction over t
    # combines s_private[t][j] into the global s[j]:
    #
    #   s[j] = sum_t s_private[t][j]
    #
    # The number of threads actually used obeys:
    #   1 <= threads_used <= T <= min(MAX_THREADS, floor(N/2))
    # so that the extra storage for s_private (threads_used x M) never
    # exceeds 50% of the size of A (N x M).
    parallelize(I)

    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # 4. Exploit SIMD and ILP along j
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # Vectorize the innermost j-loop so that:
    #   - A[i, j:j+V-1] and p[j:j+V-1] are loaded in SIMD registers,
    #   - q[i] is kept in a scalar register and updated via FMA where
    #     available,
    #   - r[i] is hoisted out of the j-loop into a scalar register and
    #     multiplied with the SIMD A[i, j:j+V-1] to update s[j:j+V-1].
    #
    # Unrolling by U within the vectorized loop further increases ILP
    # and reduces loop overhead.
    vectorize(j, V)
    unroll(j, U)
--- END OF MODEL: bicg-05 ---

#include <stdio.h>
#include <unistd.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <math.h>

/* Include polybench common header. */
#include <polybench.h>

/* Include benchmark-specific header. */
#include "cholesky.h"


/* Array initialization. */
static
void init_array(int n,
		DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(A,N,N,n,n))
{
  int i, j;

  for (i = 0; i < n; i++)
    {
      for (j = 0; j <= i; j++)
	A[i][j] = (DATA_TYPE)(-j % n) / n + 1;
      for (j = i+1; j < n; j++) {
	A[i][j] = 0;
      }
      A[i][i] = 1;
    }

  /* Make the matrix positive semi-definite. */
  int r,s,t;
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(B, DATA_TYPE, N, N, n, n);
  for (r = 0; r < n; ++r)
    for (s = 0; s < n; ++s)
      (POLYBENCH_ARRAY(B))[r][s] = 0;
  for (t = 0; t < n; ++t)
    for (r = 0; r < n; ++r)
      for (s = 0; s < n; ++s)
	(POLYBENCH_ARRAY(B))[r][s] += A[r][t] * A[s][t];
    for (r = 0; r < n; ++r)
      for (s = 0; s < n; ++s)
	A[r][s] = (POLYBENCH_ARRAY(B))[r][s];
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(B);

}


/* DCE code. Must scan the entire live-out data.
   Can be used also to check the correctness of the output. */
static
void print_array(int n,
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(A,N,N,n,n))

{
  int i, j;

  POLYBENCH_DUMP_START;
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_BEGIN("A");
  for (i = 0; i < n; i++)
    for (j = 0; j <= i; j++) {
    if ((i * n + j) % 20 == 0) fprintf (POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, "\n");
    fprintf (POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, DATA_PRINTF_MODIFIER, A[i][j]);
  }
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_END("A");
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_FINISH;
}


/* Main computational kernel. The whole function will be timed,
   including the call and return. */
static
void kernel_cholesky[[gnu::flatten, gnu::noinline]](int n,
		     DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(A,N,N,n,n))
{
  int i, j, k;


#pragma scop
  for (i = 0; i < _PB_N; i++) {
     //j<i
     for (j = 0; j < i; j++) {
        for (k = 0; k < j; k++) {
           A[i][j] -= A[i][k] * A[j][k];
        }
        A[i][j] /= A[j][j];
     }
     // i==j case
     for (k = 0; k < i; k++) {
        A[i][i] -= A[i][k] * A[i][k];
     }
     A[i][i] = SQRT_FUN(A[i][i]);
  }
#pragma endscop

}


int main(int argc, char** argv)
{
  /* Retrieve problem size. */
  int n = N;

  /* Variable declaration/allocation. */
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(A, DATA_TYPE, N, N, n, n);

  /* Initialize array(s). */
  init_array (n, POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A));

  /* Start timer. */
  polybench_start_instruments;

  /* Run kernel. */
  kernel_cholesky (n, POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A));

  /* Stop and print timer. */
  polybench_stop_instruments;
  polybench_print_instruments;

  /* Prevent dead-code elimination. All live-out data must be printed
     by the function call in argument. */
  polybench_prevent_dce(print_array(n, POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A)));

  /* Be clean. */
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(A);

  return 0;
}

    # Left-looking in-place Cholesky factorization: A becomes its own lower-triangular factor L.
    for i in seq(0, N):

        for j in seq(0, i):

        # dot_ii = Σ_{k=0}^{i-1} A[i, k] * A[i, k]

            dot_ii = sum(k in [0, i)) (A[i, k] * A[i, k])

    for i in [0, N), j in [0, i):

domain:
    i: dim in [0, N)
    j: dim in [0, N)
    k: dim in [0, N)

data:
    # Full N×N matrix stored row-major; only the lower triangle (j ≤ i) is used.
    # On input: A is symmetric positive definite.
    # On output: A holds the Cholesky factor L (lower-triangular) such that A ≈ L · Lᵀ.
    A[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j  # row-major

parameters:
    N: int  # matrix dimension

    # Cache / SIMD tuning parameters
    TI: int  # tile size for i (e.g., 32)
    TJ: int  # tile size for j (e.g., 32)
    TK: int  # tile size for k-reductions (e.g., 64)
    V:  int  # SIMD width for vectorization over k (e.g., 8 for AVX-512 double)

computation:
    # Off-diagonal entries: for each row i, columns j < i.
    # This expresses the left-looking Cholesky update:
    #   A[i,j] = (A[i,j] - ∑_{k=0}^{j-1} A[i,k] * A[j,k]) / A[j,j]
    # written in one assignment so that the sum is accumulated in registers
    # instead of repeatedly updating A[i,j] in memory.
    OFFDIAG:
        for i in seq([0, N)):
            for j in seq([0, i)):   # sequential in j: A[i,j] depends on A[i,0..j-1]
                A[i, j] =
                    ( A[i, j]
                      - sum(k in [0, j)) (A[i, k] * A[j, k]) )
                    / A[j, j]

    # Diagonal entries:
    #   A[i,i] = sqrt( A[i,i] - ∑_{k=0}^{i-1} A[i,k]^2 )
    # again with the reduction written explicitly.
    DIAG:
        for i in seq([0, N)):
            A[i, i] =
                SQRT_FUN(
                    A[i, i]
                    - sum(k in [0, i)) (A[i, k] * A[i, k])
                )

dependencies:
    # Within a fixed row i, off-diagonal elements must be computed in increasing j,
    # because A[i,j] uses A[i,k] for all k < j.
    for i in [0, N), j1 in [0, N), j2 in [0, N):
        if (j1 < j2) and (j2 < i):
            OFFDIAG(i, j1) -> OFFDIAG(i, j2)

    # Each off-diagonal element A[i,j] depends on the entire row j (0..j) being
    # already factorized, in particular on A[j,j] (for the division) and
    # A[j,k] for k < j (used in the dot product).
    # This is enforced by depending on DIAG(j), which in turn depends on all
    # OFFDIAG(j, k) with k < j.
    for i in [0, N), j in [0, N):
        if j < i:
            DIAG(j) -> OFFDIAG(i, j)

    # The diagonal element A[i,i] depends on all off-diagonal elements in row i,
    # since its reduction uses A[i,k] for k < i.
    for i in [0, N), j in [0, N):
        if j < i:
            OFFDIAG(i, j) -> DIAG(i)

optimization:
    # ------------------------------
    # Loop blocking (tiling)
    # ------------------------------

    # Block the outer i and j dimensions. This restructures the triangular
    # iteration into tiles but preserves the original lexicographic order
    # (and thus dependencies). Many tiles will be partially filled because
    # of the j < i constraint, but data locality improves: elements of nearby
    # rows/columns live in cache together.
    block(i, I, TI)
    block(j, J, TJ)
    hoist(I)   # I is the outermost loop
    hoist(J)   # J is just inside I, before the scalar i,j loops

    # Block the reduction dimension k for both reductions. This lets us:
    #   - operate on TK-sized chunks of rows A[i,*] and A[j,*],
    #   - keep those chunks in cache,
    #   - vectorize efficiently across k.
    # The transformation logically turns
    #   sum(k in [0, bound)) ...
    # into nested sums over tiles Kb and intra-tile k, handling short
    # last tiles when bound is not multiple of TK.
    block(k, Kb, TK)
    hoist(Kb)  # Kb is hoisted outside the innermost loops to reuse tiles

    # ------------------------------
    # Vectorization and unrolling
    # ------------------------------

    # Within each k-tile, vectorize the reduction over k. The loop body
    # performs independent multiply-adds A[i,k]*A[j,k] (or A[i,k]*A[i,k]),
    # so it is SIMD-friendly. The compiler can implement:
    #   - vector loads from row-major A[i,*] and A[j,*],
    #   - fused multiply-adds accumulating into scalar temporaries.
    vectorize(k, V)

    # Unroll the inner k loop by a small factor to reduce loop overhead and
    # expose more Instructions Per Cycle (IPC). This works together with
    # vectorization; the compiler can group several SIMD vectors per unrolled
    # iteration.
    unroll(k, 4)

    # ------------------------------
    # Parallelization notes
    # ------------------------------

    # The outer dimension i is kept sequential (no parallelize(i)) because
    # every row i depends on all previous rows j < i through A[j,*] and A[j,j].
    # Similarly, j is sequential within each i. Parallelism is thus mainly
    # vector-level (SIMD) and not across threads inside this kernel without
    # switching to a different (e.g., blocked/right-looking) Cholesky algorithm.

domain:
    i: dim in [0, N)            # row index
    j: dim in [0, N)            # column index (only j <= i is updated)
    k: dim in [0, N)            # reduction index for inner products

data:
    # A holds on input a symmetric positive semi-definite matrix.
    # On output, its lower triangle (including diagonal) stores the
    # Cholesky factor L such that A_in ≈ L * L^T. The upper triangle is unused.
    A[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j   # Row-major

    # Extra 1D buffer storing 1 / A[i, i] after each diagonal is computed.
    # This lets us replace expensive divisions by cheaper multiplications.
    inv_diag[i]: out DATA_TYPE = (i) -> i           # Contiguous 1D layout

parameters:
    N: int                         # problem size (matrix is N x N)

    # Tunable optimization parameters (chosen to match cache/SIMD of target):
    BJ: int                        # tile size for j (e.g., 32)
    BK: int                        # tile size for k (e.g., 64)
    VEC: int                       # SIMD width in elements (e.g., 4 for double, 8 for float)
    UNROLL_K: int                  # unroll factor for k (e.g., 4)

computation:
    # Left-looking in-place Cholesky; i and j are explicitly sequential
    # because rows and columns are mutually dependent.
    ROW_FACTOR:
        for i in seq([0, N)):                 # i must be sequential
            # Off-diagonal elements in row i: columns 0..i-1.
            OFFDIAG_ROW:
                for j in seq([0, i)):         # j must be sequential within the row
                    # L(i,j) = ( A(i,j) - sum_{k<j} L(i,k) * L(j,k) ) / L(j,j)
                    # We use inv_diag[j] so that division is turned into a multiply.
                    A[i, j] =
                        ( A[i, j]
                          - sum(k in [0, j),
                                 A[i, k] * A[j, k]) ) * inv_diag[j]

            # Diagonal element in row i:
            DIAG_ROW:
                # L(i,i) = sqrt( A(i,i) - sum_{k<i} L(i,k)^2 )
                A[i, i] =
                    SQRT_FUN( A[i, i]
                              - sum(k in [0, i),
                                     A[i, k] * A[i, k]) )

                # Precompute reciprocal of the diagonal for later rows.
                # Future off-diagonal updates with column j = i use inv_diag[i].
                inv_diag[i] = 1.0 / A[i, i]

optimization:
    # The outer row loop i is left as the outermost and strictly sequential;
    # all true loop-carried dependences go through i.
    hoist(i)

    # There are strong dependences along j within a row (each A[i,j] uses A[i,k] for k<j),
    # so we keep j sequential but tile it for locality.
    block(j, J, BJ)
    # After tiling, iterations are over:
    #   J in [0, ceil(N / BJ)), j_inner in [0, BJ)
    # with the guard j = J*BJ + j_inner < i enforced by the triangular domain.

    # Tile the k reductions (dot products) that appear in both off-diagonal and diagonal
    # updates to improve cache reuse and to create a long inner loop amenable to SIMD.
    block(k, K, BK)

    # Vectorize the innermost k dimension in the reductions. This maps naturally to
    # AVX/AVX-512 on x64 by choosing VEC to match the hardware SIMD width in elements.
    vectorize(k, VEC)

    # Unroll the k loop inside each vector chunk to reduce control overhead and
    # expose more instruction-level parallelism within each core.
    unroll(k, UNROLL_K)

    # The computation explicitly uses inv_diag[i] instead of performing
    #   A[i, j] /= A[j, j]
    # for every off-diagonal entry. This implements:
    #   1) DIAG_ROW:    inv_diag[j] = 1.0 / A[j, j]    # one division per row
    #   2) OFFDIAG_ROW: A[i, j] *= inv_diag[j]         # many cheap multiplies

    # at the cost of an extra O(N) buffer (well below 50% extra memory vs. A).

domain:
    # Matrix is N x N, lower-triangular part is meaningful.
    i: dim in [0, N)      # row index
    j: dim in [0, N)      # column index, will be used with j < i
    k: dim in [0, N)      # inner-product / reduction index

data:
    # A holds the input symmetric positive definite matrix and is overwritten
    # in-place with its Cholesky factor L (stored in the lower triangle).
    A[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j   # row-major storage

    # Temporary buffer: reciprocal of diagonal entries, used to replace
    # O(N^2) divisions by multiplications and only incur O(N) divisions.
    inv_diag[j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (j) -> j         # 1 / A[j, j] after row j is completed
                                                    # size O(N), << 50% extra memory

parameters:
    N: int                  # problem size

    # Tuning parameters for the k-dimension (reduction dimension).
    TK: int                 # tile size for k (e.g., 32–128, tuned for L1 cache)
    VEC_K: int              # vector width in k (e.g., 4 or 8 depending on SIMD width)
    UNR_K: int              # unroll factor for innermost k loop (e.g., 2–4)

computation:
    # Optional: initialize inv_diag (not strictly needed for correctness, but explicit).
    INIT_INV_DIAG:
      for j in [0, N):
        inv_diag[j] = 0

    # Main in-place left-looking Cholesky factorization:
    # for each row i, we:
    #  1. compute off-diagonal entries A[i, j] for j < i,
    #  2. compute the diagonal entry A[i, i],
    #  3. store its reciprocal in inv_diag[i] for later rows.

    for i in seq(0, N):

        # ----- Off-diagonal entries in row i: columns 0..i-1 -----
        for j in seq(0, i):
            if j < i:
                # Dot product of rows i and j up to column j-1:
                #   dot_ij = sum_{k = 0}^{j-1} A[i, k] * A[j, k]
                OFFDIAG_DOT[i, j]:
                  dot_ij = sum(k in [0, j), A[i, k] * A[j, k])

                # Solve for A[i, j]:
                # Original code:
                #   for (k = 0; k < j; k++) A[i][j] -= A[i][k] * A[j][k];
                #   A[i][j] /= A[j][j];
                #
                # Equivalent mathematically:
                #   A[i, j] = (A[i, j] - dot_ij) / A[j, j]
                #
                # Here we precompute inv_diag[j] = 1 / A[j, j] once, and use:
                OFFDIAG_UPDATE[i, j]:
                  A[i, j] = (A[i, j] - dot_ij) * inv_diag[j]

        # ----- Diagonal entry in row i -----
        # Compute:
        #   diag_correction = sum_{k = 0}^{i-1} A[i, k]^2
        # and then:
        #   A[i, i] = sqrt(A[i, i] - diag_correction)
        DIAG_DOT[i]:
          diag_correction = sum(k in [0, i), A[i, k] * A[i, k])

        DIAG_UPDATE[i]:
          A[i, i] = SQRT_FUN(A[i, i] - diag_correction)

        # Precompute 1 / A[i, i] for reuse in subsequent rows (i' > i).
        INV_DIAG_UPDATE[i]:
          inv_diag[i] = (DATA_TYPE)1.0 / A[i, i]

dependencies:
    # Naming for clarity:
    #   OFFDIAG_DOT[i, j], OFFDIAG_UPDATE[i, j]
    #   DIAG_DOT[i], DIAG_UPDATE[i], INV_DIAG_UPDATE[i]
    #   "row(i)" := all operations for this i

    # 1. Row-ordering: row i must complete before any later row that uses its data.
    #    In particular, to compute OFFDIAG_UPDATE[i, j], row j must be fully done.
    for i in [1, N):
        row(i - 1) -> row(i)

    # 2. Within a row, all OFFDIAG_* at (i, j) depend on the diagonal of row j,
    #    because they require A[j, j] (via inv_diag[j]) and A[j, k] for k < j.
    for i in [0, N), j in [0, i):
        DIAG_UPDATE[j] -> OFFDIAG_DOT[i, j]
        DIAG_UPDATE[j] -> OFFDIAG_UPDATE[i, j]
        INV_DIAG_UPDATE[j] -> OFFDIAG_UPDATE[i, j]

    # 3. Diagonal of row i depends on all off-diagonal entries in that row.
    for i in [0, N):
        for j in [0, i):
            OFFDIAG_UPDATE[i, j] -> DIAG_DOT[i]
            OFFDIAG_UPDATE[i, j] -> DIAG_UPDATE[i]

    # 4. INV_DIAG_UPDATE[i] depends on the finalized diagonal.
    for i in [0, N):
        DIAG_UPDATE[i] -> INV_DIAG_UPDATE[i]

    # 5. There are no cross-iteration dependencies inside the k-dimension reductions:
    #    OFFDIAG_DOT[i, j] and DIAG_DOT[i] each reduce into a private scalar, so
    #    iterations in k are independent modulo the reduction.

optimization:
    # 1. Arithmetic optimizations
    #    - Use explicit scalar reductions (dot_ij, diag_correction) instead of
    #      repeatedly updating A[i, j] or A[i, i] inside the k-loop.
    #    - Introduce inv_diag[j] so that:
    #         * we do only N divisions (once per diagonal) in INV_DIAG_UPDATE,
    #         * instead of O(N^2) divisions in OFFDIAG_UPDATE.
    #      The replaced operations are multiplications, which are much cheaper.

    # 2. Blocking of the reduction dimension k
    #    Apply tiling to k in all reductions (OFFDIAG_DOT and DIAG_DOT) so that
    #    each tile of A[i, k] and A[j, k] fits in L1 cache and is reused efficiently.
    #
    #    Conceptually:
    #      for k in [0, j)   ->   for K in [0, ceil(j / TK)):
    #                               for kk in [K*TK, min((K+1)*TK, j)):
    block(k, kk, TK)

    # 3. Vectorization and unrolling of innermost tiles
    #    The kk-dimension is contiguous in memory (row-major layout), so we vectorize
    #    over kk and unroll slightly to gain instruction-level parallelism.
    vectorize(kk, VEC_K)
    unroll(kk, UNR_K)

    # 4. Parallelization across kk (within a reduction)
    #    Each reduction "sum over k" is purely over reads of A; the only write is
    #    into the private accumulator (dot_ij or diag_correction).
    #    We can parallelize tiles of kk using a reduction (tree sum) without
    #    violating dependencies in i or j.
    parallelize(kk)

    # 5. Keep i and j strictly sequential
    #    Outer dimensions i and j are *not* parallelized or interchanged because:

# Optimized model for cholesky.c (lower‑triangular Cholesky factorization)

domain:
    i: dim in [0, N)         # row index
    j: dim in [0, N)         # column index (only j <= i is used)
    k: dim in [0, N)         # reduction index

data:
    # Dense N x N matrix, row-major. Only the lower triangle (j <= i) is used.
    A[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j

    # This removes repeated divisions inside the main kernel.
    inv_diag[i]: aux DATA_TYPE = (i) -> i

parameters:
    N:  int   # matrix dimension
    BI: int   # block size for i-tiling (tunable; e.g., 64)
    VF: int   # SIMD width for vectorization of reductions (e.g., 4 or 8)
    UK: int   # unroll factor for k (multiple of VF; e.g., 4 * VF)

computation:
    # In-place Cholesky factorization of symmetric positive-definite A.
    # On exit, A[i, j] for j <= i contains the lower-triangular factor L
    # such that A_original = L * L^T. The upper triangle is unused.

    for i in seq(0, N):                # 0 <= i < N, must be sequential
        # Off-diagonal entries in row i: L[i, j] for 0 <= j < i.
        # seq(0, i) denotes the half-open interval 0 <= j < i.
        for j in seq(0, i):            # loop-carried deps: j is sequential
            S_off(i, j):
                A[i, j] =
                    ( A[i, j]
                      - sum(k in [0, j),
                            A[i, k] * A[j, k]) )
                    * inv_diag[j]      # multiply by precomputed 1 / A[j, j]

        # Diagonal entry in row i: L[i, i].
        S_diag(i):
            A[i, i] =
                SQRT_FUN(              # matches SQRT_FUN used in the C code
                    A[i, i]
                    - sum(k in [0, i),
                          A[i, k] * A[i, k])
                )

        # Precompute reciprocal of the diagonal for use in later rows.
        S_inv(i):
            inv_diag[i] = 1.0 / A[i, i]

dependencies:
    # 1. Each off-diagonal element L[i, j] depends on:
    #    - the diagonal factor (via its reciprocal) from row j
    #    - all earlier off-diagonals in the same row i
    for i in [0, N), j in [0, i):
        S_inv(j) -> S_off(i, j)        # need inv_diag[j] before using it
    for i in [0, N), j in [0, i), k in [0, j):
        S_off(i, k) -> S_off(i, j)     # A[i, j] uses A[i, k] for k < j

    # 2. The diagonal of row i depends on all off-diagonals in that row.
    for i in [0, N), j in [0, i):
        S_off(i, j) -> S_diag(i)

    # 3. inv_diag[i] depends on the final value of the diagonal A[i, i].
    for i in [0, N):
        S_diag(i) -> S_inv(i)

    # Arithmetic optimization:
    # - The auxiliary array inv_diag[i] hoists one division per (i, j) pair
    #   out of the inner loops. Each off-diagonal update now performs a
    #   multiply instead of a divide, which is substantially cheaper on x64.

    # Cache / locality optimization:

    #   (their off-diagonals and partial diagonals) fits better into cache.

    hoist(I)                 # place the tile loop as outermost around i

    #   dependencies except for the scalar reduction variable, so it can be
    #   efficiently SIMD-vectorized and unrolled.

    unroll(k, UK)            # unroll the k-loop by factor UK (multiple of VF)

    # - Due to explicit dependencies between rows (i dimension) and columns
    #   (j dimension), i and j must remain sequential. Parallelism is
    #   therefore exploited only via vectorization of k.
    #   No parallelize(i) or parallelize(j) is legal here.

    #   elements with j > i; this is enforced by the bounds j < i in S_off
    #   and by using only A[i, k] with k < i in S_diag.

#include <stdio.h>
#include <unistd.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <math.h>

/* Include polybench common header. */
#include <polybench.h>

/* Include benchmark-specific header. */
#include "cholesky.h"


/* Array initialization. */
static
void init_array(int n,
		DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(A,N,N,n,n))
{
  int i, j;

  for (i = 0; i < n; i++)
    {
      for (j = 0; j <= i; j++)
	A[i][j] = (DATA_TYPE)(-j % n) / n + 1;
      for (j = i+1; j < n; j++) {
	A[i][j] = 0;
      }
      A[i][i] = 1;
    }

  /* Make the matrix positive semi-definite. */
  int r,s,t;
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(B, DATA_TYPE, N, N, n, n);
  for (r = 0; r < n; ++r)
    for (s = 0; s < n; ++s)
      (POLYBENCH_ARRAY(B))[r][s] = 0;
  for (t = 0; t < n; ++t)
    for (r = 0; r < n; ++r)
      for (s = 0; s < n; ++s)
	(POLYBENCH_ARRAY(B))[r][s] += A[r][t] * A[s][t];
    for (r = 0; r < n; ++r)
      for (s = 0; s < n; ++s)
	A[r][s] = (POLYBENCH_ARRAY(B))[r][s];
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(B);

}


/* DCE code. Must scan the entire live-out data.
   Can be used also to check the correctness of the output. */
static
void print_array(int n,
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(A,N,N,n,n))

{
  int i, j;

  POLYBENCH_DUMP_START;
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_BEGIN("A");
  for (i = 0; i < n; i++)
    for (j = 0; j <= i; j++) {
    if ((i * n + j) % 20 == 0) fprintf (POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, "\n");
    fprintf (POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, DATA_PRINTF_MODIFIER, A[i][j]);
  }
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_END("A");
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_FINISH;
}


/* Main computational kernel. The whole function will be timed,
   including the call and return. */
static
void kernel_cholesky[[gnu::flatten, gnu::noinline]](int n,
		     DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(A,N,N,n,n))
{
  int i, j, k;


#pragma scop
  for (i = 0; i < _PB_N; i++) {
     //j<i
     for (j = 0; j < i; j++) {
        for (k = 0; k < j; k++) {
           A[i][j] -= A[i][k] * A[j][k];
        }
        A[i][j] /= A[j][j];
     }
     // i==j case
     for (k = 0; k < i; k++) {
        A[i][i] -= A[i][k] * A[i][k];
     }
     A[i][i] = SQRT_FUN(A[i][i]);
  }
#pragma endscop

}


int main(int argc, char** argv)
{
  /* Retrieve problem size. */
  int n = N;

  /* Variable declaration/allocation. */
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(A, DATA_TYPE, N, N, n, n);

  /* Initialize array(s). */
  init_array (n, POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A));

  /* Start timer. */
  polybench_start_instruments;

  /* Run kernel. */
  kernel_cholesky (n, POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A));

  /* Stop and print timer. */
  polybench_stop_instruments;
  polybench_print_instruments;

  /* Prevent dead-code elimination. All live-out data must be printed
     by the function call in argument. */
  polybench_prevent_dce(print_array(n, POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A)));

  /* Be clean. */
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(A);

  return 0;
}

    # Off-diagonal entries: for each row i, columns j < i.
    # This expresses the left-looking Cholesky update:
    #   A[i,j] = (A[i,j] - ∑_{k=0}^{j-1} A[i,k] * A[j,k]) / A[j,j]
    # written in one assignment so that the sum is accumulated in registers
    # instead of repeatedly updating A[i,j] in memory.

        for i in seq([0, N)):
            for j in seq([0, i)):   # sequential in j: A[i,j] depends on A[i,0..j-1]
                A[i, j] =
                    ( A[i, j]
                      - sum(k in [0, j)) (A[i, k] * A[j, k]) )
                    / A[j, j]

    # Diagonal entries:
    #   A[i,i] = sqrt( A[i,i] - ∑_{k=0}^{i-1} A[i,k]^2 )
    # again with the reduction written explicitly.
    DIAG:
        for i in seq([0, N)):
            A[i, i] =
                SQRT_FUN(
                    A[i, i]
                    - sum(k in [0, i)) (A[i, k] * A[i, k])

    # Within a fixed row i, off-diagonal elements must be computed in increasing j,
    # because A[i,j] uses A[i,k] for all k < j.
    for i in [0, N), j1 in [0, N), j2 in [0, N):
        if (j1 < j2) and (j2 < i):
            OFFDIAG(i, j1) -> OFFDIAG(i, j2)

    # A[j,k] for k < j (used in the dot product).

    BJ: int                        # tile size for j (e.g., 32)
    BK: int                        # tile size for k (e.g., 64)
    VEC: int                       # SIMD width in elements (e.g., 4 for double, 8 for float)
    UNROLL_K: int                  # unroll factor for k (e.g., 4)

    # Left-looking in-place Cholesky; i and j are explicitly sequential
    # because rows and columns are mutually dependent.

        for i in seq([0, N)):                 # i must be sequential
            # Off-diagonal elements in row i: columns 0..i-1.
            OFFDIAG_ROW:
                for j in seq([0, i)):         # j must be sequential within the row

                    # We use inv_diag[j] so that division is turned into a multiply.
                    A[i, j] =
                        ( A[i, j]
                          - sum(k in [0, j),
                                 A[i, k] * A[j, k]) ) * inv_diag[j]

            DIAG_ROW:
                # L(i,i) = sqrt( A(i,i) - sum_{k<i} L(i,k)^2 )
                A[i, i] =
                    SQRT_FUN( A[i, i]
                              - sum(k in [0, i),
                                     A[i, k] * A[i, k]) )

                # Precompute reciprocal of the diagonal for later rows.
                # Future off-diagonal updates with column j = i use inv_diag[i].
                inv_diag[i] = 1.0 / A[i, i]

    # The outer row loop i is left as the outermost and strictly sequential;
    # all true loop-carried dependences go through i.

    vectorize(k, VEC)

    # for each row i, we:
    #  1. compute off-diagonal entries A[i, j] for j < i,
    #  2. compute the diagonal entry A[i, i],
    #  3. store its reciprocal in inv_diag[i] for later rows.

    for i in seq(0, N):

        # ----- Off-diagonal entries in row i: columns 0..i-1 -----
        for j in seq(0, i):
            if j < i:
                # Dot product of rows i and j up to column j-1:
                #   dot_ij = sum_{k = 0}^{j-1} A[i, k] * A[j, k]
                OFFDIAG_DOT[i, j]:
                  dot_ij = sum(k in [0, j), A[i, k] * A[j, k])

                # Solve for A[i, j]:
                # Original code:
                #   for (k = 0; k < j; k++) A[i][j] -= A[i][k] * A[j][k];
                #   A[i][j] /= A[j][j];
                #
                # Equivalent mathematically:
                #   A[i, j] = (A[i, j] - dot_ij) / A[j, j]
                #
                # Here we precompute inv_diag[j] = 1 / A[j, j] once, and use:
                OFFDIAG_UPDATE[i, j]:
                  A[i, j] = (A[i, j] - dot_ij) * inv_diag[j]

        # ----- Diagonal entry in row i -----
        # Compute:
        #   diag_correction = sum_{k = 0}^{i-1} A[i, k]^2
        # and then:
        #   A[i, i] = sqrt(A[i, i] - diag_correction)
        DIAG_DOT[i]:
          diag_correction = sum(k in [0, i), A[i, k] * A[i, k])

        DIAG_UPDATE[i]:
          A[i, i] = SQRT_FUN(A[i, i] - diag_correction)

        # Precompute 1 / A[i, i] for reuse in subsequent rows (i' > i).
        INV_DIAG_UPDATE[i]:
          inv_diag[i] = (DATA_TYPE)1.0 / A[i, i]

dependencies:
    # Naming for clarity:
    #   OFFDIAG_DOT[i, j], OFFDIAG_UPDATE[i, j]
    #   DIAG_DOT[i], DIAG_UPDATE[i], INV_DIAG_UPDATE[i]
    #   "row(i)" := all operations for this i

    # 1. Row-ordering: row i must complete before any later row that uses its data.
    #    In particular, to compute OFFDIAG_UPDATE[i, j], row j must be fully done.
    for i in [1, N):
        row(i - 1) -> row(i)

    # 2. Within a row, all OFFDIAG_* at (i, j) depend on the diagonal of row j,
    #    because they require A[j, j] (via inv_diag[j]) and A[j, k] for k < j.
    for i in [0, N), j in [0, i):
        DIAG_UPDATE[j] -> OFFDIAG_DOT[i, j]
        DIAG_UPDATE[j] -> OFFDIAG_UPDATE[i, j]
        INV_DIAG_UPDATE[j] -> OFFDIAG_UPDATE[i, j]

    # 3. Diagonal of row i depends on all off-diagonal entries in that row.
    for i in [0, N):
        for j in [0, i):
            OFFDIAG_UPDATE[i, j] -> DIAG_DOT[i]
            OFFDIAG_UPDATE[i, j] -> DIAG_UPDATE[i]

    # 4. INV_DIAG_UPDATE[i] depends on the finalized diagonal.
    for i in [0, N):
        DIAG_UPDATE[i] -> INV_DIAG_UPDATE[i]

    # 5. There are no cross-iteration dependencies inside the k-dimension reductions:
    #    OFFDIAG_DOT[i, j] and DIAG_DOT[i] each reduce into a private scalar, so
    #    iterations in k are independent modulo the reduction.

optimization:
    # 1. Arithmetic optimizations
    #    - Use explicit scalar reductions (dot_ij, diag_correction) instead of
    #      repeatedly updating A[i, j] or A[i, i] inside the k-loop.
    #    - Introduce inv_diag[j] so that:
    #         * we do only N divisions (once per diagonal) in INV_DIAG_UPDATE,
    #         * instead of O(N^2) divisions in OFFDIAG_UPDATE.
    #      The replaced operations are multiplications, which are much cheaper.

    # 2. Blocking of the reduction dimension k
    #    Apply tiling to k in all reductions (OFFDIAG_DOT and DIAG_DOT) so that
    #    each tile of A[i, k] and A[j, k] fits in L1 cache and is reused efficiently.
    #
    #    Conceptually:
    #      for k in [0, j)   ->   for K in [0, ceil(j / TK)):
    #                               for kk in [K*TK, min((K+1)*TK, j)):
    block(k, kk, TK)

    # 3. Vectorization and unrolling of innermost tiles
    #    The kk-dimension is contiguous in memory (row-major layout), so we vectorize
    #    over kk and unroll slightly to gain instruction-level parallelism.
    vectorize(kk, VEC_K)
    unroll(kk, UNR_K)

    # 4. Parallelization across kk (within a reduction)
    #    Each reduction "sum over k" is purely over reads of A; the only write is
    #    into the private accumulator (dot_ij or diag_correction).
    #    We can parallelize tiles of kk using a reduction (tree sum) without
    #    violating dependencies in i or j.
    parallelize(kk)

    # 5. Keep i and j strictly sequential
    #    Outer dimensions i and j are *not* parallelized or interchanged because:
    #      - off-diagonal A[i, j] uses previously computed entries A[i, k] (k < j)
    #        and the fully computed row j,
    #      - diagonal A[i, i] depends on all off-diagonals in the same row,
    #      - row i depends on all rows < i.
    #    Respecting these dependencies preserves the original left-looking Cholesky
    #    factorization order and numerical behavior.

# Optimized model for cholesky.c (lower‑triangular Cholesky factorization)

domain:
    i: dim in [0, N)         # row index
    j: dim in [0, N)         # column index (only j <= i is used)
    k: dim in [0, N)         # reduction index

data:
    # Dense N x N matrix, row-major. Only the lower triangle (j <= i) is used.
    A[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j

    # Auxiliary 1D array storing 1 / A[i, i] after row i is factored.
    # This removes repeated divisions inside the main kernel.
    inv_diag[i]: aux DATA_TYPE = (i) -> i

parameters:
    N:  int   # matrix dimension
    BI: int   # block size for i-tiling (tunable; e.g., 64)
    VF: int   # SIMD width for vectorization of reductions (e.g., 4 or 8)
    UK: int   # unroll factor for k (multiple of VF; e.g., 4 * VF)

computation:
    # In-place Cholesky factorization of symmetric positive-definite A.
    # On exit, A[i, j] for j <= i contains the lower-triangular factor L
    # such that A_original = L * L^T. The upper triangle is unused.

    for i in seq(0, N):                # 0 <= i < N, must be sequential
        # Off-diagonal entries in row i: L[i, j] for 0 <= j < i.
        # seq(0, i) denotes the half-open interval 0 <= j < i.
        for j in seq(0, i):            # loop-carried deps: j is sequential
            S_off(i, j):
                A[i, j] =
                    ( A[i, j]
                      - sum(k in [0, j),
                            A[i, k] * A[j, k]) )
                    * inv_diag[j]      # multiply by precomputed 1 / A[j, j]

        # Diagonal entry in row i: L[i, i].
        S_diag(i):
            A[i, i] =
                SQRT_FUN(              # matches SQRT_FUN used in the C code
                    A[i, i]
                    - sum(k in [0, i),
                          A[i, k] * A[i, k])
                )

        # Precompute reciprocal of the diagonal for use in later rows.
        S_inv(i):
            inv_diag[i] = 1.0 / A[i, i]

dependencies:
    # 1. Each off-diagonal element L[i, j] depends on:
    #    - the diagonal factor (via its reciprocal) from row j
    #    - all earlier off-diagonals in the same row i
    for i in [0, N), j in [0, i):
        S_inv(j) -> S_off(i, j)        # need inv_diag[j] before using it
    for i in [0, N), j in [0, i), k in [0, j):
        S_off(i, k) -> S_off(i, j)     # A[i, j] uses A[i, k] for k < j

    # 2. The diagonal of row i depends on all off-diagonals in that row.
    for i in [0, N), j in [0, i):
        S_off(i, j) -> S_diag(i)

    # 3. inv_diag[i] depends on the final value of the diagonal A[i, i].
    for i in [0, N):
        S_diag(i) -> S_inv(i)

optimization:
    # Arithmetic optimization:
    # - The auxiliary array inv_diag[i] hoists one division per (i, j) pair
    #   out of the inner loops. Each off-diagonal update now performs a
    #   multiply instead of a divide, which is substantially cheaper on x64.

    # Cache / locality optimization:
    # - Tile the outer i-loop so that the working set of a block of rows
    #   (their off-diagonals and partial diagonals) fits better into cache.
    block(i, I, BI)          # I: tile index over rows, BI: tunable tile size
    hoist(I)                 # place the tile loop as outermost around i

    # Vectorization and ILP:
    # - The k-dimension in both reductions is free of cross-iteration
    #   dependencies except for the scalar reduction variable, so it can be
    #   efficiently SIMD-vectorized and unrolled.
    vectorize(k, VF)         # use SIMD width VF along k
    unroll(k, UK)            # unroll the k-loop by factor UK (multiple of VF)

    # Parallelism:
    # - Due to explicit dependencies between rows (i dimension) and columns
    #   (j dimension), i and j must remain sequential. Parallelism is
    #   therefore exploited only via vectorization of k.
    #   No parallelize(i) or parallelize(j) is legal here.

    # Triangular structure:
    # - Only the lower triangle of A is live. No computation or stores touch
    #   elements with j > i; this is enforced by the bounds j < i in S_off
    #   and by using only A[i, k] with k < i in S_diag.
