    # which has good temporal locality for tiles of A and B.

    # Exploit symmetry of B = A * A^T to cut work almost in half.
    # This is semantics-preserving and bitwise identical because
    #   B[i, j] and B[j, i] are computed as the same sum of the same
    #   products in the same order in the original code.
    #
    # We express this as:
    #   - Restrict gram_B to i <= j (upper triangle including diagonal).
    #   - Add a symmetric fill step for the lower triangle.
    #
    # #symmetric_half_gram:
    #   for i in [0, N), j in [i, N):
    #     B[i, j] = sum(t, A[i, t] * A[j, t])
    #   for i in [0, N), j in [0, i):
    #     B[i, j] = B[j, i]

    parallelize(I_init)         # distribute row-tiles of B across cores
    vectorize(j, VECW)          # vectorize across columns inside a tile


    # ============================================================
    # Optimizations for kernel_lu (in-place LU)
    # ============================================================

    # Keep i as the outermost sequential loop (strong inter-row deps).
    hoist(i)

    # The LU_factor computation already encodes a right-looking form
    # derived from the original two nested loops via legal transforms:
    #
    #  - For the original U-update (second j-loop), we interchange (j, k):
    #       for j = i..N-1
    #         for k = 0..i-1   body(i,j,k)
    #    ->  for k = 0..i-1
    #         for j = i..N-1   body(i,j,k)
    #    This preserves the order of updates for each (i, j) element,
    #    so floating-point results are bitwise identical.
    #
    #  - For the L-update (first j-loop), we similarly transform the
    #    left-looking scheme into an equivalent right-looking one:
    #       for j = 0..i-1:
    #         for k = 0..j-1: A[i,j] -= A[i,k]*A[k,j];
    #         A[i,j] /= A[j,j];
    #    ->
    #       for k = 0..i-1:
    #         A[i,k] /= A[k,k];
    #         for j = k+1..i-1: A[i,j] -= A[i,k]*A[k,j];
    #    Again, the sequence of operations on each A[i,j] is unchanged.

    # Improve locality and vectorization in the trailing update (inner j-loop).
    block(j, J_lu, TJ_lu)       # work on tiles along the row (j dimension)
    hoist(J_lu)

    # For a fixed (i, k), each j-tile J_lu touches a contiguous segment
    # of rows i and k, ideal for cache lines and SIMD.

    # Parallelize across independent j-tiles within each row i.
    # Each tile updates a disjoint interval of row i and only reads
    # shared, read-only data from previous rows, so no synchronization
    # is needed beyond the natural barrier at each i.
    parallelize(J_lu)

    # Vectorize inside j-tiles: the inner loop becomes a SAXPY-like
    # fused multiply-subtract on contiguous memory (A[k, j], A[i, j]).
    vectorize(j, VECW)

    # Unroll k to increase instruction-level parallelism in the chain
    # over previous columns while keeping code size reasonable.
    unroll(k, UNROLL_K)

    # Implicit scalar/temporal hoisting (captured by the loop form):
    #   - A[i, k] is loaded once per (i, k), kept in a scalar register
    #   - A[k, j] is streamed contiguously inside each tile
    #   - A[i, j] is accumulated in registers across k and written back once
--- END OF MODEL: lu-02 ---

--- START OF MODEL: lu-03 ---
domain:
    # Matrix is N x N, 0-based as in the C code
    i:  dim in [0, N)      # row index
    jL: dim in [0, N)      # column index for L-part (j < i)
    jU: dim in [0, N)      # column index for U-part (j >= i)
    k:  dim in [0, N)      # reduction / inner-product index

data:
    # In-place LU factors, stored in a single row-major array:
    #   - strict lower triangle (i > j): L (unit diagonal implied)
    #   - upper triangle (i <= j): U
    A[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j  # row-major layout

parameters:
    N: int                    # problem size
    # Tuning knobs for performance (compile-time or run-time constants):
    TJ: int                   # tile size for jU (columns of trailing submatrix), e.g., 64–256
    TK: int                   # tile size for k in U-part, e.g., 16–64
    TK_L: int                 # tile size for k in L-part, typically smaller than TK
    VJ: int                   # SIMD width used for vectorizing over columns (jU)
    UK: int                   # unroll factor for K in U-part
    UK_L: int                 # unroll factor for K in L-part

computation:
    # For each row i, first compute L(i, j) for j < i, then U(i, j) for j >= i.
    # This matches the original kernel_lu loop nest structurally.

    for i in seq([0, N)):

        # --- L update: strict lower triangle, row i, columns 0 .. i-1 ---
        # A[i, jL] = ( A[i, jL] - sum_{k=0}^{jL-1} A[i, k] * A[k, jL] ) / A[jL, jL]
        # jL must be processed in increasing order because A[i, k] for k < jL
        # are produced by earlier jL iterations.
        L(i, jL):
            for jL in seq([0, i)):
                A[i, jL] =
                    ( A[i, jL]
                      - sum(k in [0, jL): A[i, k] * A[k, jL] )
                    ) / A[jL, jL]

        # --- U update: upper triangle including diagonal, row i, columns i .. N-1 ---
        # A[i, jU] = A[i, jU] - sum_{k=0}^{i-1} A[i, k] * A[k, jU]
        # For fixed i, different jU iterations are independent.
        U(i, jU):
            for jU in [i, N):
                A[i, jU] =
                    A[i, jU]
                    - sum(k in [0, i): A[i, k] * A[k, jU])

dependencies:
    # The row loop i is explicitly sequential (seq), so rows execute in order:
    #   all updates for row i happen before row i+1.
    #
    # Within each row i:
    #   - L(i, jL) is sequential in jL by construction (seq).
    #   - U(i, jU) is independent across jU once all L(i, *) are known.
    #
    # To make this explicit:
    for i in [0, N), jL in [0, i), jU in [i, N):
        L(i, jL) -> U(i, jU)   # complete the L-part of row i before any U-part of row i

optimization:
    # High-level goals:
    #   - Respect all true data dependencies (no pivoting is introduced).
    #   - Keep the lower-triangular (L) jL-loop strictly sequential.
    #   - Turn the U-part into a cache-friendly, vectorized, and parallel update
    #     over the trailing submatrix.

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 1. Reorder the U update to improve reuse (saxpy-like formulation)
    # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
    # U(i, jU) currently computes:
    #   A[i, jU] = A[i, jU] - sum_{k=0}^{i-1} A[i, k] * A[k, jU]
    # which is mathematically a reduction over k. The contributions from
    # different k are associative (up to FP round-off), so we can swap jU and k.
    #
    # Conceptual transformed order for the U-part at fixed i:
    #   for k in [0, i):
    #       let aik = A[i, k]    # hoist to a scalar
    #       for jU in [i, N):
    #           A[i, jU] -= aik * A[k, jU]
    #
    # This:
    #   - keeps A[i, k] (aik) in a register across many jU,
    #   - streams A[k, jU] and A[i, jU] in contiguous row-major order,
    #   - preserves the mathematical result.
    #
    # We express this via an interchange of jU and k in the U reduction.
    # (L's use of k is unchanged.)
    interchange(jU, k)  # applied only where jU and k are both active, effectively in U

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 2. Tiling / blocking of U’s jU and k dimensions
    # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
    # After reordering, U’s effective structure per row i is:
    #   for k in [0, i):
    #     for jU in [i, N):
    #       A[i, jU] -= A[i, k] * A[k, jU]
    #
    # We tile jU and k to form cache-sized blocks over the trailing submatrix.
    # TJ and TK are tunable tile sizes that should be chosen to fit L1/L2.
    block(jU, JU, TJ)   # tile the trailing columns for better spatial locality
    block(k,  K,  TK)   # tile the reduction dimension to improve reuse of A[k, *]

    # Place tile loops just inside i to expose parallelism and maximize reuse
    hoist(JU)
    hoist(K)

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 3. Vectorization and parallelization of U over columns
    # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
    # After tiling, a typical inner kernel for U has shape:
    #   for K in tiles of k:
    #     for JU in tiles of jU:
    #       for k in K:
    #         aik = A[i, k]
    #         for jU in JU:
    #           A[i, jU] -= aik * A[k, jU]
    #
    # The innermost jU loop touches contiguous elements of A[i, jU] and A[k, jU],
    # so it is ideal for SIMD vectorization.
    vectorize(JU, VJ)   # VJ chosen per SIMD width (e.g., 4 or 8 doubles)

    # For fixed i, iterations over tiles JU are independent (no write conflicts),
    # so we can parallelize them across threads. The i loop itself remains
    # strictly sequential to respect the LU dependencies across rows.
    parallelize(JU)

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 4. Micro-optimizations for U’s reduction over k
    # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Within each K tile, unroll the k-loop and keep A[i, k] in registers.
    # This reduces loop overhead and lets the compiler schedule FMAs efficiently.
    unroll(K, UK)

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 5. Local optimizations for the L update (lower triangle)
    # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
    # L(i, jL) has an inner sum:
    #   sum_{k=0}^{jL-1} A[i, k] * A[k, jL]
    # which:
    #   - cannot reorder jL (data dependence along jL),
    #   - *can* tile/unroll k for slightly better cache behavior and ILP.
    #
    # We apply a modest tile of k (TK_L) and unroll that tile. The jL loop
    # itself remains 'seq' and is not parallelized or interchanged.
    block(k,  KL, TK_L)  # within L’s sum only; TK_L kept relatively small
    unroll(KL, UK_L)

    # NOTE:
    # - No additional large buffers are introduced; all updates are in-place on A.
    # - Extra storage, if any, is limited to a few scalars and small tiles
    #   implied by unrolling, well within the 50% memory-usage constraint.
--- END OF MODEL: lu-03 ---

--- START OF MODEL: lu-04 ---
domain:
    # Problem size
    N: size

    # Loop indices following the original kernel
    i: dim in [0, N)      # row index
    j: dim in [0, N)      # column index
    k: dim in [0, N)      # reduction index

    # Auxiliary index used only in dependency specifications
    row: dim in [0, N)

data:
    # A stores both L and U in-place, row-major:
    #  - strictly lower triangle (j < i) holds L(i, j)
    #  - diagonal and upper triangle (j >= i) hold U(i, j)
    A[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j

    # Reciprocal of diagonal pivots 1 / A[j, j]; used to avoid repeated divisions.
    inv_diag[j]: aux DATA_TYPE = (j) -> j   # contiguous 1D array

parameters:
    # Matrix dimension
    N: int

    # Tunable tile sizes for the upper-factor update (row-panel update)
    BK: int  # block size along k (previous rows), e.g., 32
    BJ: int  # block size along j (columns of U), e.g., 64

    # Optional vector width along the j (column) dimension
    VEC_J: int  # e.g., 4 for AVX2 double, 8 for AVX2 float

computation:
    # In-place, no-pivot LU factorization of A.
    # L has unit diagonal; its strictly lower part is stored in A[i, j] for j < i.
    # U is stored in the upper triangle of A, including the diagonal.

    for i in seq(0, N):              # outer loop over rows is strictly sequential

        # ---- 1. Compute strict lower-triangular entries L(i, j), 0 <= j < i ----
        #      L(i, j) = ( A(i, j) - sum_{k=0..j-1} L(i, k) * U(k, j) ) / U(j, j)
        #      We use inv_diag[j] = 1 / U(j, j) to replace division by multiplication.
        for j in seq(0, i):          # j ranges [0, i)
            L_update:
            A[i, j] =
                ( A[i, j]
                  - sum(k in [0, j): A[i, k] * A[k, j] )
                ) * inv_diag[j]

        # ---- 2. Compute upper-triangular row U(i, j), i <= j < N ----
        #      U(i, j) = A(i, j) - sum_{k=0..i-1} L(i, k) * U(k, j)
        for j in [i, N):
            U_update:
            A[i, j] =
                A[i, j]
                - sum(k in [0, i): A[i, k] * A[k, j])

        # ---- 3. Cache reciprocal of the new pivot for use in later rows ----
        # inv_diag[i] is used in L_update(row, j = i) for all row > i.
        DIAG_RECIP:
        inv_diag[i] = 1.0 / A[i, i]


dependencies:
    # 1. Within a given row i, lower-factor entries L(i, j) must be computed
    #    from left to right because L(i, j) depends on all L(i, k) with k < j.
    for i in [0, N), j in [0, i-1]:
        L_update(i, j) -> L_update(i, j + 1)

    # 2. Upper-factor entries U(i, j) on row i depend on the complete set of
    #    L(i, 0..i-1) multipliers of the same row.
    for i in [0, N), j in [i, N), k in [0, i):
        L_update(i, k) -> U_update(i, j)

    # 3. The cached reciprocal inv_diag[i] depends on the pivot U(i, i)
    #    and must be available before it is used in lower rows.
    for i in [0, N):
        U_update(i, i) -> DIAG_RECIP(i)
    for i in [0, N), row in (i, N):
        DIAG_RECIP(i) -> L_update(row, i)

    # Note: The outer i loop remains globally ordered (0, 1, 2, ...), preserving
    #       standard Doolittle LU dependencies across rows.


optimization:
    # ============================================================
    # Global structure
    # ============================================================
    # The i-loop carries true dependences and must remain sequential.
    hoist(i)

    # (Optional) Row blocking: preserves row order but can help cache behavior
    # when combined with other blocking. TI is fixed at compile-time or chosen
    # empirically; it does not change semantics.
    block(i, I, 32)   # I is row-block index; process rows in blocks of 32

    # ============================================================
    # Optimizations for reductions over k (both L_update and U_update)
    # ============================================================
    # The inner sums over k are reductions; we can safely unroll and vectorize
    # them using a private accumulator in registers.
    unroll(k, 4)
    vectorize(k, 4)   # implement as tree-reduction in SIMD registers

    # ============================================================
    # Optimizations specific to U_update (j >= i)
    # ============================================================
    # For fixed i, U_update has the form:
    #   A[i, j] -= sum_{k < i} A[i, k] * A[k, j]
    # Different j in [i, N) are independent for fixed i.

    # 1. 2D blocking in (k, j) to improve locality:
    #    - A[i, k] (the multipliers of row i) are reused for all j,
    #      so tiling over k lets us keep a subset of them hot in L1/L2.
    #    - A[k, j] is stored row-major, so blocking j makes accesses to
    #      A[k, j] contiguous.
    block(k, K, BK)         # BK tuned for L1/L2 (e.g., 32)
    block(j, J, BJ)         # BJ tuned for L1/L2/L3 (e.g., 64)
    interchange(K, J)       # iterate over k-tiles outer, j-tiles inner

    # Conceptually, for each fixed i, this gives:
    #   for K in tiles of k in [0, i):
    #     for J in tiles of j in [i, N):
    #       for k in K:
    #         for j in J:
    #           A[i, j] -= A[i, k] * A[k, j]

    # 2. Parallelism across j (columns of U):
    #    Within a fixed row i and fixed K-tile, updates to different columns are
    #    independent. We therefore parallelize over J (column tiles).
    parallelize(J)          # distribute column tiles J across threads

    # 3. SIMD along the j dimension:
    #    Within each J-tile, j is the fastest-varying index in row-major A,
    #    so SIMD over j achieves contiguous loads/stores.
    vectorize(j, VEC_J)

    # 4. Residual unrolling on the k loop inside each (K, J) tile for better
    #    instruction-level parallelism and FMA utilization (if available).
    unroll(k, 4)

    # ============================================================
    # Optimization for DIAG_RECIP
    # ============================================================
    # DIAG_RECIP is already hoisted outside the inner loops and computed once
    # per row. This replaces O(N^2) divisions in L_update by cheaper
    # multiplications with inv_diag[j], while adding only an O(N)-sized
    # temporary (inv_diag) well within the allowed memory overhead.
--- END OF MODEL: lu-04 ---

--- START OF MODEL: lu-05 ---
domain:
    # Global iteration space (upper bounds are compile-time constant N)
    i: dim in [0, N)
    j: dim in [0, N)
    k: dim in [0, N)

data:
    # Single dense matrix, stored row-major, updated in-place.
    # On input: arbitrary SPD matrix A.
    # On output: in-place LU factorization without pivoting:
    #   - L has unit diagonal and is stored in the strict lower triangle of A.
    #   - U is stored in the diagonal and upper triangle of A.
    A[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j  # row-major

parameters:
    # Problem size (matches PolyBench's N and _PB_N)
    N: int

    # Tuning parameters for performance (not affecting correctness)
    TJ: int  # tile size for column dimension in upper update, e.g., 64
    UK: int  # unroll factor for inner products over k, e.g., 4
    VLEN: int  # SIMD width (number of DATA_TYPE lanes), e.g., 4 or 8

computation:
    # In-place LU factorization without pivoting.
    # This is a Doolittle-like algorithm:
    #   For each row i:
    #     1) Compute L[i, 0..i-1] (strict lower part of row i).
    #     2) Compute U[i, i..N-1] (diagonal and upper part of row i).
    #
    # The original C code:
    #   for (i)
    #     for (j < i) { for (k < j) A[i][j] -= A[i][k]*A[k][j]; A[i][j] /= A[j][j]; }
    #     for (j >= i) for (k < i) A[i][j] -= A[i][k]*A[k][j];

    for i in seq([0, N)):                # outer loop must be sequential (row-to-row dependence)

        # 1) Compute strict lower part of row i: L(i, j) for j < i.
        #    Each A[i, j] is updated as:
        #       A[i, j] = (A[i, j] - sum_{k=0}^{j-1} A[i, k] * A[k, j]) / A[j, j]
        #    Note that A[i, k] for k < j are entries of L in row i, so j must be
        #    processed in increasing order (loop-carried dependence on row i).
        for j in seq([0, i)):
            A[i, j] =
                ( A[i, j]
                  - sum(k in [0, j), A[i, k] * A[k, j]) )
                / A[j, j]

        # 2) Compute diagonal and upper part of row i: U(i, j) for j >= i.
        #    Each A[i, j] is updated as:
        #       A[i, j] = A[i, j] - sum_{k=0}^{i-1} A[i, k] * A[k, j]
        #    All A[i, k] with k < i are now fixed (L row i is complete), and all
        #    A[k, j] with k < i, j >= i are from previously computed rows.
        #    Therefore, for fixed i:
        #      - different columns j in [i, N) are independent,
        #      - the sum over k is a pure reduction for each (i, j).
        for j in [i, N):
            A[i, j] =
                A[i, j]
                - sum(k in [0, i), A[i, k] * A[k, j])

dependencies:
    # Row dependencies:
    #   All computations at row i depend on rows 0..i-1.
    #   This enforces that i must be executed sequentially.
    for i in [1, N), j in [0, N):
        (all computations producing A[i-1, *]) -> (all computations using A[0..i-1, j] at row i)

    # Within-row, lower-part (L) dependencies:
    #   For fixed i, L(i, j) depends on previously computed entries in the same row i.
    for i in [0, N), j in [1, i), k in [0, j):
        A[i, k] -> A[i, j]   # j-loop in the lower update must be sequential

    # Within-row, upper-part (U) dependencies:
    #   For fixed i, U(i, j) for different j in [i, N) are independent:
    #     - They only share read-only data A[i, 0..i-1] and A[0..i-1, *].
    #     - No write-after-write or read-after-write between (i, j1) and (i, j2).
    for i in [0, N), j1 in [i, N), j2 in [i, N), j1 != j2:
        # No dependence between (i, j1) and (i, j2); they form a parallel set.
        (A[i, j1] update) --||-- (A[i, j2] update)

optimization:
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # High-level remarks:
    #   - The i-loop is inherently sequential because row i uses rows < i.
    #   - The lower-triangular loop over j (j < i) is also sequential because
    #     L(i, j) uses previously computed L(i, k) with k < j.
    #   - The upper-triangular loop (j >= i) has no loop-carried dependencies
    #     in j and is the dominant cost (~O(N^3/2) FLOPs). We exploit this
    #     for parallelism and vectorization.
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------

    # 1. Improve data locality and expose parallelism in the upper (U) update.
    #
    # We tile the j-dimension only for the upper-part update, then parallelize
    # tiles. This maintains the original evaluation order for the reduction over k
    # (we do not interchange j and k), therefore preserving C’s semantics for
    # each dot product A[i, j] −= sum_k A[i, k]*A[k, j].

    # block(j, JU, TJ) conceptually transforms:
    #   for j in [i, N):
    #       ...
    # into:
    #   for JU in [i, N) step TJ:
    #       for j in [JU, min(JU+TJ, N)):
    #           ...
    #
    # It is applied only to the "upper" j-loop.
    block(j /* in upper update */, JU, TJ)

    # Move the tile loop JU directly under i to make the parallel work chunks
    # coarser-grained and cache-friendly.
    hoist(JU)

    # Parallelize tiles of columns in the upper update.
    # For a given row i:
    #   - Different JU tiles cover disjoint column ranges.
    #   - There are no dependencies between tiles.
    #   - Each thread processes several adjacent columns, improving spatial locality.
    parallelize(JU)

    # Within a tile, encourage SIMD vectorization in the column dimension j.
    # This lets the compiler apply vector loads/stores for A[i, j] and A[k, j]
    # across nearby columns, even though the inner reduction is over k.
    vectorize(j, VLEN)

    # 2. Make inner products over k efficient in both L and U updates.
    #
    # The reductions over k in:
    #   sum(k in [0, j), ...)   and   sum(k in [0, i), ...)
    # are short-to-moderate-length dot products along the k-dimension.
    # We unroll and vectorize k to extract ILP and exploit SIMD where possible.
    #
    # Note: accesses A[i, k] are contiguous within a row; A[k, j] is strided by N.
    # Unrolling helps hide the latency of these strided loads.

    # Apply to both lower and upper k-reductions:
    unroll(k, UK)
    vectorize(k, VLEN)

    # 3. (Optional) Mild i-blocking for better cache behavior.
    #
    # This does *not* introduce parallelism (i-blocks must still execute in order)
    # but can reduce working-set size for large N by grouping nearby rows.
    # The transformation is:
    #   for i in [0, N):
    # into:
    #   for I in [0, N) step TI:
    #     for i in [I, min(I+TI, N)):
    #       ...
    #
    # TI is chosen so that the active part of rows 0..i and columns around i
    # fit better in caches on the target machine.
    # This is semantics-preserving because the internal order of i is unchanged.
    #
    # If desired, enable with a suitable TI (not shown as a parameter above):
    #   block(i, I, TI)
    #   hoist(I)

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Memory-usage considerations:
    #   - No additional O(N^2) data structures are introduced; A remains the
    #     only N×N array.
    #   - Extra storage is limited to scalar temporaries and small vector
    #     registers (implied by sum/unroll/vectorize), keeping additional
    #     memory well below the allowed +50% over the original footprint.
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
--- END OF MODEL: lu-05 ---

/* Array initialization. */
static
void init_array (int n,
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(A,N,N,n,n),
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(b,N,n),
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(x,N,n),
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(y,N,n))
{
  int i, j;
  DATA_TYPE fn = (DATA_TYPE)n;

  for (i = 0; i < n; i++)
    {
      x[i] = 0;
      y[i] = 0;
      b[i] = (i+1)/fn/2.0 + 4;
    }

  for (i = 0; i < n; i++)
    {
      for (j = 0; j <= i; j++)
	A[i][j] = (DATA_TYPE)(-j % n) / n + 1;
      for (j = i+1; j < n; j++) {
	A[i][j] = 0;
      }
      A[i][i] = 1;
    }

  /* Make the matrix positive semi-definite. */
  /* not necessary for LU, but using same code as cholesky */
  int r,s,t;
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(B, DATA_TYPE, N, N, n, n);
  for (r = 0; r < n; ++r)
    for (s = 0; s < n; ++s)
      (POLYBENCH_ARRAY(B))[r][s] = 0;
  for (t = 0; t < n; ++t)
    for (r = 0; r < n; ++r)
      for (s = 0; s < n; ++s)
	(POLYBENCH_ARRAY(B))[r][s] += A[r][t] * A[s][t];
    for (r = 0; r < n; ++r)
      for (s = 0; s < n; ++s)
	A[r][s] = (POLYBENCH_ARRAY(B))[r][s];
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(B);

}


/* DCE code. Must scan the entire live-out data.
   Can be used also to check the correctness of the output. */
static
void print_array(int n,
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(x,N,n))

{
  int i;

  POLYBENCH_DUMP_START;
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_BEGIN("x");
  for (i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    if (i % 20 == 0) fprintf (POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, "\n");
    fprintf (POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, DATA_PRINTF_MODIFIER, x[i]);
  }
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_END("x");
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_FINISH;
}


/* Main computational kernel. The whole function will be timed,
   including the call and return. */
static
void kernel_ludcmp[[gnu::flatten, gnu::noinline]](int n,
		   DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(A,N,N,n,n),
		   DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(b,N,n),
		   DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(x,N,n),
		   DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(y,N,n))
{
  int i, j, k;

  DATA_TYPE w;

#pragma scop
  for (i = 0; i < _PB_N; i++) {
    for (j = 0; j <i; j++) {
       w = A[i][j];
       for (k = 0; k < j; k++) {
          w -= A[i][k] * A[k][j];
       }
        A[i][j] = w / A[j][j];
    }
   for (j = i; j < _PB_N; j++) {
       w = A[i][j];
       for (k = 0; k < i; k++) {
          w -= A[i][k] * A[k][j];
       }
       A[i][j] = w;
    }
  }

  for (i = 0; i < _PB_N; i++) {
     w = b[i];
     for (j = 0; j < i; j++)
        w -= A[i][j] * y[j];
     y[i] = w;
  }

   for (i = _PB_N-1; i >=0; i--) {
     w = y[i];
     for (j = i+1; j < _PB_N; j++)
        w -= A[i][j] * x[j];
     x[i] = w / A[i][i];
  }
#pragma endscop

}


int main(int argc, char** argv)
{
  /* Retrieve problem size. */
  int n = N;

  /* Variable declaration/allocation. */
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(A, DATA_TYPE, N, N, n, n);
  POLYBENCH_1D_ARRAY_DECL(b, DATA_TYPE, N, n);
  POLYBENCH_1D_ARRAY_DECL(x, DATA_TYPE, N, n);
  POLYBENCH_1D_ARRAY_DECL(y, DATA_TYPE, N, n);


  /* Initialize array(s). */
  init_array (n,
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A),
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(b),
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(x),
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(y));

  /* Start timer. */
  polybench_start_instruments;

  /* Run kernel. */
  kernel_ludcmp (n,
		 POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A),
		 POLYBENCH_ARRAY(b),
		 POLYBENCH_ARRAY(x),
		 POLYBENCH_ARRAY(y));

  /* Stop and print timer. */
  polybench_stop_instruments;
  polybench_print_instruments;

  /* Prevent dead-code elimination. All live-out data must be printed
     by the function call in argument. */
  polybench_prevent_dce(print_array(n, POLYBENCH_ARRAY(x)));

  /* Be clean. */
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(A);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(b);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(x);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(y);

  return 0;
}

    i: dim in [0, N)        # row index
    j: dim in [0, N)        # column index

data:
    # In-place LU factors:
    #   - On and above diagonal (i <= j): U(i,j)
    #   - Below diagonal (i > j):        L(i,j)
    #   with implicit L(i,i) = 1
    A[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j  # row-major

    x[i]: out DATA_TYPE = i          # solution of A * x = b
    y[i]: out DATA_TYPE = i          # temporary for forward substitution

parameters:
    N: int                      # problem size

    # Tuning knobs (no change in mathematical result)
    TJ:   int                   # tile size for j (columns) in LU
    TK:   int                   # tile size for k (inner products) in LU
    TJ_f: int                   # tile size for j in forward substitution
    TJ_b: int                   # tile size for j in backward substitution
    VEC_J: int                  # vector width for j-dimension
    VEC_K: int                  # vector width for k-dimension
    UK:    int                  # unroll factor for k-reductions

computation:
    # In-place LU factorization without pivoting.
    # This matches the original nested i–j–k structure exactly:
    #   for i = 0..N-1:
    #     (1) compute L(i,0..i-1)
    #     (2) compute U(i,i..N-1)

    for i in seq([0, N)):
        L_factor:                         # compute strict lower part of row i
            for j in seq([0, i)):         # 0 <= j < i
                # A[i, j] := L(i,j)
                A[i, j] =
                    ( A[i, j]
                      - sum(k in seq([0, j)), A[i, k] * A[k, j]) )
                    / A[j, j]

        U_factor:                         # compute upper part of row i
            for j in seq([i, N)):         # i <= j < N
                # A[i, j] := U(i,j)
                A[i, j] =
                    A[i, j]
                    - sum(k in seq([0, i)), A[i, k] * A[k, j])

    # Forward substitution: solve L * y = b.
    # L has unit diagonal; lower part stored in A(i,j) for j < i.
    Forward:
        for i in seq([0, N)):
            y[i] =
                b[i]
                - sum(j in seq([0, i)), A[i, j] * y[j])

    # Backward substitution: solve U * x = y.
    # U is upper-triangular, stored in A(i,j) for j >= i.
    Backward:
        # descending loop: i = N-1, N-2, ..., 0
        for i in seq([0, N)) reversed:
            x[i] =
                ( y[i]
                  - sum(j in seq([i+1, N)), A[i, j] * x[j]) )
                / A[i, i]

dependencies:
    # 1. LU factorization (panel-wise, row i depends on rows 0..i-1)

    # L(i,j) depends on previous entries in the same row (L(i,0..j-1))
    # and on U(k,j) in rows k < j < i.
    for i in [0, N), j in [1, i):                   # j >= 1
        for k in [0, j):
            L_factor(i, k) -> L_factor(i, j)        # A[i,k] used in sum
            U_factor(k, j) -> L_factor(i, j)        # A[k,j] used in sum

    # U(i,j) depends on the entire L(i,0..i-1) and on U(0..i-1, j).
    for i in [0, N), j in [i, N):

            U_factor(k, j) -> U_factor(i, j)        # A[k,j] used in sum

    # -----------------------------------------------------------------
    # High-level notes:
    #  - Outer loop i must remain sequential for LU and both solves
    #    because each row i depends on all rows < i (and, for x,
    #    on rows > i).
    #  - Inner products (sums over k or j) are true reductions and
    #    are good targets for unrolling, vectorization and partial
    #    blocking.
    #  - For a single right-hand side, parallelism is available
    #    inside the U update (j >= i) but not in the L update (j < i).
    # -----------------------------------------------------------------

    # Keep i as the outermost loop for all phases (LU, forward, backward).
    hoist(i)

    # ---------------- LU factorization ----------------
    # Cache blocking for j and k in both L_factor and U_factor.
    # Tiles are processed in increasing index order to preserve all
    # loop-carried dependencies in the triangular L-part.
    #
    # For each fixed i:
    #   - L_factor: 0 <= j < i, 0 <= k < j
    #   - U_factor: i <= j < N, 0 <= k < i

    # Block j and k to keep active rows and columns of A in L1/L2.
    block(j, J, TJ)     # j = J..min(J+TJ, bound_of_j)
    block(k, K, TK)     # k = K..min(K+TK, bound_of_k)

    # This preserves the dependence of L(i,j) on L(i,0..j-1).

    # For U_factor at a given i, updates of U(i,j) for j >= i are

    #     for J in tiles of [i, N):
    #       parallel over J:

    # i must remain sequential (triangular dependency on y[0..i-1]).
    # The inner sum over j is a reduction; we can:

    #   - vectorize j within each row,
    #   - optionally implement the reduction with a small SIMD micro-kernel.
    block(j, J_f, TJ_f)       # tile j in Forward

    # i must remain sequential in descending order (triangular dependency
    # on x[i+1..N-1]). The inner sum over j is again a reduction.
    block(j, J_b, TJ_b)       # tile j in Backward
    vectorize(j, VEC_J)

domain:
    i: dim in [0, N)
    j: dim in [0, N)
    k: dim in [0, N)

data:
    # A is stored row-major and overwritten in-place with LU factors:
    #   - L has unit diagonal, stored in the strict lower triangle of A
    #   - U is stored in the upper triangle of A (including the diagonal)
    A[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j

    # Right-hand side and solution vectors
    b[i]: in DATA_TYPE    = i -> i
    y[i]: inout DATA_TYPE = i -> i  # forward-substitution result (Ly = b)
    x[i]: out DATA_TYPE   = i -> i  # final solution (Ux = y)

    # Optional temporary buffer used only by an optimization that precomputes
    # 1 / A[i, i] to replace divisions by multiplications.
    # Size N << N^2, so extra memory is well below +50% of the original footprint.
    diag_inv[i]: inout DATA_TYPE = i -> i  # holds 1 / A[i, i] when enabled

parameters:
    N:  int   # matrix and vector dimension
    TI: int   # tile size for i (row blocking)
    TJ: int   # tile size for j (column blocking)
    TK: int   # tile size for k (reduction blocking)
    VJ: int   # SIMD width for vectorization along j
    UK: int   # unrolling factor for reductions over k

computation:
    # In-place LU factorization without pivoting.
    # On entry:  A contains the original dense matrix.
    # On exit:   A encodes L and U such that A_orig = L * U,
    #            with L unit-diagonal lower-triangular and U upper-triangular.
    LU_factor:
        for i in seq([0, N)):
            # Compute strict lower-triangular entries L[i, 0..i-1].
            L_row:
                for j in seq([0, i)):
                    A[i, j] =
                        ( A[i, j]
                          - sum(k in [0, j)) A[i, k] * A[k, j] )
                        / A[j, j]

            # Compute upper-triangular entries U[i, i..N-1].
            U_row:
                for j in [i, N):
                    A[i, j] =
                        A[i, j]
                        - sum(k in [0, i)) A[i, k] * A[k, j]

    # Forward substitution: solve L y = b.
    Forward_substitution:
        for i in seq([0, N)):
            y[i] =
                b[i]
                - sum(j in [0, i)) A[i, j] * y[j]

    # Backward substitution: solve U x = y.
    # Implemented as a forward sweep in the reversed index r = N-1-i
    # so that the loop variable still increases while respecting dependencies.
    Backward_substitution:
        for i in seq([0, N)):
            x[N - 1 - i] =
                ( y[N - 1 - i]
                  - sum(j in (N - 1 - i + 1, N))
                        A[N - 1 - i, j] * x[j] )
                / A[N - 1 - i, N - 1 - i]

optimization:
    # -----------------------------
    # 1. Cache blocking / tiling
    # -----------------------------
    # Tile all three logical dimensions involved in the cubic work of LU.
    # The transformation preserves the original lexicographic order of (i, j, k)
    # within each tile, so numerical semantics (up to FP rounding) are unchanged.
    block(i, Ii, TI)   # outer tiles over rows i
    block(j, Jj, TJ)   # outer tiles over columns j
    block(k, Kk, TK)   # outer tiles over reduction dimension k
    hoist(Ii)          # process panels of rows as the outermost loop

    # -----------------------------
    # 2. Improve U-row locality via loop interchange
    # -----------------------------
    # For the upper-triangular update (U_row), interchange loops over j and k:
    #
    #   Original (for fixed i):
    #       for j in [i, N):
    #           A[i, j] -= sum(k in [0, i)) A[i, k] * A[k, j]
    #
    #   After interchange:
    #       for k in [0, i):
    #           L_ik = A[i, k]
    #           for j in [i, N):
    #               A[i, j] -= L_ik * A[k, j]
    #
    # This turns U_row into a sequence of rank-1 updates
    #   A[i, i:N) -= L[i, k] * U[k, i:N)
    # over contiguous memory in j (row-major layout), greatly improving
    # cache locality and allowing efficient SIMD across j.
    interchange(U_row.k, U_row.j)

    # -----------------------------
    # 3. Vectorization and unrolling
    # -----------------------------
    # Vectorize along the contiguous j-dimension wherever possible:
    #  - inner j-loops of U_row after the interchange
    #  - j-dimension in the sums of the triangular solves (where legal)
    vectorize(j, VJ)

    # Unroll inner reductions over k to increase instruction-level parallelism
    # in both LU_factor and the triangular solves.
    unroll(k, UK)

    # -----------------------------
    # 4. Parallelization
    # -----------------------------
    # The outer i-loops in LU_factor and the triangular solves are inherently
    # sequential (each row depends on all previous ones), so we keep i
    # sequential and only parallelize where there is no loop-carried dependence.
    #
    # In U_row, for fixed (i, k) after the interchange, each j-iteration:
    #     A[i, j] -= A[i, k] * A[k, j]
    # is independent of other j-iterations, so j (or its tiled version Jj)
    # can be safely parallelized.
    parallelize(U_row.j)

    # -----------------------------
    # 5. Division elimination via diagonal reciprocals (optional)
    # -----------------------------
    # Custom optimization: precompute reciprocals of the diagonal entries
    # to replace expensive divisions with multiplications.
    #
    #   for i in seq([0, N)):
    #       # After U_row has finalized A[i, i], cache its reciprocal:
    #       diag_inv[i] = 1 / A[i, i]
    #
    # Then rewrite:
    #   - In L_row:
    #       A[i, j] = ( ... ) / A[j, j]
    #     as:
    #       A[i, j] = ( ... ) * diag_inv[j]
    #
    #   - In Backward_substitution:
    #       x[N-1-i] = w / A[N-1-i, N-1-i]
    #     as:
    #       x[N-1-i] = w * diag_inv[N-1-i]
    #
    # This introduces one extra DATA_TYPE[N] buffer (diag_inv), which is
    # negligible compared to the N^2 matrix (well under +50% memory),
    # and removes O(N^3) scalar divisions, replacing them with multiplications.
    # In real arithmetic the result is identical; in floating point only the
    # rounding order changes slightly.
    precompute_diagonal_inverses(A, diag_inv)

domain:
    i:  dim in [0, N)
    j:  dim in [0, N)
    k:  dim in [0, N)

data:
    # A initially holds the symmetric positive semi-definite matrix.
    # After kernel_ludcmp, A stores L (strict lower triangle, unit diagonal)
    # and U (upper triangle including diagonal) in-place.
    A[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j      # Row-major

    # Right-hand side and solution vectors
    b[i]:    in    DATA_TYPE = i -> i                   # Row-major 1D
    x[i]:    out   DATA_TYPE = i -> i
    y[i]:    inout DATA_TYPE = i -> i

    # Extra temporary: reciprocal of the diagonal of U.
    # Used to replace O(N^2) divisions by O(N) divisions + O(N^2) multiplies.
    invD[i]: temp  DATA_TYPE = i -> i

parameters:
    N:  int      # Problem size, matches runtime n and _PB_N
    TI: int      # Tile size for i (rows) in factorization
    TJ: int      # Tile size for j (columns) in factorization
    TK: int      # Tile size for k (reduction dimension)
    UK: int      # Unroll factor for k
    VK: int      # Vector width (SIMD) for k / j reductions

computation:
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # 1. LU factorization without pivoting (in-place in A)
    #    L has unit diagonal; L(i, j) for j < i is stored in A[i, j]
    #    U(i, j) for j >= i is stored in A[i, j]
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    for i in seq([0, N)):
        # Compute row i of L in the strict lower triangle: j < i
        for j in seq([0, i)):
            L_FACT[i, j]:
                A[i, j] =
                    ( A[i, j]
                      - sum(k in seq([0, j)),
                            A[i, k] * A[k, j]) )
                    * invD[j]     # invD[j] = 1 / A[j, j]

        # Compute row i of U in the upper triangle including the diagonal: j >= i
        for j in [i, N):
            U_FACT[i, j]:
                A[i, j] =
                    A[i, j]
                    - sum(k in seq([0, i)),
                          A[i, k] * A[k, j])

        # Precompute the reciprocal of the diagonal U(i, i) for later use
        DIAG_INV[i]:
            invD[i] = 1.0 / A[i, i]

    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # 2. Forward substitution: solve L * y = b
    #    L has unit diagonal, stored in the strict lower triangle of A.
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    for i in seq([0, N)):
        FWD[i]:
            y[i] =
                b[i]
                - sum(j in seq([0, i)),
                      A[i, j] * y[j])

    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # 3. Backward substitution: solve U * x = y
    #    U is stored in the upper triangle of A including the diagonal.
    #    We use invD[i] instead of dividing by A[i, i].
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    for i in seq([N-1, -1]):   # i = N-1, N-2, ..., 0
        BWD[i]:
            x[i] =
                ( y[i]
                  - sum(j in seq([i+1, N)),
                        A[i, j] * x[j]) )
                * invD[i]      # multiply by 1 / A[i, i] instead of divide

dependencies:
    # Factorization is fundamentally sequential in i: row i depends on all rows < i.

    # Each L_FACT(i2, j) and U_FACT(i2, j) for i2 > i1 need completed row i1
    # (both U row i1 and its diagonal reciprocal).
    for i1 in [0, N), i2 in [i1+1, N):
        DIAG_INV[i1] -> L_FACT[i2, j]   # access A[*, j] from row i1
        DIAG_INV[i1] -> U_FACT[i2, j]   # access A[*, j] from row i1

    # For a fixed row i, the L update (j < i) must complete before any U update.
    for i in [0, N):
        for jU in [i, N):
            L_FACT[i, jL] -> U_FACT[i, jU]    # jL ranges over [0, i)

    # invD[i] must be ready before any later use of 1 / A[i, i]
    for i in [0, N):
        DIAG_INV[i] -> L_FACT[i2, j]   where i2 in [i+1, N) and j in [0, i2)
        DIAG_INV[i] -> BWD[i]          # x[i] uses invD[i]

    # Forward substitution Ly = b is strictly sequential in i (y[i] depends on y[0..i-1]).
    for i in [1, N):
        FWD[i-1] -> FWD[i]

    # Forward substitution starts only after LU is available.
    for i in [0, N):
        DIAG_INV[j] -> FWD[i]  # for all j in [0, i], conservatively

    # Backward substitution Ux = y starts after forward substitution completes.
    for i in [0, N):
        FWD[i] -> BWD[i]

    # Backward substitution is strictly sequential in i in reverse direction:
    # x[i] depends on x[j] for all j > i.
    for i in [0, N-1), j in [i+1, N):
        BWD[j] -> BWD[i]

optimization:
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # Loop tiling for the O(N^3) LU factorization
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # Tile i, j, k to operate on submatrices that fit better in cache.
    # Tiling preserves the increasing order in i to respect factorization
    # dependencies across rows.
    block(i, Ii, TI)       # i = Ii * TI + ii
    block(j, J, TJ)        # j = J  * TJ + jj
    block(k, K, TK)        # k = K  * TK + kk
    hoist(Ii)              # outermost tile loop over row blocks
    hoist(J)               # next tile loop over column blocks

    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # Parallelization
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # Within each fixed row i, the U update loop over j in [i, N) has
    # no loop-carried dependencies (each iteration reads shared A[i, k],
    # A[k, j] and writes a distinct A[i, j]), so it can be parallelized.
    # L update (j < i) is left sequential because it carries dependencies
    # along j through A[i, k].
    parallelize(j)         # applied only to U_FACT[i, j] (j in [i, N))

    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # SIMD and unrolling
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # The k-dimension reductions in L_FACT and U_FACT are the innermost
    # arithmetic hot spots. Unroll and vectorize along k to increase ILP
    # and utilize SIMD FMA units.
    unroll(k, UK)          # unroll k in both L_FACT and U_FACT sums
    vectorize(k, VK)       # vector reduction over k (A[i, k] contiguous)

    # The inner sums in forward/backward substitution can likewise be
    # vectorized; they are short but still benefit from SIMD.
    vectorize(j, VK)       # vectorize inner sums in FWD and BWD where legal

    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # Arithmetic optimization
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # Using invD[i] replaces O(N^2) scalar divisions (in both L_FACT and BWD)
    # with O(N^2) multiplications and only O(N) divisions to form invD[i],
    # which is significantly cheaper on modern CPUs.

domain:
    # Global matrix / vector dimensions (square system of size N)
    i: dim in [0, N)
    j: dim in [0, N)
    k: dim in [0, N)

data:
    # A stores the LU factorization in-place (Doolittle, no pivoting).
    #   L: unit diagonal, strict lower part in A[i,j] for i>j
    #   U: upper part (including diagonal) in A[i,j] for i<=j
    A[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j  # row-major

    # Right-hand side b, solution x, intermediate y
    b[i]: in DATA_TYPE  = i
    x[i]: out DATA_TYPE = i
    y[i]: temp DATA_TYPE = i

    # New: reciprocal of diagonal of U, D[i] = 1 / U[i,i]
    # Used to replace repeated divisions by cheaper multiplications.
    D[i]: temp DATA_TYPE = i

    # Optional logical views (no extra storage; for reasoning only)
    #L[i, j]: view DATA_TYPE = (i, j) ->
    #    if i > j then A[i, j]
    #    else if i == j then 1
    #    else 0
    #U[i, j]: view DATA_TYPE = (i, j) ->
    #    if i <= j then A[i, j]
    #    else 0

parameters:
    N: int  # problem size

    # Tunable optimization parameters (chosen based on cache/SIMD/hardware)
    TJ_U: int      # tile size along j for U-row updates and back substitution
    TJ_TRSV: int   # tile size along j for forward/backward triangular solves
    VEC_WIDTH: int # SIMD width for vectorization along contiguous j

computation:
    #--------------------------------------------------------------
    # 1. In-place LU factorization without pivoting (A -> L and U),
    #    with reciprocals of diagonal elements stored in D.
    #    This models kernel_ludcmp's first loop nest.
    #--------------------------------------------------------------
    FACT_LU:
      for i in seq[0, N):                    # rows must be processed in order
        #------------------------------------
        # 1.a. Compute L(i, 0..i-1): strict lower part of row i
        #      L(i,j) = (A(i,j) - Σ_{k < j} L(i,k) * U(k,j)) / U(j,j)
        #      Division by U(j,j) replaced by multiplication with D[j].
        #------------------------------------
        FACT_L_ROW[i]:
          for j in seq[0, i):                # j sequential: depends on A[i,0..j-1]
            A[i, j] =
              ( A[i, j]
                - sum(k in [0, j), A[i, k] * A[k, j])  # A[i,k]=L(i,k), A[k,j]=U(k,j)
              ) * D[j]                        # D[j] = 1 / A[j, j] (U(j,j))

        #------------------------------------
        # 1.b. Compute U(i, i..N-1): upper part of row i
        #
        # Original code:
        #   for (j = i; j < N; ++j) {
        #     w = A[i][j];
        #     for (k = 0; k < i; ++k)
        #       w -= A[i][k] * A[k][j];
        #     A[i][j] = w;
        #   }
        #
        # We interchange k and j to expose a rank-1 update structure:
        #   for k in [0, i):
        #     for j in [i, N):
        #       A[i,j] -= A[i,k] * A[k,j];
        #
        # For each fixed (i,j), the sequence of products over k is the same
        # (k increases from 0 to i-1), so even floating-point rounding is
        # preserved. This makes j the innermost loop with contiguous
        # accesses (row-major A), enabling vectorization and j-tiling.
        #------------------------------------
        U_ROW_UPDATE[i]:
          for k in seq[0, i):                # accumulation over previous rows
            for j in [i, N):                 # j has no loop-carried deps
              A[i, j] = A[i, j] - A[i, k] * A[k, j]

        #------------------------------------
        # 1.c. Diagonal of U is now A[i,i]. Store its reciprocal in D[i]
        #      for later reuse (in L formation for later rows and in
        #      backward substitution).
        #------------------------------------
        DIAG_RECIP[i]:
          D[i] = 1 / A[i, i]

    #--------------------------------------------------------------
    # 2. Forward substitution: solve L * y = b
    #    (unit-diagonal lower triangular system with L in A).
    #    Models kernel_ludcmp's second loop nest.
    #    y is internal: not printed, but used in step 3.
    #--------------------------------------------------------------
    FWD_SUB:
      for i in seq[0, N):                    # strictly sequential (depends on y[0..i-1])
        FWD[i]:
          y[i] = b[i] - sum(j in [0, i), A[i, j] * y[j]

    #--------------------------------------------------------------
    # 3. Backward substitution: solve U * x = y
    #    (upper triangular system with U in A).
    #    Division by diagonal replaced with multiplication by D[i].
    #    Models kernel_ludcmp's final loop nest.
    #--------------------------------------------------------------
    BWD_SUB:
      for i in seq(N-1 downto 0):           # reverse sequential order
        BWD[i]:
          x[i] =
            ( y[i]
              - sum(j in [i+1, N), A[i, j] * x[j]
              ) * D[i]                      # D[i] = 1 / A[i, i]

dependencies:
    # LU factorization: row i depends on all previous rows < i
    for i1 in [0, N), i2 in [i1+1, N):
        FACT_L_ROW(i1)    -> FACT_L_ROW(i2)
        U_ROW_UPDATE(i1)  -> FACT_L_ROW(i2)
        U_ROW_UPDATE(i1)  -> U_ROW_UPDATE(i2)
        DIAG_RECIP(i1)    -> FACT_L_ROW(i2)   # D[j] used in later rows i>j

    # Triangular solves depend on completed LU (and D)
    for i in [0, N):
        DIAG_RECIP(i)     -> FWD(i)
        FACT_L_ROW(i)     -> FWD(i)
        U_ROW_UPDATE(i)   -> FWD(i)

    # Forward substitution: y[i] depends on y[0..i-1]
    for i1 in [0, N), i2 in [i1+1, N):
        FWD(i1) -> FWD(i2)

    # Backward substitution: x[i] depends on x[i+1..N-1] and D[i]
    for i1 in [0, N), i2 in [i1+1, N):
        BWD(i2) -> BWD(i1)                  # reverse order
        DIAG_RECIP(i1) -> BWD(i1)

    # Backward substitution must run after forward substitution
    for i in [0, N):
        FWD(i) -> BWD(i)

optimization:
    #----------------------------------------------------------
    # 1. Arithmetic optimizations
    #----------------------------------------------------------
    # Precompute and reuse reciprocals of U's diagonal in D:
    #   - L(i,j) formation uses multiplication by D[j] instead of
    #     division by A[j,j] for all i > j.
    #   - Backward substitution uses multiplication by D[i] instead
    #     of division by A[i,i].
    # This reduces O(N^2) divisions to O(N) divisions + O(N^2) multiplies.
    # (Already modeled explicitly via D and DIAG_RECIP.)
    #----------------------------------------------------------

    #----------------------------------------------------------
    # 2. Loop restructuring for better locality and SIMD
    #----------------------------------------------------------
    # U-row update now has j as innermost dimension over contiguous
    # memory. Further tile j to create cache-friendly chunks and
    # coarser-grain parallel tasks.
    block(j, Jt_U, TJ_U)    # only within U_ROW_UPDATE's inner j-loop

    # Forward/backward substitution sums over j also operate on
    # contiguous slices A[i, j] and x[j] / y[j]; tile those too.
    block(j, Jt_TRSV, TJ_TRSV)  # within sum(j, ...) in FWD_SUB and BWD_SUB

    #----------------------------------------------------------
    # 3. Parallelization
    #----------------------------------------------------------
    # Trailing U-row updates are independent across columns j,
    # once i and k are fixed. Parallelize over j-tiles for each row i.
    parallelize(Jt_U)
    # (Parallel region per i; Jt_U partitions row i into tiles, each
    #  processed by a different thread; no two threads update the
    #  same A[i,j] concurrently.)

    # Optional: similar fine-grain parallelism in back substitution
    # for each row i (limited benefit vs LU, but safe):
    # parallelize(Jt_TRSV)

    # NOTE: i remains sequential in all three phases due to true
    #       data dependencies; we do NOT parallelize i.

    #----------------------------------------------------------
    # 4. Vectorization and unrolling
    #----------------------------------------------------------
    # Vectorize inner j-loops that operate on contiguous memory:
    #  - U_ROW_UPDATE: A[i, j] and A[k, j] along j
    #  - FWD/BWD sums: A[i, j] and x[j]/y[j] along j
    vectorize(j, VEC_WIDTH)

    # Unroll short k-loops to expose ILP and reduce loop overhead:
    #  - L-row computation reductions over k
    #  - U-row update outer accumulation over k
    unroll(k, factor=4)

    #----------------------------------------------------------
    # 5. Optional cache/blocking across i (purely sequential)
    #----------------------------------------------------------
    # Tiling i can improve temporal locality for very large N
    # without changing the strict sequential dependence along i.
    # This expresses:
    #   for I in seq blocks of size TI:
    #     for ii in seq within block:
    #       i = I * TI + ii
    # and preserves the global order of i.
    block(i, I, TI)
    hoist(I)  # hoist tile index to outermost level to maximize reuse of rows of A within a tile.

/**
 * This version is stamped on May 10, 2016
 *
 * Contact:
 *   Louis-Noel Pouchet <pouchet.ohio-state.edu>
 *   Tomofumi Yuki <tomofumi.yuki.fr>

/* ludcmp.c: this file is part of PolyBench/C */

#include <stdio.h>
#include <unistd.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <math.h>

/* Include polybench common header. */
#include <polybench.h>

/* Include benchmark-specific header. */
#include "ludcmp.h"


/* Array initialization. */
static
void init_array (int n,
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(A,N,N,n,n),
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(b,N,n),
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(x,N,n),
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(y,N,n))
{
  int i, j;
  DATA_TYPE fn = (DATA_TYPE)n;

  for (i = 0; i < n; i++)
    {
      x[i] = 0;
      y[i] = 0;
      b[i] = (i+1)/fn/2.0 + 4;
    }

  for (i = 0; i < n; i++)
    {
      for (j = 0; j <= i; j++)
	A[i][j] = (DATA_TYPE)(-j % n) / n + 1;
      for (j = i+1; j < n; j++) {
	A[i][j] = 0;
      }
      A[i][i] = 1;
    }

  /* Make the matrix positive semi-definite. */
  /* not necessary for LU, but using same code as cholesky */
  int r,s,t;
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(B, DATA_TYPE, N, N, n, n);
  for (r = 0; r < n; ++r)
    for (s = 0; s < n; ++s)
      (POLYBENCH_ARRAY(B))[r][s] = 0;
  for (t = 0; t < n; ++t)
    for (r = 0; r < n; ++r)
      for (s = 0; s < n; ++s)
	(POLYBENCH_ARRAY(B))[r][s] += A[r][t] * A[s][t];
    for (r = 0; r < n; ++r)
      for (s = 0; s < n; ++s)
	A[r][s] = (POLYBENCH_ARRAY(B))[r][s];
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(B);

}


/* DCE code. Must scan the entire live-out data.
   Can be used also to check the correctness of the output. */
static
void print_array(int n,
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(x,N,n))

{
  int i;

  POLYBENCH_DUMP_START;
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_BEGIN("x");
  for (i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    if (i % 20 == 0) fprintf (POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, "\n");
    fprintf (POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, DATA_PRINTF_MODIFIER, x[i]);
  }
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_END("x");
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_FINISH;
}


/* Main computational kernel. The whole function will be timed,
   including the call and return. */
static
void kernel_ludcmp[[gnu::flatten, gnu::noinline]](int n,
		   DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(A,N,N,n,n),
		   DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(b,N,n),
		   DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(x,N,n),
		   DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(y,N,n))
{
  int i, j, k;

  DATA_TYPE w;

#pragma scop
  for (i = 0; i < _PB_N; i++) {
    for (j = 0; j <i; j++) {
       w = A[i][j];
       for (k = 0; k < j; k++) {
          w -= A[i][k] * A[k][j];
       }
        A[i][j] = w / A[j][j];
    }
   for (j = i; j < _PB_N; j++) {
       w = A[i][j];
       for (k = 0; k < i; k++) {
          w -= A[i][k] * A[k][j];
       }
       A[i][j] = w;
    }
  }

  for (i = 0; i < _PB_N; i++) {
     w = b[i];
     for (j = 0; j < i; j++)
        w -= A[i][j] * y[j];
     y[i] = w;
  }

   for (i = _PB_N-1; i >=0; i--) {
     w = y[i];
     for (j = i+1; j < _PB_N; j++)
        w -= A[i][j] * x[j];
     x[i] = w / A[i][i];
  }
#pragma endscop

}


int main(int argc, char** argv)
{
  /* Retrieve problem size. */
  int n = N;

  /* Variable declaration/allocation. */
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(A, DATA_TYPE, N, N, n, n);
  POLYBENCH_1D_ARRAY_DECL(b, DATA_TYPE, N, n);
  POLYBENCH_1D_ARRAY_DECL(x, DATA_TYPE, N, n);
  POLYBENCH_1D_ARRAY_DECL(y, DATA_TYPE, N, n);


  /* Initialize array(s). */
  init_array (n,
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A),
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(b),
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(x),
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(y));

  /* Start timer. */
  polybench_start_instruments;

  /* Run kernel. */
  kernel_ludcmp (n,
		 POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A),
		 POLYBENCH_ARRAY(b),
		 POLYBENCH_ARRAY(x),
		 POLYBENCH_ARRAY(y));

  /* Stop and print timer. */
  polybench_stop_instruments;
  polybench_print_instruments;

  /* Prevent dead-code elimination. All live-out data must be printed
     by the function call in argument. */
  polybench_prevent_dce(print_array(n, POLYBENCH_ARRAY(x)));

  /* Be clean. */
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(A);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(b);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(x);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(y);

  return 0;
}

                ( A[i, j]
                  - sum(k in [0, j)) ( A[i, k] * A[k, j] ) )
                / A[j, j]

        # 1.b Compute U(i, j) for j >= i  (upper triangle)
        #     U(i, j) = A(i, j) - sum_{k<i} L(i, k) * U(k, j)
        for j in [i, N):
            A[i, j] =
                A[i, j] - sum(k in [0, i)) ( A[i, k] * A[k, j] )

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 2. Forward substitution: solve L * y = b
    #    L has unit diagonal stored implicitly.
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    for i in seq([0, N)):
        y[i] =
            b[i] - sum(j in [0, i)) ( A[i, j] * y[j] )

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 3. Backward substitution: solve U * x = y
    #    Executed in decreasing i order: i = N-1, ..., 0.
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    for i in seq([0, N)) decreasing:   # semantics: process i = N-1 .. 0
        x[i] =
            ( y[i] - sum(j in (i, N)) ( A[i, j] * x[j] ) )
            / A[i, i]

dependencies:
    # LU factorization row dependencies:
    #  - Row i depends on all rows < i (both L and U entries).
    for i1 in [0, N), i2 in [0, N), i1 < i2:
        LU_row(i1) -> LU_row(i2)

    # Within the L-part of row i, iteration j depends on all prior j' < j:
    for i in [0, N), j1 in [0, i), j2 in [0, i), j1 < j2:
        L_update(i, j1) -> L_update(i, j2)

    # Within the U-part of a fixed row i, different j are independent
    # (given all required L(i, k) and previous rows are available).
    # There is no dependency between U_update(i, j1) and U_update(i, j2)
    # for j1 != j2 at fixed i.

    # Forward substitution (L * y = b): y[i] depends on all y[j], j < i.
    for i1 in [0, N), i2 in [0, N), i1 < i2:
        y_update(i1) -> y_update(i2)

    # Backward substitution (U * x = y): x[i] depends on all x[j], j > i.
    for i1 in [0, N), i2 in [0, N), i1 > i2:
        x_update(i1) -> x_update(i2)

optimization:
    # ================================================================
    # High-level algorithmic optimization: blocked right-looking LU
    # ================================================================
    # Replace the purely row-wise LU factorization by an equivalent
    # right-looking *blocked* LU to improve cache reuse and expose
    # coarse-grain parallelism in the trailing submatrix updates.
    #
    # The transformation preserves the algebra:
    #   - Panel factorization within each block uses the same formulas
    #     as in 'computation' and obeys the same dependencies.
    #   - Updates of A[r, c] are merely regrouped (associativity of +, *)
    #     and performed in blocks instead of elementwise.

    # Panel blocking along i (row dimension) for LU factorization.
    block(i, I_panel, NB_panel)
    # For each panel I_panel = [ii, ii+NB_panel):
    #   1. Factor the diagonal block A[ii:ii+NB_panel, ii:ii+NB_panel]
    #      sequentially using the scalar LU loops above (same semantics).
    #   2. Compute block row (U) and block column (L) adjacent to the
    #      diagonal block (Level-2 BLAS-like operations).
    #   3. Update the trailing submatrix A22 = A22 - L21 * U12, which
    #      is GEMM-like and optimized further below.

    # ================================================================
    # Cache/SIMD-friendly blocking for trailing submatrix updates
    # ================================================================
    # The GEMM-like trailing update after each panel has the form:
    #   for i in (panel_end, N):
    #     for j in (panel_end, N):
    #       A[i, j] -= sum(k in panel) A[i, k] * A[k, j]
    #
    # Apply 2D tiling over (i, j) to improve locality and create
    # independent tiles for parallel execution.
    block(i, I_trail, NB_trail_i)   # tile trailing rows
    block(j, J_trail, NB_trail_j)   # tile trailing columns

    # Arrange the innermost loops as:
    #   for I_trail:
    #     for J_trail:
    #       for k in panel:
    #         for j in J_trail (contiguous in memory)
    # to get contiguous access in j and good reuse of A[i, k].
    interchange(J_trail, k)

    # Vectorize and unroll across J_trail in the trailing GEMM-like kernel.
    vectorize(J_trail, VEC_J)
    unroll(J_trail, 4)

    # ================================================================
    # Exploiting parallelism
    # ================================================================
    # LU factorization:
    #   - I_panel (panels) remain sequential due to strong inter-panel
    #     dependencies.
    #   - Within a fixed panel, the U-part loop over j for a given i
    #     has no intra-row dependencies and is amenable to SIMD.
    #
    # Vectorize U-part j-loops (j in [i, N)):
    vectorize(j, VEC_J)    # only for the U update in each row
    unroll(j, 4)

    # Trailing submatrix update tiles (I_trail, J_trail) are independent
    # for a fixed panel. Parallelize over these tiles.
    parallelize(I_trail)
    parallelize(J_trail)

    # Forward and backward substitutions are inherently sequential in i,
    # but their inner j-loops can still be optimized.
    unroll(j, 4)           # for inner j in both solves
    vectorize(j, VEC_J)    # especially for backward solve (j in (i, N))

    # ================================================================
    # Scalar / memory micro-optimizations
    # ================================================================
    # - Hoist row pointers A[i, *] and frequently reused values
    #   (e.g., A[j, j] in L updates) outside inner loops.
    # - Keep accumulator 'w' in registers (already modeled in the code).
    # - Ensure A, b, x, y are aligned to vector width to maximize SIMD efficiency.
    hoist(i)  # hoist i-invariant address arithmetic out of inner loops
--- END OF MODEL: ludcmp-01 ---

domain:
    # Matrix / vector indices
    i: dim in [0, N)        # row index
    j: dim in [0, N)        # column index
    k: dim in [0, N)        # reduction index

data:
    # In-place LU factors:
    #   - On and above diagonal (i <= j): U(i,j)
    #   - Below diagonal (i > j):        L(i,j)
    #   with implicit L(i,i) = 1
    A[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j  # row-major

    # Right-hand side b and solution x, intermediate y
    b[i]: in DATA_TYPE  = i          # 1D row-major
    x[i]: out DATA_TYPE = i          # solution of A * x = b
    y[i]: out DATA_TYPE = i          # temporary for forward substitution

parameters:
    N: int                      # problem size

    # Tuning knobs (no change in mathematical result)
    TJ:   int                   # tile size for j (columns) in LU
    TK:   int                   # tile size for k (inner products) in LU
    TJ_f: int                   # tile size for j in forward substitution
    TJ_b: int                   # tile size for j in backward substitution
    VEC_J: int                  # vector width for j-dimension
    VEC_K: int                  # vector width for k-dimension
    UK:    int                  # unroll factor for k-reductions

computation:
    # In-place LU factorization without pivoting.
    # This matches the original nested i–j–k structure exactly:
    #   for i = 0..N-1:
    #     (1) compute L(i,0..i-1)
    #     (2) compute U(i,i..N-1)

    for i in seq([0, N)):
        L_factor:                         # compute strict lower part of row i
            for j in seq([0, i)):         # 0 <= j < i
                # A[i, j] := L(i,j)
                A[i, j] =
                    ( A[i, j]
                      - sum(k in seq([0, j)), A[i, k] * A[k, j]) )
                    / A[j, j]

        U_factor:                         # compute upper part of row i
            for j in seq([i, N)):         # i <= j < N
                # A[i, j] := U(i,j)
                A[i, j] =
                    A[i, j]
                    - sum(k in seq([0, i)), A[i, k] * A[k, j])

    # Forward substitution: solve L * y = b.
    # L has unit diagonal; lower part stored in A(i,j) for j < i.
    Forward:
        for i in seq([0, N)):
            y[i] =
                b[i]
                - sum(j in seq([0, i)), A[i, j] * y[j])

    # Backward substitution: solve U * x = y.
    # U is upper-triangular, stored in A(i,j) for j >= i.
    Backward:
        # descending loop: i = N-1, N-2, ..., 0
        for i in seq([0, N)) reversed:
            x[i] =
                ( y[i]
                  - sum(j in seq([i+1, N)), A[i, j] * x[j]) )
                / A[i, i]

dependencies:
    # 1. LU factorization (panel-wise, row i depends on rows 0..i-1)

    # L(i,j) depends on previous entries in the same row (L(i,0..j-1))
    # and on U(k,j) in rows k < j < i.
    for i in [0, N), j in [1, i):                   # j >= 1
        for k in [0, j):
            L_factor(i, k) -> L_factor(i, j)        # A[i,k] used in sum
            U_factor(k, j) -> L_factor(i, j)        # A[k,j] used in sum

    # U(i,j) depends on the entire L(i,0..i-1) and on U(0..i-1, j).
    for i in [0, N), j in [i, N):
        for k in [0, i):
            L_factor(i, k) -> U_factor(i, j)        # A[i,k] used in sum
            U_factor(k, j) -> U_factor(i, j)        # A[k,j] used in sum

    # 2. Forward substitution y: y[i] depends on all y[0..i-1]
    #    and on L(i,0..i-1).
    for i in [0, N):
        for j in [0, i):
            L_factor(i, j) -> Forward(i)
            Forward(j)     -> Forward(i)

    # 3. Backward substitution x: x[i] depends on x[i+1..N-1]
    #    and on U(i,i..N-1).
    for i in [0, N):
        for j in [i+1, N):
            U_factor(i, j) -> Backward(i)
            Backward(j)    -> Backward(i)

optimization:
    # -----------------------------------------------------------------
    # High-level notes:
    #  - Outer loop i must remain sequential for LU and both solves
    #    because each row i depends on all rows < i (and, for x,
    #    on rows > i).
    #  - Inner products (sums over k or j) are true reductions and
    #    are good targets for unrolling, vectorization and partial
    #    blocking.
    #  - For a single right-hand side, parallelism is available
    #    inside the U update (j >= i) but not in the L update (j < i).
    # -----------------------------------------------------------------

    # Keep i as the outermost loop for all phases (LU, forward, backward).
    hoist(i)

    # ---------------- LU factorization ----------------
    # Cache blocking for j and k in both L_factor and U_factor.
    # Tiles are processed in increasing index order to preserve all
    # loop-carried dependencies in the triangular L-part.
    #
    # For each fixed i:
    #   - L_factor: 0 <= j < i, 0 <= k < j
    #   - U_factor: i <= j < N, 0 <= k < i
    #
    # Block j and k to keep active rows and columns of A in L1/L2.
    block(j, J, TJ)     # j = J..min(J+TJ, bound_of_j)
    block(k, K, TK)     # k = K..min(K+TK, bound_of_k)

    # Within each j-tile of L_factor, maintain sequential j order.
    # This preserves the dependence of L(i,j) on L(i,0..j-1).

    # Parallelize only the U-part in j (columns) for each fixed i.
    # For U_factor at a given i, updates of U(i,j) for j >= i are
    # independent of each other, so they can be distributed across
    # threads safely.
    #
    #   for fixed i:
    #     for J in tiles of [i, N):
    #       parallel over J:
    #         for j in J:
    #           U(i,j) update ...
    parallelize(J)    # apply only to U_factor j-tiles (j >= i)

    # Vectorize inner products over k and column updates over j
    # where no loop-carried dependencies exist (U_factor and reductions).
    vectorize(k, VEC_K)       # inner reductions in L_factor and U_factor
    vectorize(j, VEC_J)       # U_factor column-wise updates

    # Unroll k to expose more ILP and better use fused-multiply-add (FMA)
    # units in the core.
    unroll(k, UK)

    # ---------------- Forward substitution (Ly = b) ----------------
    # i must remain sequential (triangular dependency on y[0..i-1]).
    # The inner sum over j is a reduction; we can:
    #   - block j for cache,
    #   - vectorize j within each row,
    #   - optionally implement the reduction with a small SIMD micro-kernel.
    block(j, J_f, TJ_f)       # tile j in Forward
    vectorize(j, VEC_J)

    # ---------------- Backward substitution (Ux = y) ----------------
    # i must remain sequential in descending order (triangular dependency
    # on x[i+1..N-1]). The inner sum over j is again a reduction.
    block(j, J_b, TJ_b)       # tile j in Backward
    vectorize(j, VEC_J)

    # ---------------- Optional extensions (conceptual) --------------
    # - If multiple right-hand sides are available, extend b, x, y to
    #   data structures b[i, r], x[i, r], y[i, r] over an extra
    #   dimension r (RHS index) and:
    #     * parallelize(r)
    #     * vectorize(r, VEC_R)
    #   turning the forward/back substitution into a level-3 BLAS-like
    #   TRSM operation with much higher arithmetic intensity.
    #
    # - On architectures with large caches, TJ and TK can be chosen so
    #   that a panel of several rows of L and a block of columns of U
    #   fit in L2, improving reuse of A[k, j] across different i.
--- END OF MODEL: ludcmp-02 ---
