/* mvt.c: this file is part of PolyBench/C */

#include <stdio.h>
#include <unistd.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <math.h>

/* Include polybench common header. */
#include <polybench.h>

/* Include benchmark-specific header. */
#include "mvt.h"


/* Array initialization. */
static
void init_array(int n,
		DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(x1,N,n),
		DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(x2,N,n),
		DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(y_1,N,n),
		DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(y_2,N,n),
		DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(A,N,N,n,n))
{
  int i, j;

  for (i = 0; i < n; i++)
    {
      x1[i] = (DATA_TYPE) (i % n) / n;
      x2[i] = (DATA_TYPE) ((i + 1) % n) / n;
      y_1[i] = (DATA_TYPE) ((i + 3) % n) / n;
      y_2[i] = (DATA_TYPE) ((i + 4) % n) / n;
      for (j = 0; j < n; j++)
	A[i][j] = (DATA_TYPE) (i*j % n) / n;
    }
}


/* DCE code. Must scan the entire live-out data.
   Can be used also to check the correctness of the output. */
static
void print_array(int n,
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(x1,N,n),
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(x2,N,n))

{
  int i;

  POLYBENCH_DUMP_START;
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_BEGIN("x1");
  for (i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    if (i % 20 == 0) fprintf (POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, "\n");
    fprintf (POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, DATA_PRINTF_MODIFIER, x1[i]);
  }
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_END("x1");

  POLYBENCH_DUMP_BEGIN("x2");
  for (i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    if (i % 20 == 0) fprintf (POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, "\n");
    fprintf (POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, DATA_PRINTF_MODIFIER, x2[i]);
  }
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_END("x2");
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_FINISH;
}


/* Main computational kernel. The whole function will be timed,
   including the call and return. */
static
void kernel_mvt[[gnu::flatten, gnu::noinline]](int n,
		DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(x1,N,n),
		DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(x2,N,n),
		DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(y_1,N,n),
		DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(y_2,N,n),
		DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(A,N,N,n,n))
{
  int i, j;

#pragma scop
  for (i = 0; i < _PB_N; i++)
    for (j = 0; j < _PB_N; j++)
      x1[i] = x1[i] + A[i][j] * y_1[j];
  for (i = 0; i < _PB_N; i++)
    for (j = 0; j < _PB_N; j++)
      x2[i] = x2[i] + A[j][i] * y_2[j];
#pragma endscop

}


int main(int argc, char** argv)
{
  /* Retrieve problem size. */
  int n = N;

  /* Variable declaration/allocation. */
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(A, DATA_TYPE, N, N, n, n);
  POLYBENCH_1D_ARRAY_DECL(x1, DATA_TYPE, N, n);
  POLYBENCH_1D_ARRAY_DECL(x2, DATA_TYPE, N, n);
  POLYBENCH_1D_ARRAY_DECL(y_1, DATA_TYPE, N, n);
  POLYBENCH_1D_ARRAY_DECL(y_2, DATA_TYPE, N, n);


  /* Initialize array(s). */
  init_array (n,
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(x1),
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(x2),
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(y_1),
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(y_2),
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A));

  /* Start timer. */
  polybench_start_instruments;

  /* Run kernel. */
  kernel_mvt (n,
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(x1),
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(x2),
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(y_1),
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(y_2),
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A));

  /* Stop and print timer. */
  polybench_stop_instruments;
  polybench_print_instruments;

  /* Prevent dead-code elimination. All live-out data must be printed
     by the function call in argument. */
  polybench_prevent_dce(print_array(n, POLYBENCH_ARRAY(x1), POLYBENCH_ARRAY(x2)));

  /* Be clean. */
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(A);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(x1);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(x2);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(y_1);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(y_2);

  return 0;
}

    # High-level semantics of the kernel:
    #   x1 := x1 + A * y_1
    #   x2 := x2 + A^T * y_2
    #
    # I.e., for all i in [0, N):

    #   x2[i]_out = x2[i]_in + Σ_{j=0}^{N-1} A[j, i]   * y_2[j]

    MV1: for i in [0, N):
             x1[i] = x1[i] + sum(j in [0, N), A[i, j] * y_1[j])

    MV2: for i in [0, N):
             x2[i] = x2[i] + sum(j in [0, N), A[j, i] * y_2[j])

dependencies:
    # MV1:
    #   For each fixed i, there is a reduction dependence along j on x1[i].
    #   Different i values are independent.
    #
    # MV2:
    #   For each fixed i, there is a reduction dependence along j on x2[i].
    #   Different i values are independent.
    #
    # MV1 and MV2 only share read-only data (A, y_1, y_2), so there are no
    # cross-dependencies between them.

optimization:
    #--------------------------------------------------------------
    # 1) Fuse the two matrix–vector products to reuse A[i, j] loads
    #--------------------------------------------------------------
    # Instead of making two full passes over A, we implement MV1 and MV2
    # together in a single row-major traversal:
    #
    #   for i in [0, N):
    #     tmp1 = x1[i]      # accumulator for x1[i]
    #     tmp2 = y_2[i]     # reused across all j for this i
    #     for j in [0, N):
    #       a = A[i, j]
    #       tmp1   += a * y_1[j]
    #       x2[j]  += a * tmp2
    #     x1[i] = tmp1
    #
    # This preserves the mathematical results:
    #   x1[i] = x1[i]_in + Σ_j A[i,j] * y_1[j]
    #   x2[j] = x2[j]_in + Σ_i A[i,j] * y_2[i]
    #
    # and halves the number of A loads compared to running MV1 and MV2
    # separately.
    fuse(MV1, MV2, along = {i, j})
    # 'fuse(MV1, MV2, along = {i, j})' (custom) means:
    #   - introduce a single 2D loop nest over (i, j) in row-major order of A
    #   - within that loop, perform both MV1 and MV2 updates as above.

    #--------------------------------------------------------------
    # 2) 2D blocking of the fused (i, j) iteration space
    #--------------------------------------------------------------

    # the corresponding pieces of x1, x2, y_1, y_2, fits in cache.

    block(j, J, TJ)    # J: tile index over cols, inner dimension still called j

    hoist(J)

    # temporal locality for y_1 (reused across i within a J-tile) and for
    # x2 updates within a J-tile.

    #--------------------------------------------------------------
    # 3) Parallelization across row tiles with privatized x2
    #--------------------------------------------------------------
    # Parallelize over I (row tiles). Each tile I works on a disjoint subset
    # of rows of A and of x1; x1 has no cross-tile dependencies.
    #

    # race on x2. We therefore privatize x2 for each parallel worker and
    # reduce after the fused loop.
    parallelize(I)

    #   privatize(x2[j], over = I)

    #   - for each parallel instance of tile I, allocate a private vector
    #     x2_private[0..N)
    #   - initialize x2_private[j] from the global x2[j]_in (or from 0 and
    #     add x2[j]_in in a final reduction step)
    #   - inside the fused, tiled loops, replace updates
    #         x2[j] += ...
    #     with
    #         x2_private[j] += ...
    #   - after all tiles finish, do a reduction:
    #         x2[j]_out = x2[j]_in + Σ_I x2_private_I[j]
    #
    # Extra memory: T * N elements, where T is the number of threads.
    # Since A holds N^2 elements, choosing T ≤ N / 2 keeps this below 50%
    # of A's size, satisfying the memory-usage constraint for typical N.
    privatize(x2[j], over = I)

    #--------------------------------------------------------------
    # 4) SIMD vectorization and unrolling along j
    #--------------------------------------------------------------
    # The innermost j loop operates on contiguous elements of A[i, j],
    # y_1[j], and x2[j], making it ideal for SIMD.
    vectorize(j, VEC)   # map j-loop to SIMD instructions of width VEC
    unroll(j, 4)        # additional unrolling to hide latency and reduce overhead

    #--------------------------------------------------------------
    # 5) Scalarization (register promotion) of hot scalar values
    #--------------------------------------------------------------
    # Promote frequently reused array elements to scalar temporaries so
    # they live in registers across inner-loop iterations.
    #
    # - x1[i] is accumulated across all j for a given i;
    # - y_2[i] is used for all j at a given i;
    # - within a tile, we can also keep x2_private[j] in registers when possible.
    #
    # 'scalarize' / 'scalarize_tile' are custom directives:
    #   scalarize(expr)        -> load once before the inner loop, store after
    #   scalarize_tile(expr)   -> same, but scoped to the current (I, J) tile.
    scalarize(x1[i])          # tmp1 accumulator instead of repeatedly loading/storing x1[i]
    scalarize(y_2[i])         # tmp2 = y_2[i] reused across j
    scalarize_tile(x2[j])     # keep x2_private[j] in registers within the innermost loop

    # 6) Optional: alternative coarse-grain parallelization
    #--------------------------------------------------------------
    # As an alternative (especially if fusion is disabled), each original
    # matrix–vector product can be parallelized independently over i:
    #
    #   parallelize(MV1.i)
    #   parallelize(MV2.i)
    #
    # In that case, no privatization of x2 is required because each i owns
    # a distinct output element in each kernel. This gives simpler
    # parallelism at the cost of two full passes over A.

            x2[i] = x2[i] + sum(j, A[j, i] * y_2[j])

    # dependence on x1[i] and x2[i]. There are no dependencies across i.

    #

    #   for j: x2[j] += sum_i A[i, j] * y_2[i]

    #------------------------------------------------------------------

    #------------------------------------------------------------------

    #   - load y_2[i] once and reuse it across all j in that row.
    #

    register_block(i, scalars={x1[i], y_2[i]})

    #       s2   = y_2[i]           # hoisted once per row
    #       for j in [0, N):
    #           acc1   += A[i, j] * y_1[j]
    #           x2[j]  += A[i, j] * s2
    #       x1[i] = acc1

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 2. Cache blocking (tiling) in i and j
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Tile the fused (i, j) space so that:
    #  - Rows of A are processed in blocks of BI to exploit L2/L3 reuse.
    #  - Columns of A, and the corresponding segments of x2 and y_1,
    #    are processed in blocks of BJ to fit in L1 and L2.
    block(i, I, BI)   # i = I * BI + i_inner
    block(j, J, BJ)   # j = J * BJ + j_inner

    # The resulting schedule is conceptually:
    #   for I in [0, ceil(N/BI)):
    #     for J in [0, ceil(N/BJ)):
    #       for i in I-tile:
    #         acc1 = x1[i]
    #         s2   = y_2[i]
    #         for j in J-tile:
    #           acc1  += A[i, j] * y_1[j]
    #           x2[j] += A[i, j] * s2
    #         x1[i] = acc1

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 3. SIMD vectorization and unrolling over j (inner, contiguous dim)
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # j is the contiguous dimension in row-major A and in the x2 and y_1
    # vectors; it is thus the natural candidate for SIMD vectorization.
    vectorize(J, VECLEN)   # vectorize inner j-iterations within each tile
    unroll(J, 4)           # unroll j-loop body by a small factor to reduce loop overhead

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 4. Parallelization over outer i-tiles with reduction on x2
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Directly parallelizing the fused outer i-loop causes races on x2[j],
    # because each i-row contributes to all entries of x2. We resolve this
    # with a classical reduction scheme using thread-local buffers x2_priv.
    #
    # Semantics of the directive below:
    #   - The I-tiles are distributed across T worker threads.
    #   - Each thread t accumulates into its private x2_priv[t, j] inside
    #     the fused kernel instead of directly into x2[j].
    #   - After all tiles are processed, a final reduction step:
    #       for j: x2[j] += sum_t x2_priv[t, j]
    #     merges the partial sums into the global x2.
    #
    # This adds T * N temporary storage. For N large (PolyBench sizes)
    # and T <= N/2, the extra memory remains below 50% of the original N×N A.
    parallelize(I)  # reduction(x2, +) implemented via thread-local x2_priv[t, j]

    # Concretely, inside each thread t, the fused, tiled kernel becomes:
    #
    #   for I in thread-local subset of [0, ceil(N/BI)):
    #     for J in [0, ceil(N/BJ)):
    #       for i in I-tile:
    #         acc1 = x1[i]
    #         s2   = y_2[i]
    #         for j in J-tile:
    #           acc1              += A[i, j] * y_1[j]
    #           x2_priv[t, j]     += A[i, j] * s2
    #         x1[i] = acc1
    #
    #   # global reduction after all threads finish:
    #   for j in [0, N):
    #     x2[j] = x2[j] + sum_t x2_priv[t, j]
--- END OF MODEL: mvt-03 ---

--- START OF MODEL: mvt-04 ---
domain:
    i1: dim in [0, N)   # row index for x1 update (A * y_1)
    i2: dim in [0, N)   # column index for x2 update (A^T * y_2)
    j:  dim in [0, N)   # reduction index

data:
    # Matrix A is stored once, row-major. Both kernels reuse this layout.
    A[i1, j]: in DATA_TYPE = (i1, j) -> i1 * N + j
        # Access A[i1, j] for the first kernel (row i1, col j).
        # Access A[j,  i2] for the second kernel (row j,  col i2) – same storage, different indices.

    # Vectors
    x1[i1]: inout DATA_TYPE = i1 -> i1
        # Initially contains x1_in; after kernel: x1_out[i1] = x1_in[i1] + Σ_j A[i1, j] * y_1[j].
    x2[i2]: inout DATA_TYPE = i2 -> i2
        # Initially contains x2_in; after kernel: x2_out[i2] = x2_in[i2] + Σ_j A[j, i2] * y_2[j].

    y_1[j]: in DATA_TYPE = j -> j
    y_2[j]: in DATA_TYPE = j -> j

parameters:
    # Problem size
    N: int

    # Tuning parameters (chosen for the target machine; all > 0)
    TI_X1: int   # tile size for i1 in the x1 update
    TJ_X1: int   # tile size for j  in the x1 update
    TI_X2: int   # tile size for i2 in the x2 update
    TJ_X2: int   # tile size for j  in the x2 update
    VLEN:  int   # SIMD vector width (elements per vector register)
    U_X1:  int   # unroll factor for the innermost loop in x1 update
    U_X2:  int   # unroll factor for the innermost loop in x2 update

computation:
    # 1) x1 <- x1 + A * y_1
    #
    #    For each i1, this is a scalar reduction over j. Different i1 values are independent.
    X1:
        for i1:
            x1[i1] = x1[i1] + sum(j, A[i1, j] * y_1[j])

    # 2) x2 <- x2 + A^T * y_2
    #
    #    For each i2, this is a scalar reduction over j using A[j, i2].
    #    Different i2 values are independent. This is logically a GEMV with A^T.
    X2:
        for i2:
            x2[i2] = x2[i2] + sum(j, A[j, i2] * y_2[j])

optimization:
    # General notes:
    # - Keep A row-major; do not materialize A^T. We only change loop orders and tiling.
    # - Reductions over j (in both X1 and X2) are implemented with register accumulators:
    #       acc = x?[i?];
    #       for j-tile / j:
    #           acc += A[...] * y_[...];
    #       x?[i?] = acc;
    #   This minimizes loads/stores of x1[i1]/x2[i2].
    # - Any extra temporaries are O(TI_*, TJ_*) scalars at most, so added memory is
    #   negligible compared to the original O(N^2) matrix (well below +50% footprint).

    # --- Optimizations for X1: x1 <- x1 + A * y_1 ---
    X1:
        # Tile in i1 and j to improve cache locality for A and y_1 and to expose
        # a coarse-grain parallel dimension on the i1 tiles.
        block(i1, I1, TI_X1)   # i1 = I1 * TI_X1 + (intra-tile i1)
        block(j,  J1, TJ_X1)   # j  = J1 * TJ_X1 + (intra-tile j)

        # Make the i1 tile index the outermost loop so each thread works on a
        # contiguous band of rows of A and a contiguous segment of x1.
        hoist(I1)

        # Parallelize across i1 tiles: each tile owns a disjoint subset of x1,
        # so there are no write conflicts.
        parallelize(I1)

        # Within a fixed (I1, J1) tile:
        #   - j is the fast-varying index; A[i1, j] is read contiguously in memory.
        #   - y_1[j] is also read contiguously and reused across all i1 within the tile.
        #
        # Vectorize and unroll the reduction over j to exploit SIMD and hide latency.
        vectorize(j, VLEN)
        unroll(j, U_X1)

        # Implementation detail:
        #   - For each fixed j (or J1-tile), load y_1[j] once and reuse it inside the
        #     innermost loop over i1 within that tile when profitable.
        #   - Use a scalar accumulator per (i1) in a register to avoid repeated
        #     loads/stores of x1[i1].

    # --- Optimizations for X2: x2 <- x2 + A^T * y_2 ---
    X2:
        # The naive loop order (i2 outer, j inner) accesses A[j, i2] as a column
        # with large strides. Interchange i2 and j so that we traverse A by rows:
        #   for j:
        #     for i2:
        #       x2[i2] += A[j, i2] * y_2[j];
        interchange(i2, j)

        # Now tile in i2 so that we can parallelize over disjoint chunks of x2.
        block(i2, I2, TI_X2)   # i2 = I2 * TI_X2 + (intra-tile i2)
        block(j,  J2, TJ_X2)   # j  = J2 * TJ_X2 + (intra-tile j)

        # Hoist the i2 tile index to the outermost level:
        #   for I2 (parallel):
        #     for J2:
        #       for j in J2-tile:
        #         for i2 in I2-tile:
        #           x2[i2] += A[j, i2] * y_2[j];
        hoist(I2)

        # Parallelize across I2: each thread owns a distinct segment of x2
        # (and the corresponding columns of A), so there are no races.
        parallelize(I2)

        # After interchange, the innermost loop is over i2:
        #   - A[j, i2] is read row-major (contiguous in memory).
        #   - x2[i2] is written contiguously, improving cache line utilization.
        #
        # Vectorize and unroll this innermost i2 loop.
        vectorize(i2, VLEN)
        unroll(i2, U_X2)

        # Implementation detail:
        #   - For each fixed j in a J2-tile, load y_2[j] once into a scalar and reuse it
        #     across the entire inner loop over i2 in that tile.
        #   - Use a scalar accumulator for x2[i2] in registers when possible.

    # --- Whole-kernel concurrency ---
    # X1 and X2 work on disjoint output vectors (x1 vs x2) and only read A, y_1, y_2.
    # They can therefore execute concurrently as separate tasks, each using its own
    # parallel region over I1 or I2, without additional synchronization beyond the
    # normal thread-join at kernel end.
--- END OF MODEL: mvt-04 ---

--- START OF MODEL: mvt-05 ---
domain:
    # Problem size
    i: dim in [0, N)        # row index
    j: dim in [0, N)        # column index

data:
    # Matrices / vectors; all are dense and contiguous.
    A[i, j]: in DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j
        # Row-major 2D array of size N×N.

    x1[i]: inout DATA_TYPE = i
        # Length-N vector, updated as x1 += A * y1.

    x2[j]: inout DATA_TYPE = j
        # Length-N vector, updated as x2 += A^T * y2.
        # Note: we index x2 by 'j' (column index) to make the reduction
        # direction explicit in the optimized form below.

    y1[j]: in DATA_TYPE = j
        # Length-N input vector.

    y2[i]: in DATA_TYPE = i
        # Length-N input vector.
        # Note: indexed by 'i' (row index) so that x2 becomes a reduction
        # over the row dimension.

parameters:
    N: int                   # Problem size, N > 0.

    # Tuning parameters (chosen based on cache/ISA; examples in comments).
    TI: int                  # Tile size along i (rows), e.g., 64–256.
    TJ: int                  # Tile size along j (cols), e.g., 64–256.
    VEC: int                 # SIMD width along j, e.g., 8 for AVX2 doubles, 16 for AVX-512.
    UNR: int                 # Inner-loop unroll factor, e.g., 4 or 8.

computation:
    # Reference mathematical semantics of the kernel (after safe index renaming).
    #
    # Original C:
    #   for i: for j: x1[i] += A[i][j] * y_1[j];
    #   for i: for j: x2[i] += A[j][i] * y_2[j];
    #
    # For x2 we rename indices (i <-> j) in the sum:
    #   x2[j] = x2[j] + sum_i A[i][j] * y2[i]
    # which is algebraically equivalent because both i and j range over [0, N).

    X1: for i in [0, N):
            x1[i] = x1[i] + sum(j in [0, N),
                                 A[i, j] * y1[j])

    X2: for j in [0, N):
            x2[j] = x2[j] + sum(i in [0, N),
                                 A[i, j] * y2[i])

optimization:
    #---------------------------------------------------------
    # 0. High-level view
    #---------------------------------------------------------
    # Both updates are matrix–vector products:
    #   x1 = x1 + A * y1
    #   x2 = x2 + A^T * y2
    #
    # After the index renaming in X2, *both* use the same element A[i, j]:
    #   contribution to x1[i] depends on (i, j) via y1[j]
    #   contribution to x2[j] depends on (i, j) via y2[i]
    #
    # This enables a fused 2D loop over (i, j) where each loaded A[i, j]
    # is used twice, improving cache reuse and halving A traffic.

    #---------------------------------------------------------
    # 1. Fuse the two matrix–vector products
    #---------------------------------------------------------
    fuse(X1, X2) along (i, j)
        # Fuses the computations X1 and X2 into a single loop nest over (i, j):
        #   for i in [0, N):
        #       for j in [0, N):
        #           x1[i] += A[i, j] * y1[j]
        #           x2[j] += A[i, j] * y2[i]
        #
        # This is equivalent to the 'sum' formulations:
        #   x1[i] = x1[i] + sum_j A[i, j] * y1[j]
        #   x2[j] = x2[j] + sum_i A[i, j] * y2[i]
        #
        # but now each A[i, j] is read once and reused for both updates.

    #---------------------------------------------------------
    # 2. 2D blocking (tiling) for cache locality
    #---------------------------------------------------------
    block(i, I, TI)
        # Split i into tile index I and intra-tile index i:
        #   i = I * TI + i_in, with i_in in [0, TI) (clipped at N).
        # Goal: keep a TI×TJ tile of A plus the corresponding x1/x2/y1/y2
        # slices resident in L2 cache.

    block(j, J, TJ)
        # Similarly, split j into tile index J and intra-tile index j:
        #   j = J * TJ + j_in, j_in in [0, TJ).

    hoist(I)
    hoist(J)
        # Reorder the loops so that the execution order is:
        #   for I in seq([0, ceil(N/TI))):
        #     for J in seq([0, ceil(N/TJ))):
        #       for i in [I*TI, min((I+1)*TI, N)):
        #         for j in [J*TJ, min((J+1)*TJ, N)):
        #           ...
        #
        # This outer I,J tiling ensures that we work on TI×TJ submatrices of A
        # and the matching contiguous chunks of y1, y2, x1, x2, improving
        # spatial and temporal locality.

    #---------------------------------------------------------
    # 3. Exploit reduction structure for parallelism
    #---------------------------------------------------------
    # After fusion and index renaming, we have explicit reductions:
    #   - x1[i] is a reduction over j
    #   - x2[j] is a reduction over i
    #
    # This allows safe parallelization across tiles in the i-dimension,
    # provided we treat x2 as a reduction variable along i.

    parallelize(I) with reduction(x2, +, i)
        # Parallelize the outer tile loop I across threads.
        # Each thread processes a subset of i-tiles.
        #
        # For x1:
        #   - Each i belongs to exactly one I-tile,
        #     so each element x1[i] is updated by a single thread.
        #
        # For x2:
        #   - x2[j] receives contributions from all i.
        #   - Those are reduced along the i-dimension.
        #   - 'reduction(x2, +, i)' expresses that the updates to x2[j]
        #     form a sum-reduction over i, so threads either:
        #       * use per-thread partial x2[j] and combine at the end of I,
        #         or
        #       * use atomic additions on x2[j].
        #
        # The implementation is free to choose the most efficient scheme
        # as long as it preserves:
        #   x2[j] = x2_initial[j] + sum_i A[i, j] * y2[i].

    #---------------------------------------------------------
    # 4. Inner-loop scalar hoisting
    #---------------------------------------------------------
    # Inside a given (I, i) row-tile, y2[i] is invariant w.r.t. the inner j-loop.

    # scalar_hoist(y2_i = y2[i], over j)
        # Conceptual directive:
        #   - Introduce a scalar temporary y2_i for each i.
        #   - Load y2_i = y2[i] once before the inner loop on j in that row.
        #   - Use y2_i inside the j-loop instead of reloading y2[i].
        #
        # This cuts the number of y2 loads by a factor of N.

    #---------------------------------------------------------
    # 5. Vectorization and unrolling of the innermost loop
    #---------------------------------------------------------
    vectorize(j, VEC)
        # Vectorize the innermost j-loop:
        #   - A[i, j], y1[j], and x2[j] are all contiguous in j
        #     under our row-major layout and loop ordering.
        #   - This allows efficient SIMD loads/stores/FMA operations
        #     of width VEC.

    unroll(j, UNR)
        # Unroll the j-loop by a small factor (e.g., 4 or 8) to:
        #   - expose more ILP (instruction-level parallelism),
        #   - reduce loop-control overhead,
        #   - and help the compiler schedule FMAs and memory ops efficiently.

    #---------------------------------------------------------
    # 6. Summary of optimized execution order
    #---------------------------------------------------------
    # The resulting (conceptual) optimized schedule is:
    #
    #   for I in parallel [0, ceil(N / TI)):
    #     for J in seq [0, ceil(N / TJ)):
    #       for i in [I*TI, min((I+1)*TI, N)):
    #         y2_i = y2[i]                 # scalar hoisted
    #         # x1_acc may be kept in a register by the compiler
    #         for j in [J*TJ, min((J+1)*TJ, N)) vectorized, unrolled:
    #           x1[i] += A[i, j] * y1[j]
    #           x2[j] += A[i, j] * y2_i    # '+'-reduction across I-tiles
    #
    # Mathematically, this is still:
    #   x1[i] = x1_initial[i] + sum_j A[i, j] * y1[j]
    #   x2[j] = x2_initial[j] + sum_i A[i, j] * y2[i]
    # which is equivalent to the original mvt.c kernel.
--- END OF MODEL: mvt-05 ---

/**
 * This version is stamped on May 10, 2016
 *
 * Contact:
 *   Louis-Noel Pouchet <pouchet.ohio-state.edu>
 *   Tomofumi Yuki <tomofumi.yuki.fr>
 *
 * Web address: http://polybench.sourceforge.net
 */
/* symm.c: this file is part of PolyBench/C */

#include <stdio.h>
#include <unistd.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <math.h>

/* Include polybench common header. */
#include <polybench.h>

/* Include benchmark-specific header. */
#include "symm.h"


/* Array initialization. */
static
void init_array(int m, int n,
		DATA_TYPE *alpha,
		DATA_TYPE *beta,
		DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(C,M,N,m,n),
		DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(A,M,M,m,m),
		DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(B,M,N,m,n))
{
  int i, j;

  *alpha = 1.5;
  *beta = 1.2;
  for (i = 0; i < m; i++)
    for (j = 0; j < n; j++) {
      C[i][j] = (DATA_TYPE) ((i+j) % 100) / m;
      B[i][j] = (DATA_TYPE) ((n+i-j) % 100) / m;
    }
  for (i = 0; i < m; i++) {
    for (j = 0; j <=i; j++)
      A[i][j] = (DATA_TYPE) ((i+j) % 100) / m;
    for (j = i+1; j < m; j++)
      A[i][j] = -999; //regions of arrays that should not be used
  }
}


/* DCE code. Must scan the entire live-out data.
   Can be used also to check the correctness of the output. */
static
void print_array(int m, int n,
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(C,M,N,m,n))
{
  int i, j;

  POLYBENCH_DUMP_START;
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_BEGIN("C");
  for (i = 0; i < m; i++)
    for (j = 0; j < n; j++) {
	if ((i * m + j) % 20 == 0) fprintf (POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, "\n");
	fprintf (POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, DATA_PRINTF_MODIFIER, C[i][j]);
    }
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_END("C");
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_FINISH;
}


/* Main computational kernel. The whole function will be timed,
   including the call and return. */
static
void kernel_symm[[gnu::flatten, gnu::noinline]](int m, int n,
		 DATA_TYPE alpha,
		 DATA_TYPE beta,
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(C,M,N,m,n),
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(A,M,M,m,m),
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(B,M,N,m,n))
{
  int i, j, k;
  DATA_TYPE temp2;

//BLAS PARAMS
//SIDE = 'L'
//UPLO = 'L'
// =>  Form  C := alpha*A*B + beta*C
// A is MxM
// B is MxN
// C is MxN
//note that due to Fortran array layout, the code below more closely resembles upper triangular case in BLAS
#pragma scop
   for (i = 0; i < _PB_M; i++)
      for (j = 0; j < _PB_N; j++ )
      {
        temp2 = 0;
        for (k = 0; k < i; k++) {
           C[k][j] += alpha*B[i][j] * A[i][k];
           temp2 += B[k][j] * A[i][k];
        }
        C[i][j] = beta * C[i][j] + alpha*B[i][j] * A[i][i] + alpha * temp2;
     }
#pragma endscop

}


int main(int argc, char** argv)
{
  /* Retrieve problem size. */
  int m = M;
  int n = N;

  /* Variable declaration/allocation. */
  DATA_TYPE alpha;
  DATA_TYPE beta;
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(C,DATA_TYPE,M,N,m,n);
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(A,DATA_TYPE,M,M,m,m);
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(B,DATA_TYPE,M,N,m,n);

  /* Initialize array(s). */
  init_array (m, n, &alpha, &beta,
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(C),
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A),
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(B));

  /* Start timer. */
  polybench_start_instruments;

  /* Run kernel. */
  kernel_symm (m, n,
	       alpha, beta,
	       POLYBENCH_ARRAY(C),
	       POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A),
	       POLYBENCH_ARRAY(B));

  /* Stop and print timer. */
  polybench_stop_instruments;
  polybench_print_instruments;

  /* Prevent dead-code elimination. All live-out data must be printed
     by the function call in argument. */
  polybench_prevent_dce(print_array(m, n, POLYBENCH_ARRAY(C)));

  /* Be clean. */
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(C);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(A);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(B);

  return 0;
}

domain:
    # Matrix dimensions follow the PolyBench symm kernel:
    #   A: M x M  (symmetric, lower triangle stored)
    #   B: M x N
    #   C: M x N
    i: dim in [0, M)
    j: dim in [0, N)
    k: dim in [0, M)

data:
    # A is stored in row-major order; only the lower triangle (i >= k)
    # is initialized and used. Logically we interpret A as symmetric:
    #   A_sym[i, k] = A[max(i, k), min(i, k)].
    A[i, k]: in DATA_TYPE =
        (i, k) -> i * M + k      # row-major, valid only for k <= i

    # B and C are full MxN row-major matrices.
    B[i, j]: in  DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j
    C[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j

    # 1D temporary buffers over j (columns). They are reused for each i and
    # do not change the mathematical result; they are introduced only in
    # the optimized schedule (see 'optimization' section).
    temp1[j]: tmp DATA_TYPE = (j) -> j   # holds alpha * B[i, j] for fixed i
    temp2[j]: tmp DATA_TYPE = (j) -> j   # holds sum_{k<i} A[i,k] * B[k, j]

parameters:
    alpha: DATA_TYPE
    beta:  DATA_TYPE

    # Tuning parameters (not part of the mathematical semantics):
    BM: int  # suggested block size in i (rows)  – can be left unused or 0
    BN: int  # block size in j (columns), e.g., 64–256 depending on cache
    VJ: int  # SIMD vector length in j, e.g., 4 or 8 for doubles
    UK: int  # unroll factor for k, e.g., 4

computation:
    # Logical BLAS SYMM semantics (SIDE = 'L', UPLO = 'L'):
    #   C_out = beta * C_in + alpha * Symm(A) * B,
    # where Symm(A) is the full symmetric matrix whose lower triangle is
    # stored in A:
    #   Symm(A)[i, k] = A[max(i, k), min(i, k)].
    #
    # Written explicitly to use only the stored lower triangle of A:
    #
    #   C[i, j] = beta * C[i, j]
    #             + alpha * (
    #                   A[i, i] * B[i, j]
    #                 + sum_{k=0..i-1}   A[i, k] * B[k, j]
    #                 + sum_{k=i+1..M-1} A[k, i] * B[k, j]
    #               )
    #
    # This exactly matches the PolyBench kernel, which accumulates the
    # k < i part directly for C[i, j] and the k > i part indirectly via
    # updates to C[k, j] at larger outer indices.
    for i, j:
        C[i, j] = beta * C[i, j] \
                  + alpha * (
                        A[i, i] * B[i, j]
                      + sum(k in [0, i),   A[i, k] * B[k, j])
                      + sum(k in [i+1, M), A[k, i] * B[k, j])
                  )

optimization:
    # -----------------------------------------------------------------
    # Custom optimization primitive:
    #   transform(NAME)
    # denotes an algorithmic transformation that is mathematically
    # equivalent to the 'computation' but changes loop structure and
    # introduces temporaries as described in the comments around it.
    # -----------------------------------------------------------------

    # 1. Hoist the beta scaling of C out of the main symmetric multiply.
    #
    # From:
    #   C[i,j] = beta*C[i,j] + alpha*F(i,j)
    # To:
    #   C[i,j] = beta*C[i,j]        # separate pass over C
    #   C[i,j] += alpha*F(i,j)      # main kernel no longer multiplies by beta
    #
    # This reduces work in the hot triangular kernel and exposes a
    # simple, easily vectorizable and parallelizable scaling pass.
    transform(scale_C_by_beta)

    # 2. Reorder the main kernel into an i–k–j loop nest with 1D
    #    temporary vectors to improve cache locality and reduce memory
    #    traffic. For each fixed row i:
    #
    #   # Precompute scaled row of B and zero accumulator.
    #   for j in [0, N):
    #       temp1[j] = alpha * B[i, j]
    #       temp2[j] = 0
    #
    #   # Handle contributions from the strictly lower part (k < i):
    #   for k in [0, i):                 # sequential in k, triangular
    #       a_ik = A[i, k]               # hoisted out of the j-loop
    #       for j in [0, N):             # innermost, contiguous in memory
    #           # C[k, j] gets alpha * A[i,k] * B[i,j]
    #           C[k, j] += a_ik * temp1[j]
    #           # temp2[j] accumulates A[i,k] * B[k,j]
    #           temp2[j] += a_ik * B[k, j]
    #
    #   # Finalize row i using the diagonal and the accumulated temp2.
    #   a_ii = A[i, i]
    #   for j in [0, N):
    #       C[i, j] += a_ii * temp1[j] + alpha * temp2[j]
    #
    # Together with the separate C *= beta pass above, this is
    # algebraically identical to the specification in 'computation':
    #   each A[i,k] (i>k) contributes once to C[k,*] and once to C[i,*],
    #   exactly matching Symm(A)*B, and no element of the upper triangle
    #   A[i,k] with k>i is ever read.
    #
    # Advantages:
    #   - Inner loops run over j, the contiguous dimension of row-major
    #     B and C, enabling efficient SIMD vectorization.
    #   - A[i,k] and alpha*B[i,j] are reused across many operations
    #     (rank-1 updates), reducing loads and multiplications.
    #   - temp1 and temp2 are length-N vectors; extra memory is O(N),
    #     well within the 50% overhead budget.
    transform(symm_rank1_update_with_temp_vectors)

    # 3. Block the column dimension j to improve cache locality for B
    #    and C and to provide a natural unit for parallel work.  After
    #    'block(j, Jb, BN)', Jb ranges over tiles and j ranges within
    #    each tile.
    block(j, Jb, BN)

    # 4. Expose parallelism over independent column tiles.
    #    - Different Jb tiles write to disjoint sets of C[*, j] and read
    #      disjoint columns of B, so they are free of data races.
    #    - The outer i loop remains sequential because rows C[k, *] are
    #      updated across multiple i values (reduction-like dependence).
    parallelize(Jb)

    # 5. Vectorize innermost j loops inside each tile.
    #    - With the i–k–j ordering from the transform above and row-
    #      major layout, the j-loop accesses B[i, j], B[k, j], C[k, j],
    #      C[i, j], temp1[j], and temp2[j] with unit stride.
    #    - VJ should match the SIMD width (e.g., 4 or 8 doubles).
    vectorize(j, VJ)

    # 6. Optionally unroll the k-loop to increase instruction-level
    #    parallelism and reduce loop control overhead within each
    #    (i, Jb) tile. The triangular bound (k < i) is preserved.
    unroll(k, UK)

    # 7. The outer i loop is kept sequential to respect the triangular
    #    dependency pattern on C:
    #      C[k, j] accumulates contributions from all i > k.
    #    We *do not* apply parallelize(i); any parallelization across i
    #    would require an explicit reduction scheme on C.
--- END OF MODEL: symm-01 ---

--- START OF MODEL: symm-02 ---
domain:
    # Matrix dimensions (PolyBench: M == m, N == n)
    i: dim in [0, M)          # row index of A and C
    j: dim in [0, N)          # column index of B and C
    k: dim in [0, M)          # reduction index over rows of B / columns of A

data:
    # A is an MxM symmetric matrix stored in row-major *lower-triangular* form:
    #   A[i, k] is valid only for k <= i; elements with k > i are never read.
    A[i, k]: in DATA_TYPE = (i, k) -> i * M + k        # row-major, lower triangle used

    # B is an MxN dense matrix, row-major.
    B[i, j]: in DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j        # row-major

    # C is an MxN dense matrix, row-major, updated in place.
    C[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j     # row-major

    # Optional logical view (no extra storage):
    # S[i, k] = A[i, k]  if k <= i
    #         = A[k, i]  if k >  i
    # S is the full symmetric matrix implied by the stored lower triangle of A.
    # All computations below are expressed directly in terms of A to avoid
    # touching the unused upper triangle.
    #S[i, k]: virtual DATA_TYPE  # symmetric view over A (lower-triangular storage)

parameters:
    alpha: DATA_TYPE
    beta: DATA_TYPE
    M: int
    N: int

    # Tuning parameters for the optimized kernel (no semantic effect):
    TI: int    # tile size in i (rows of A,C)
    TJ: int    # tile size in j (cols of B,C)
    TK: int    # tile size in k (rows of B / columns of A)
    VJ: int    # vector width along j for SIMD
    UK: int    # unroll factor for the k-reduction inside a tile

computation:
    # High-level mathematical specification derived from the kernel:
    #   SIDE = 'L', UPLO = 'L'
    #   C := alpha * A_sym * B + beta * C
    # where A_sym is the symmetric matrix defined by A's lower triangle.
    #
    # For each output element C[i, j], the symmetric product can be written
    # without ever reading A's upper triangle as:
    #
    #   C[i, j] = beta * C[i, j]
    #             + alpha * [ sum_{k = 0..i}   A[i, k] * B[k, j]
    #                        + sum_{k = i+1..M-1} A[k, i] * B[k, j] ]
    #
    # The first sum uses row i of the stored lower triangle (including the
    # diagonal), the second sum uses column i of the strictly lower part.

    for i, j:
        C[i, j] =
            beta * C[i, j]
            + alpha * (
                  sum(k in [0, i+1),   A[i, k] * B[k, j])      # k <= i
                + sum(k in [i+1, M),   A[k, i] * B[k, j])      # k >  i
              )

dependencies:
    # Each (i, j) computes C[i, j] exactly once from the input values of
    # A, B, and the original C[i, j]. No C[i, j] depends on any other
    # C[i', j'] with (i', j') != (i, j).
    #
    # The only reductions are over k inside each (i, j), using a private
    # accumulator. Therefore:
    #   - All (i, j) iterations are mutually independent.
    #   - The k-reductions can be freely reordered or blocked, provided
    #     they remain associative and use a private accumulator per (i, j).

optimization:
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # 1. Cache-friendly 3D blocking (tiling)
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # Tile the i (rows of A,C), j (cols of B,C), and k (rows of B)
    # dimensions. TK should be chosen so that a tile of B[Kk, Jj] and the
    # corresponding rows of C[i, Jj] fit in L1/L2 cache. TI and TJ tune
    # spatial locality for C and B.
    block(i, Ii, TI)     # Ii: tile index over rows of A,C
    block(j, Jj, TJ)     # Jj: tile index over columns of B,C
    block(k, Kk, TK)     # Kk: tile index over the reduction dimension

    # After blocking, the core computation conceptually becomes:
    #   for Ii, Jj, Kk:
    #     for i in tile(Ii), j in tile(Jj):
    #       C[i, j] += alpha * sum(k in tile(Kk) ∩ domain(i),
    #                              symmetric_A_times_B(i, k, j))
    # where domain(i) encodes the triangular constraint:
    #   k <= i   -> use A[i, k]
    #   k >  i   -> use A[k, i]

    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # 2. Loop reordering to reuse B and C (k-major, then i/j tiles)
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # Hoist the k-tile loop Kk outward so that we process one band of rows
    # of B (B[Kk, :]) at a time, reusing it across many rows i and columns j
    # of C before moving to the next k-tile.
    #
    # Effective loop order (conceptually):
    #   for Kk:                         # outermost: k-tiles
    #     for Ii:                       # tiles over rows of A,C
    #       for Jj:                     # tiles over columns of B,C
    #         for i in tile(Ii):
    #           for j in tile(Jj):
    #             accumulate over k in tile(Kk) ∩ domain(i)
    hoist(Kk)

    # Hoist Ii and Jj above the point where the k-slice of B is fully
    # available; within a fixed Kk we then sweep C by tiles. This exposes
    # coarse-grain parallelism and improves temporal locality on C.
    hoist(Ii)
    hoist(Jj)

    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # 3. Exploit symmetry of A explicitly
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # Within each (Kk, Ii) tile, split the k-iteration into the two affine
    # regions implied by the triangular structure of A:
    #
    #   for i in tile(Ii):
    #     # Part 1: k in [0, i] ∩ tile(Kk): use row i of A (A[i, k])
    #     for k in [0, i+1) ∩ tile(Kk):
    #       ... use A[i, k] * B[k, j] ...
    #
    #     # Part 2: k in [i+1, M) ∩ tile(Kk): use column i (A[k, i])
    #     for k in [i+1, M) ∩ tile(Kk):
    #       ... use A[k, i] * B[k, j] ...
    #
    # This guarantees that we never read A[i, k] with k > i (those entries
    # were initialized to a sentinel value and are semantically undefined).
    # It also allows the compiler/polyhedral optimizer to drop unreachable
    # parts of the iteration space and reduce conditionals in the innermost
    # loops.
    # (This is a semantic property, so we express it as a comment-level
    #  constraint on the reduced k-domain rather than as a new directive.)

    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # 4. Parallelization
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # All (i, j) iterations are independent, so we can parallelize
    # over outer tiles. On a 32-core/64-thread x64 machine, a 2D tiling
    # over Ii and Jj gives good load balance; a runtime can map the 2D
    # iteration space to threads.
    parallelize(Ii)      # distribute i-tiles across threads
    parallelize(Jj)      # optionally also distribute j-tiles (2D decomposition)

    # The k-tiles Kk are reductions; they execute sequentially with respect
    # to each (i, j), but different (i, j) tiles are independent.

    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # 5. Vectorization and unrolling
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # j is the unit-stride dimension in row-major storage for both B and C.
    # Make j the innermost loop inside each tile and vectorize it to exploit
    # SIMD (AVX/AVX2/AVX-512). VJ should match the hardware vector width.
    vectorize(j, VJ)

    # Unroll the k-loop within each tile to:
    #   - reduce loop overhead,
    #   - expose multiple independent FMA chains for better ILP.
    unroll(k, UK)

    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # 6. Scalar hoisting and reuse (micro-optimizations)
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # Within the innermost loops (after blocking/reordering), hoist:
    #   - alpha into a register,
    #   - a per-(i, k) scalar s = alpha * (A[i, k] or A[k, i]),
    # so that for a fixed (i, k) we compute s once and reuse it across the
    # inner j-loop:
    #
    #   s = alpha * (i >= k ? A[i, k] : A[k, i])
    #   for j in tile(Jj):
    #       C[i, j] += s * B[k, j]
    #
    # This eliminates redundant multiplications by alpha and reduces loads
    # from A inside the innermost FMA loop.
    #
    # (Expressed here as a comment-level guideline; it corresponds to
    #  common scalar replacement and strength-reduction performed by -O3.)
--- END OF MODEL: symm-02 ---

--- START OF MODEL: symm-03 ---
# Optimized model for symm.c
# (C := alpha * A * B + beta * C, with A symmetric and only its lower triangle stored)

domain:
    i: dim in [0, M)   # rows of A and C
    j: dim in [0, N)   # columns of B and C
    k: dim in [0, M)   # rows of B / columns of A

data:
    # A is conceptually symmetric. Only its lower triangle (k <= i) is initialized:
    #   A[i, k] is valid for 0 <= k <= i < M.
    # For k > i, A[i, k] holds a sentinel (-999) and must never be read.
    # We model it as a full MxM row-major array with a "lower_symmetric" access convention.
    A[i, k]: in DATA_TYPE  = (i, k) -> i * M + k   # row-major, valid for k <= i only

    # B and C are dense MxN row-major matrices.
    B[k, j]: in    DATA_TYPE   = (k, j) -> k * N + j   # row-major
    C[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE   = (i, j) -> i * N + j   # row-major

    # Temporary buffer: a copy of B pre-scaled by alpha, to reduce multiplications
    # inside the main symmetric product.
    B_alpha[k, j]: temp DATA_TYPE = (k, j) -> k * N + j  # same layout as B

parameters:
    alpha: DATA_TYPE
    beta:  DATA_TYPE

    # Tunable blocking and SIMD parameters (hardware/caches dependent).
    Ti:  int  # tile size in i (rows of A, C), e.g., 64
    Tj:  int  # tile size in j (cols of B, C), e.g., 64
    Tk:  int  # tile size in k (rows of B / cols of A), e.g., 64
    VEC: int  # SIMD width along j, e.g., 4 (double) or 8 (float)
    UJ:  int  # unroll factor for innermost j-loop (multiple of VEC)

computation:
    # 1) Scale C by beta.
    # In the original kernel, each C[i, j] is multiplied by beta exactly once when i matches
    # the row index. Doing it here in a separate pass is mathematically equivalent and exposes
    # a simple, fully parallel loop.
    scale_C:
        for i, j:
            C[i, j] = beta * C[i, j]

    # 2) Pre-scale B by alpha once and reuse.
    # This trades one global M*N multiply for many per-(i, k, j) multiplications,
    # reducing arithmetic in the main kernel and allowing FMAs on (A * B_alpha).
    pre_scale_B:
        for k, j:
            B_alpha[k, j] = alpha * B[k, j]

    # 3) Symmetric matrix-matrix product:
    #    Conceptual symmetric matrix A_sym is defined by:
    #        A_sym[i, k] = A[i, k]  if k <= i
    #                    = A[k, i]  if k > i
    #    Only initialized entries of A (its lower triangle) are ever accessed.
    #
    #    Final result:
    #        C[i, j] = beta * C0[i, j] + alpha * sum_{k=0..M-1} A_sym[i, k] * B[k, j]
    #
    #    Using B_alpha (already multiplied by alpha) and the implicit A_sym:
    symm_main:
        for i, j:
            C[i, j] = C[i, j] +
                      sum(k,
                          (if k <= i
                           then A[i, k]
                           else A[k, i]) * B_alpha[k, j])

dependencies:
    # C must be fully scaled before symmetric contributions are accumulated.
    for i in [0, M), j in [0, N):
        scale_C(i, j) -> symm_main(i, j)

    # Each symm_main(i, j) uses B_alpha[k, j] for all k, so it depends on all
    # pre_scale_B(k, j) for that column j.
    for i in [0, M), j in [0, N), k in [0, M):
        pre_scale_B(k, j) -> symm_main(i, j)

optimization:
    # --- Cache blocking / tiling ---

    # Tile all three logical dimensions so that blocks of A, B_alpha, and C fit in cache.
    block(i, I, Ti)   # I indexes row tiles of A and C
    block(j, J, Tj)   # J indexes column tiles of B_alpha and C
    block(k, K, Tk)   # K indexes row tiles of B_alpha / column tiles of A

    # Execute tiles in the order (I, K, J) for better reuse of A and B_alpha:
    #   for I
    #     for K
    #       for J
    #         ... inner scalar loops over i, k, j inside the tiles ...
    hoist(I)
    hoist(K)
    hoist(J)

    # Inside each (I, K) tile, enforce the symmetric lower-triangular structure:
    # - Implement the k-sum of symm_main using only initialized entries of A:
    #       if k <= i then read A[i, k]
    #       else         read A[k, i]
    # - A code generator may choose equivalent implementations, e.g.:
    #     * Split the reduction over k into [0, i) and (i, M), or
    #     * Iterate only over the lower-triangular region (i >= k) and, for each
    #       (i, k), update both C[i, j] and C[k, j] in one pass:
    #           for i in [0, M)
    #             for k in [0, i]
    #               a = A[i, k]
    #               if i == k:
    #                 for j: C[i, j] += a * B_alpha[i, j]
    #               else:
    #                 for j:
    #                   C[i, j] += a * B_alpha[k, j]
    #                   C[k, j] += a * B_alpha[i, j]
    #   This variant matches the standard BLAS SYMM(L, L) algorithm and maximizes
    #   reuse of each A[i, k].

    # --- Parallelism ---

    # Different columns of C (different j) are completely independent:
    # C[:, j0] depends only on B_alpha[:, j0] and A.
    # Parallelize across column tiles to avoid write conflicts:
    parallelize(J)

    # With an implementation that privatizes or atomically updates tiles of C, additional
    # parallelism over I tiles can be exposed as well:
    # parallelize(I)

    # --- SIMD vectorization and unrolling ---

    # Ensure the innermost loop runs over j so that C[i, j] and B_alpha[k, j]
    # are accessed with unit stride (row-major layout).
    vectorize(j, VEC)
    unroll(j, UJ)

    # --- Optional layout optimization for A (packed lower triangle) ---
    # packed_lower(A, A_packed)
    #   # A_packed is a conceptual 1D buffer of length M*(M+1)/2 that stores the lower
    #   # triangle of A row by row:
    #   #   A_packed[offset(i, k)] = A[i, k]   for 0 <= k <= i < M
    #   #   offset(i, k) = i*(i+1)/2 + k
    #   #
    #   # All uses of:
    #   #   if k <= i then A[i, k] else A[k, i]
    #   # are implemented as:
    #   #   A_packed[offset(max(i, k), min(i, k))]
    #   #
    #   # This reduces the memory footprint and bandwidth for A, while never accessing
    #   # the sentinel region A[i, k] (k > i). Numerical results are unchanged.
--- END OF MODEL: symm-03 ---

--- START OF MODEL: symm-04 ---
domain:
    i: dim in [0, M)   # row index of A and C
    j: dim in [0, N)   # column index of B and C
    k: dim in [0, M)   # shared dimension (row of B / col or row of A)

data:
    # A is stored as an M×M row-major matrix, but only the lower triangle (k <= i)
    # contains valid data; the upper triangle is unused (filled with -999).
    A[i, k]: in DATA_TYPE = (i, k) -> i * M + k   # row-major, lower-triangular used

    # B and C are dense M×N row-major matrices.
    B[k, j]: in    DATA_TYPE = (k, j) -> k * N + j  # row-major
    C[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j  # row-major

parameters:
    alpha: DATA_TYPE
    beta:  DATA_TYPE

    # Tuning parameters for cache blocking and SIMD; chosen to fit target cache sizes
    # and vector width on the x64 machine.
    TI: int > 0  # tile size for i (rows of A and C)
    TJ: int > 0  # tile size for j (columns of B and C)
    TK: int > 0  # tile size for k (rows of B / columns of A)

    VEC_WIDTH: int > 0  # SIMD width in elements for vectorization along j

computation:
    # High-level semantics:
    #   C := beta * C + alpha * A_sym * B
    # where A_sym is the symmetric matrix:
    #   A_sym[i, k] = A[i, k] if k <= i, else A[k, i]
    # Only the stored lower triangle of A is ever read.

    SCALE_C:
    for i, j:
        C[i, j] = beta * C[i, j]

    # Symmetric matrix-matrix multiply contribution.
    # Expanded to avoid any access to the unused upper part of A.
    UPDATE_C:
    for i, j:
        C[i, j] += alpha * (
            A[i, i] * B[i, j]                          # diagonal term
            + sum(k in [0, i))  A[i, k] * B[k, j]      # k < i: use A[i, k]
            + sum(k in (i, M)) A[k, i] * B[k, j]       # k > i: use A[k, i]
        )

dependencies:
    # The scaling of C must precede the symmetric update for each element.
    for i in [0, M), j in [0, N):
        SCALE_C(i, j) -> UPDATE_C(i, j)

    # Within UPDATE_C, for each fixed (i, j), the terms over k form a reduction.
    # There are no dependencies across different (i, j) pairs.
    # This permits reordering and parallelization over i and j, while k is a
    # pure reduction dimension.
    for i in [0, M), j in [0, N), k1 in [0, M), k2 in [0, M):
        if k1 < k2:
            UPDATE_C(i, j, k1) -> UPDATE_C(i, j, k2)

optimization:
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 1. Parallelize and vectorize the scaling of C (embarrassingly parallel).
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    parallelize(i)           # distribute rows of C across threads in SCALE_C
    vectorize(j, VEC_WIDTH)  # SIMD over contiguous columns of C in SCALE_C

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 2. Treat UPDATE_C as a GEMM-like kernel with a symmetric left matrix.
    #    Apply 3D tiling for cache locality.
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Tile the logical dimensions:
    block(i, I, TI)  # tiles of rows  of A and C
    block(k, K, TK)  # tiles of the shared dimension (rows of B / cols of A)
    block(j, J, TJ)  # tiles of columns of B and C

    # Choose a loop ordering that:
    #   - keeps j innermost for unit-stride access in B[k, j] and C[i, j];
    #   - reuses A[i, k] and A[k, i] across many j within a tile;
    #   - reuses B[k, j] across multiple i within a (K, J) tile.
    #
    # Target order inside UPDATE_C:
    #   for I in tiles(i):
    #     for K in tiles(k):
    #       for J in tiles(j):
    #         for i in I:
    #           for k in K:
    #             for j in J:  # innermost, unit-stride
    #               use A[i,k] or A[k,i], B[k,j], update C[i,j]
    interchange(K, J)  # make j-tiles (J) the innermost tile loop within each (I, K)

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 3. Exploit thread-level and data-parallelism in the tiled UPDATE_C.
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    parallelize(I)           # distribute independent row-tiles of C across cores
    vectorize(j, VEC_WIDTH)  # SIMD on the innermost j-loop in each (I, K, J) tile
    unroll(k, 4)             # modest unrolling of the k-loop inside each K-tile
                             # to increase ILP and register reuse

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 4. Algebraic hoisting of alpha out of the innermost loop.
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Conceptual transformation (no extra arrays required):
    #   For each (i, k) in a tile, compute once:
    #       a_ik = (k <= i ? A[i, k] : A[k, i])
    #       a_scaled = alpha * a_ik

    #       C[i, j] += a_scaled * B[k, j]

    # multiplication, reducing arithmetic and enabling efficient FMA use.
    #scale_A_by_alpha(A)  # # conceptual optimization: hoist alpha*A into registers

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 5. Symmetry-aware access to A: avoid touching the unused upper triangle.
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Implement the A_sym access in UPDATE_C by always mapping to the lower
    # triangle of A:
    #   if k <= i: use A[i, k]
    #   else:      use A[k, i]
    #
    # This preserves the original semantics (never reading the sentinel -999
    # entries) while enabling symmetric reuse of each stored A[i, k].
    #symm_lower(A)  # # conceptual: enforce lower-triangular-only loads from A

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 6. (Optional) Per-thread or per-tile scratch buffers.
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # For large N, it can be beneficial to allocate a small temporary buffer per
    # (I, K) tile (on the stack or in thread-local storage) to hold a contiguous
    # block of B[K, J] or partial C[I, J], improving prefetching and alignment.
    # The total extra memory is O(TI * TJ + TK * TJ) per thread, which can be
    # kept well below 50% of the original footprint for reasonable tile sizes.

domain:
    i: dim in [0, M)      # row index of A and C
    j: dim in [0, N)      # column index of B and C
    k: dim in [0, M)      # row index of B / column index of A

data:
    # A stores only the lower triangular part of a logical symmetric matrix S:
    #   S[i, k] = A[i, k] if i >= k, else S[i, k] = A[k, i]
    # Entries A[i, k] with k > i are never used.
    A[i, k]: in DATA_TYPE = (i, k) -> i * M + k        # row-major M×M

    B[k, j]: in DATA_TYPE = (k, j) -> k * N + j        # row-major M×N
    C[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j     # row-major M×N

    alpha: scalar DATA_TYPE
    beta:  scalar DATA_TYPE

    # Loop-private temporaries (no extra asymptotic storage)
    s: scalar DATA_TYPE   # symmetric matrix element S(i,k)
    t: scalar DATA_TYPE   # alpha * s

parameters:
    # Tunable tile sizes (chosen for cache hierarchy of the target machine).
    TI: int   # tile size for i (rows of A,C), e.g., 32–64
    TK: int   # tile size for k (rows of B / cols of A), e.g., 32–64
    TJ: int   # tile size for j (columns of B,C), e.g., 64–256

    VEC: int  # SIMD width for vectorization along j (e.g., 4/8/16 depending on DATA_TYPE and ISA)

computation:
    # Mathematical semantics of the kernel:
    #   Let S(i,k) = A[i,k] if i >= k else A[k,i].
    #   Then for all i,j:
    #       C_out[i,j] = beta * C_in[i,j]
    #                    + alpha * sum_{k=0..M-1} S(i,k) * B[k,j]
    #
    # This is exactly the effect of the original kernel_symm, which implements
    # C := alpha * S * B + beta * C using only the stored lower triangle of S.

    # 1. Scale C by beta.
    SCALE:
      for i, j:
        C[i, j] = beta * C[i, j]

    # 2. Symmetric matrix–matrix product using only the stored lower triangle of A.
    #    The logical symmetric element is formed on the fly to avoid ever reading
    #    the A[i,k] entries with k > i that are marked as unused (-999).
    SYMM:
      for i, k:
        if i >= k:
          s = A[i, k]
        else:
          s = A[k, i]        # use symmetric counterpart from the lower triangle
        t = alpha * s        # invariant across j for this (i,k) pair

        for j:
          C[i, j] = C[i, j] + t * B[k, j]

dependencies:
    # Each C[i,j] must be scaled by SCALE before being updated by SYMM.
    for i in [0, M), j in [0, N):
        SCALE(i, j) -> SYMM(i, *, j)

optimization:
    # --- High-level algorithmic change --------------------------------------
    # The original code updates both C[i,j] and C[k,j] inside the same (i,k)
    # iteration to exploit symmetry and maintain triangular loop bounds.
    #
    # Here we instead use the *logical* symmetric matrix S derived from A and
    # compute the row-wise GEMM-like form
    #     C[i, :] = beta * C[i, :] + alpha * sum_k S(i,k) * B[k, :]
    #
    # This keeps all writes to C confined to a single row i at a time, which:
    #   - removes cross-row dependencies,
    #   - allows straightforward parallelization over i, and
    #   - enables contiguous access to both B[k, j] and C[i, j] in the inner loop.
    #
    # The mathematical result is identical to the original kernel in real
    # arithmetic (same symmetric matrix S and same linear operation).

    # --- Loop tiling (blocking) ---------------------------------------------
    # Tile all three dimensions to improve cache reuse:
    #   - i (rows of A,C): reuse C[i, :] across many k-blocks.
    #   - k (rows of B / cols of A): reuse B[k, :] and A[:,k] across j-blocks.
    #   - j (columns of B,C): operate on contiguous slices that fit in cache
    #     and map well to SIMD registers.
    block(i, I, TI)    # I: index of i-tiles of height TI
    block(k, K, TK)    # K: index of k-tiles of height TK
    block(j, J, TJ)    # J: index of j-tiles of width TJ

    # After blocking, the intended loop structure is (schematically):
    #   for I in 0..ceil(M/TI):
    #     for i in tile(I):
    #       # (Optionally SCALE fused here per row i, see 'fuse' below)
    #       for K in 0..ceil(M/TK):
    #         for k in tile(K):
    #           s = (i >= k ? A[i,k] : A[k,i])
    #           t = alpha * s
    #           for J in 0..ceil(N/TJ):
    #             for j in tile(J):
    #               C[i,j] += t * B[k,j]

    hoist(I)           # move I to the outermost position
    hoist(K)           # next outermost: tile over k
    hoist(J)           # outer tile over j, inner j remains innermost within each tile

    # --- Parallelization ----------------------------------------------------
    # Rows of C (i dimension) are now independent in SYMM.
    # Parallelizing over outer i-tiles balances load across cores and keeps
    # each thread working on contiguous rows of C.
    parallelize(I)

    # --- Vectorization and unrolling ---------------------------------------
    # The innermost loop iterates over j, which is contiguous in memory for
    # both B[k, j] and C[i, j], making it ideal for SIMD.
    vectorize(j, VEC)  # map inner j-loop to SIMD with hardware-appropriate width
    unroll(j, 4)       # moderate unrolling to hide FMA and load latency

    # --- Scalar hoisting / strength reduction -------------------------------
    # The product t = alpha * s is invariant over j for a fixed (i,k).
    # Compilers should hoist this out of the inner j-loop automatically, but
    # this model makes that explicit via the scalar 't' assigned before the j-loop.
    # No extra directive needed; this is encoded in the SYMM computation itself.

    # --- Optional loop fusion for better locality ---------------------------
    # Define a custom optimization:
    #   fuse(L1, L2, dim):
    #     Merge the loops labeled L1 and L2 along dimension 'dim' when they share
    #     the same bounds, preserving the original intra-iteration order of
    #     statements (all L1 body statements execute before L2's for each value
    #     of 'dim').
    #
    # Here we fuse SCALE and SYMM along dimension i so that each row of C is
    # scaled once and then immediately updated, improving temporal locality on C.
    fuse(SCALE, SYMM, i)   # # custom directive as described above

/**
 * This version is stamped on May 10, 2016
 *
 * Contact:
 *   Louis-Noel Pouchet <pouchet.ohio-state.edu>
 *   Tomofumi Yuki <tomofumi.yuki.fr>
 *
 * Web address: http://polybench.sourceforge.net
 */
/* symm.c: this file is part of PolyBench/C */

#include <stdio.h>
#include <unistd.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <math.h>

/* Include polybench common header. */
#include <polybench.h>

/* Include benchmark-specific header. */
#include "symm.h"


/* Array initialization. */
static
void init_array(int m, int n,
		DATA_TYPE *alpha,
		DATA_TYPE *beta,
		DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(C,M,N,m,n),
		DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(A,M,M,m,m),
		DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(B,M,N,m,n))
{
  int i, j;

  *alpha = 1.5;
  *beta = 1.2;
  for (i = 0; i < m; i++)
    for (j = 0; j < n; j++) {
      C[i][j] = (DATA_TYPE) ((i+j) % 100) / m;
      B[i][j] = (DATA_TYPE) ((n+i-j) % 100) / m;
    }
  for (i = 0; i < m; i++) {
    for (j = 0; j <=i; j++)
      A[i][j] = (DATA_TYPE) ((i+j) % 100) / m;
    for (j = i+1; j < m; j++)
      A[i][j] = -999; //regions of arrays that should not be used
  }
}


/* DCE code. Must scan the entire live-out data.
   Can be used also to check the correctness of the output. */
static
void print_array(int m, int n,
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(C,M,N,m,n))
{
  int i, j;

  POLYBENCH_DUMP_START;
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_BEGIN("C");
  for (i = 0; i < m; i++)
    for (j = 0; j < n; j++) {
	if ((i * m + j) % 20 == 0) fprintf (POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, "\n");
	fprintf (POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, DATA_PRINTF_MODIFIER, C[i][j]);
    }
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_END("C");
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_FINISH;
}


/* Main computational kernel. The whole function will be timed,
   including the call and return. */
static
void kernel_symm[[gnu::flatten, gnu::noinline]](int m, int n,
		 DATA_TYPE alpha,
		 DATA_TYPE beta,
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(C,M,N,m,n),
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(A,M,M,m,m),
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(B,M,N,m,n))
{
  int i, j, k;
  DATA_TYPE temp2;

//BLAS PARAMS
//SIDE = 'L'
//UPLO = 'L'
// =>  Form  C := alpha*A*B + beta*C
// A is MxM
// B is MxN
// C is MxN
//note that due to Fortran array layout, the code below more closely resembles upper triangular case in BLAS
#pragma scop
   for (i = 0; i < _PB_M; i++)
      for (j = 0; j < _PB_N; j++ )
      {
        temp2 = 0;
        for (k = 0; k < i; k++) {
           C[k][j] += alpha*B[i][j] * A[i][k];
           temp2 += B[k][j] * A[i][k];
        }
        C[i][j] = beta * C[i][j] + alpha*B[i][j] * A[i][i] + alpha * temp2;
     }
#pragma endscop

}


int main(int argc, char** argv)
{
  /* Retrieve problem size. */
  int m = M;
  int n = N;

  /* Variable declaration/allocation. */
  DATA_TYPE alpha;
  DATA_TYPE beta;
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(C,DATA_TYPE,M,N,m,n);
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(A,DATA_TYPE,M,M,m,m);
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(B,DATA_TYPE,M,N,m,n);

  /* Initialize array(s). */
  init_array (m, n, &alpha, &beta,
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(C),
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A),
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(B));

  /* Start timer. */
  polybench_start_instruments;

  /* Run kernel. */
  kernel_symm (m, n,
	       alpha, beta,
	       POLYBENCH_ARRAY(C),
	       POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A),
	       POLYBENCH_ARRAY(B));

  /* Stop and print timer. */
  polybench_stop_instruments;
  polybench_print_instruments;

  /* Prevent dead-code elimination. All live-out data must be printed
     by the function call in argument. */
  polybench_prevent_dce(print_array(m, n, POLYBENCH_ARRAY(C)));

  /* Be clean. */
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(C);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(A);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(B);

  return 0;
}

domain:
    # Matrix dimensions follow the PolyBench symm kernel:
    #   A: M x M  (symmetric, lower triangle stored)
    #   B: M x N
    #   C: M x N
    i: dim in [0, M)
    j: dim in [0, N)
    k: dim in [0, M)

data:
    # A is stored in row-major order; only the lower triangle (i >= k)
    # is initialized and used. Logically we interpret A as symmetric:
    #   A_sym[i, k] = A[max(i, k), min(i, k)].
    A[i, k]: in DATA_TYPE =
        (i, k) -> i * M + k      # row-major, valid only for k <= i

    # B and C are full MxN row-major matrices.
    B[i, j]: in  DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j
    C[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j

    # 1D temporary buffers over j (columns). They are reused for each i and
    # do not change the mathematical result; they are introduced only in
    # the optimized schedule (see 'optimization' section).
    temp1[j]: tmp DATA_TYPE = (j) -> j   # holds alpha * B[i, j] for fixed i
    temp2[j]: tmp DATA_TYPE = (j) -> j   # holds sum_{k<i} A[i,k] * B[k, j]

parameters:
    alpha: DATA_TYPE
    beta:  DATA_TYPE

    # Tuning parameters (not part of the mathematical semantics):
    BM: int  # suggested block size in i (rows)  – can be left unused or 0
    BN: int  # block size in j (columns), e.g., 64–256 depending on cache
    VJ: int  # SIMD vector length in j, e.g., 4 or 8 for doubles
    UK: int  # unroll factor for k, e.g., 4

computation:
    # Logical BLAS SYMM semantics (SIDE = 'L', UPLO = 'L'):
    #   C_out = beta * C_in + alpha * Symm(A) * B,
    # where Symm(A) is the full symmetric matrix whose lower triangle is
    # stored in A:
    #   Symm(A)[i, k] = A[max(i, k), min(i, k)].
    #
    # Written explicitly to use only the stored lower triangle of A:
    #
    #   C[i, j] = beta * C[i, j]
    #             + alpha * (
    #                   A[i, i] * B[i, j]
    #                 + sum_{k=0..i-1}   A[i, k] * B[k, j]
    #                 + sum_{k=i+1..M-1} A[k, i] * B[k, j]
    #               )
    #
    # This exactly matches the PolyBench kernel, which accumulates the
    # k < i part directly for C[i, j] and the k > i part indirectly via
    # updates to C[k, j] at larger outer indices.
    for i, j:
        C[i, j] = beta * C[i, j] \
                  + alpha * (
                        A[i, i] * B[i, j]
                      + sum(k in [0, i),   A[i, k] * B[k, j])
                      + sum(k in [i+1, M), A[k, i] * B[k, j])
                  )

optimization:
    # -----------------------------------------------------------------
    # Custom optimization primitive:
    #   transform(NAME)
    # denotes an algorithmic transformation that is mathematically
    # equivalent to the 'computation' but changes loop structure and
    # introduces temporaries as described in the comments around it.
    # -----------------------------------------------------------------

    # 1. Hoist the beta scaling of C out of the main symmetric multiply.
    #
    # From:
    #   C[i,j] = beta*C[i,j] + alpha*F(i,j)
    # To:
    #   C[i,j] = beta*C[i,j]        # separate pass over C
    #   C[i,j] += alpha*F(i,j)      # main kernel no longer multiplies by beta
    #

    # simple, easily vectorizable and parallelizable scaling pass.

    #    temporary vectors to improve cache locality and reduce memory
    #    traffic. For each fixed row i:

    #   for j in [0, N):
    #       temp1[j] = alpha * B[i, j]
    #       temp2[j] = 0

    #   for k in [0, i):                 # sequential in k, triangular
    #       a_ik = A[i, k]               # hoisted out of the j-loop
    #       for j in [0, N):             # innermost, contiguous in memory
    #           # C[k, j] gets alpha * A[i,k] * B[i,j]

    #           # temp2[j] accumulates A[i,k] * B[k,j]
    #           temp2[j] += a_ik * B[k, j]
    #
    #   # Finalize row i using the diagonal and the accumulated temp2.
    #   a_ii = A[i, i]
    #   for j in [0, N):
    #       C[i, j] += a_ii * temp1[j] + alpha * temp2[j]
    #
    # Together with the separate C *= beta pass above, this is
    # algebraically identical to the specification in 'computation':
    #   each A[i,k] (i>k) contributes once to C[k,*] and once to C[i,*],
    #   exactly matching Symm(A)*B, and no element of the upper triangle
    #   A[i,k] with k>i is ever read.
    #
    # Advantages:
    #   - Inner loops run over j, the contiguous dimension of row-major
    #     B and C, enabling efficient SIMD vectorization.
    #   - A[i,k] and alpha*B[i,j] are reused across many operations
    #     (rank-1 updates), reducing loads and multiplications.
    #   - temp1 and temp2 are length-N vectors; extra memory is O(N),
    #     well within the 50% overhead budget.
    transform(symm_rank1_update_with_temp_vectors)

    #    and C and to provide a natural unit for parallel work.  After
    #    'block(j, Jb, BN)', Jb ranges over tiles and j ranges within
    #    each tile.
    block(j, Jb, BN)

    # 4. Expose parallelism over independent column tiles.
    #    - Different Jb tiles write to disjoint sets of C[*, j] and read
    #      disjoint columns of B, so they are free of data races.
    #    - The outer i loop remains sequential because rows C[k, *] are
    #      updated across multiple i values (reduction-like dependence).

    #    - With the i–k–j ordering from the transform above and row-

    #      C[i, j], temp1[j], and temp2[j] with unit stride.
    #    - VJ should match the SIMD width (e.g., 4 or 8 doubles).
    vectorize(j, VJ)

    #    parallelism and reduce loop control overhead within each
    #    (i, Jb) tile. The triangular bound (k < i) is preserved.
    unroll(k, UK)

    #    dependency pattern on C:
    #      C[k, j] accumulates contributions from all i > k.
    #    We *do not* apply parallelize(i); any parallelization across i
    #    would require an explicit reduction scheme on C.

domain:
    # Matrix dimensions (PolyBench: M == m, N == n)
    i: dim in [0, M)          # row index of A and C
    j: dim in [0, N)          # column index of B and C
    k: dim in [0, M)          # reduction index over rows of B / columns of A

data:
    # A is an MxM symmetric matrix stored in row-major *lower-triangular* form:
    #   A[i, k] is valid only for k <= i; elements with k > i are never read.
    A[i, k]: in DATA_TYPE = (i, k) -> i * M + k        # row-major, lower triangle used

    # B is an MxN dense matrix, row-major.
    B[i, j]: in DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j        # row-major

    # C is an MxN dense matrix, row-major, updated in place.

    # Optional logical view (no extra storage):
    # S[i, k] = A[i, k]  if k <= i
    #         = A[k, i]  if k >  i
    # S is the full symmetric matrix implied by the stored lower triangle of A.
    # All computations below are expressed directly in terms of A to avoid
    # touching the unused upper triangle.
    #S[i, k]: virtual DATA_TYPE  # symmetric view over A (lower-triangular storage)

parameters:
    alpha: DATA_TYPE
    beta: DATA_TYPE
    M: int
    N: int

    # Tuning parameters for the optimized kernel (no semantic effect):
    TI: int    # tile size in i (rows of A,C)
    TJ: int    # tile size in j (cols of B,C)
    TK: int    # tile size in k (rows of B / columns of A)
    VJ: int    # vector width along j for SIMD
    UK: int    # unroll factor for the k-reduction inside a tile

computation:
    # High-level mathematical specification derived from the kernel:
    #   SIDE = 'L', UPLO = 'L'
    #   C := alpha * A_sym * B + beta * C
    # where A_sym is the symmetric matrix defined by A's lower triangle.
    #
    # For each output element C[i, j], the symmetric product can be written
    # without ever reading A's upper triangle as:
    #
    #   C[i, j] = beta * C[i, j]
    #             + alpha * [ sum_{k = 0..i}   A[i, k] * B[k, j]
    #                        + sum_{k = i+1..M-1} A[k, i] * B[k, j] ]
    #
    # The first sum uses row i of the stored lower triangle (including the
    # diagonal), the second sum uses column i of the strictly lower part.

    for i, j:
        C[i, j] =
            beta * C[i, j]
            + alpha * (
                  sum(k in [0, i+1),   A[i, k] * B[k, j])      # k <= i
                + sum(k in [i+1, M),   A[k, i] * B[k, j])      # k >  i
              )

dependencies:
    # Each (i, j) computes C[i, j] exactly once from the input values of
    # A, B, and the original C[i, j]. No C[i, j] depends on any other
    # C[i', j'] with (i', j') != (i, j).
    #
    # The only reductions are over k inside each (i, j), using a private
    # accumulator. Therefore:
    #   - All (i, j) iterations are mutually independent.
    #   - The k-reductions can be freely reordered or blocked, provided
    #     they remain associative and use a private accumulator per (i, j).

optimization:
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # 1. Cache-friendly 3D blocking (tiling)
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # Tile the i (rows of A,C), j (cols of B,C), and k (rows of B)
    # dimensions. TK should be chosen so that a tile of B[Kk, Jj] and the
