domain:
    i: dim in [0, N)
    j: dim in [0, N)
    k: dim in [0, M)

data:
    # A and B are N x M, row-major
    A[i, k]: in DATA_TYPE = (i, k) -> i * M + k
    B[i, k]: in DATA_TYPE = (i, k) -> i * M + k

    # C is N x N, row-major. Only the lower triangular part (j <= i) is updated.
    C[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j

parameters:
    alpha: DATA_TYPE
    beta:  DATA_TYPE

    # Tunable transformation parameters (chosen empirically for a given machine)
    TI: int  # tile size for i (rows of C)
    TJ: int  # tile size for j (cols / lower-triangular index of C)
    TK: int  # tile size for k (inner-product dimension)
    VK: int  # SIMD width for vectorization along k
    # (Typical starting points on a modern x64: TI ≈ 128, TJ ≈ 128, TK ≈ 256, VK = hardware SIMD width)

computation:
    # Symmetric rank-2k update on the lower triangular part of C
    #
    # BLAS SYR2K semantics with UPLO='L', TRANS='N':
    #   C := beta * C + alpha * A * B^T + alpha * B * A^T,
    #   but only the lower triangle (j <= i) is stored and updated.
    #
    # For all 0 <= j <= i < N:
    #   C[i, j] = beta * C[i, j]
    #             + alpha * Σ_{k=0..M-1} ( A[j, k] * B[i, k] + B[j, k] * A[i, k] )
    #
    # Elements with j > i are not touched by the kernel and keep their input values.
    for i in [0, N):
        for j in [0, N):
            if j <= i:
                C[i, j] = beta * C[i, j] +
                          alpha * sum(k in [0, M),
                                      A[j, k] * B[i, k] +
                                      B[j, k] * A[i, k])

optimization:
    # 1) Cache blocking (tiling) in all three logical dimensions.
    #    The goal is to work on submatrices that fit in cache:
    #      - A-panel:  rows j in a J-tile, columns k in a K-tile
    #      - B-panel:  rows i in an I-tile, columns k in a K-tile
    #      - C-tile:   rows i in an I-tile, cols j in a J-tile (lower triangular subset)
    #
    #    This reduces capacity and conflict misses by increasing temporal reuse of A, B, and C.
    block(i, I, TI)   # tile the row dimension of C into outer tiles I of size TI
    block(j, J, TJ)   # tile the column dimension of C into outer tiles J of size TJ
    block(k, K, TK)   # tile the reduction dimension k into panels K of size TK

    # After blocking, we conceptually obtain a loop nest of the form
    #   for I, J, K:
    #     for i in tile I:
    #       for j in tile J:
    #         if j <= i:
    #           C[i, j] += alpha * Σ_{k in tile K} ...
    #
    # Hoist the tile loops to the outermost level so that we have a clean 3-level
    # blocked structure with micro-kernels operating inside the I,J,K tiles.
    hoist(I)
    hoist(J)
    hoist(K)

    # 2) Parallelism.
    #    Different (I, J) tiles cover disjoint subsets of C’s lower triangle:
    #      - Each (i, j) with j <= i is updated in exactly one tile.
    #      - The reduction in k is fully local to that (i, j).
    #    Therefore there are no cross-tile dependencies and tiles can execute in parallel.
    parallelize(I)       # distribute row-tiles of C across threads
    # Optionally, J can also be parallelized for very large N if load imbalance from the
    # triangular shape is acceptable:
    # parallelize(J)

    # 3) Vectorization and unrolling along the reduction dimension k.
    #    For fixed (i, j) (or a small block of them), accesses are:
    #      A[j, k], B[j, k], A[i, k], B[i, k] with k varying.
    #    Since arrays are row-major, varying k gives unit-stride accesses, ideal for SIMD.
    vectorize(k, VK)     # generate SIMD operations over the k-dimension
    unroll(k, 4)         # unroll the inner k-loop to increase ILP and hide latency

    # 4) Exploit invariants in the arithmetic to reduce work.
    #    For fixed (i, k), the quantities A[i, k], B[i, k] and alpha are invariant over all j.
    #    An efficient implementation can:
    #      - precompute tAi_k = alpha * A[i, k]
    #      - precompute tBi_k = alpha * B[i, k]
    #      - and then use:
    #          C[i, j] += A[j, k] * tBi_k + B[j, k] * tAi_k
    #        for all j in the current J-tile with j <= i.
    #    This avoids redundant multiplications by alpha inside the j-loop and
    #    keeps repeated per-(i,k) values in registers while streaming over j.

    # 5) Respect and exploit symmetry / triangular storage.
    #    The condition "if j <= i" precisely encodes the lower-triangular update:
    #      - no work is done for j > i (upper triangle),
    #      - upper-triangular entries of C remain equal to their initialized values.
    #    Implementations can use this knowledge to:
    #      - skip full J-tiles that lie entirely above the main diagonal, and
    #      - clip partially intersecting tiles to only iterate j-ranges with j <= i.
--- END OF MODEL: syr2k-02 ---

--- START OF MODEL: syr2k-03 ---
domain:
    # Problem sizes as in the C code: N (n), M (m).
    i: dim in [0, N)
    j: dim in [0, N)
    k: dim in [0, M)

data:
    # A is N x M, row-major: A[i][k] in C.
    A[i, k]: in DATA_TYPE = (i, k) -> i * M + k  # Row-major

    # B is N x M, row-major: B[i][k] in C.
    B[i, k]: in DATA_TYPE = (i, k) -> i * M + k  # Row-major

    # C is N x N, row-major: C[i][j] in C. Only the lower triangle (j <= i) is updated.
    C[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j  # Row-major

    # Temporary 1D buffers used inside kernel_syr2k.
    # They store alpha-scaled copies of row i of A and B and are reused across all j for that i.
    # Size is O(M), so the extra memory is negligible (< 50% of original footprint).
    alphaA[k]: temp DATA_TYPE = (k) -> k  # scratch for alpha * A[i, k], length M
    alphaB[k]: temp DATA_TYPE = (k) -> k  # scratch for alpha * B[i, k], length M

parameters:
    alpha: DATA_TYPE
    beta:  DATA_TYPE

    # Tuning parameters for performance (passed as compile-time or run-time constants).
    TI: int  # tile size for i (row) dimension, controls cache behavior and parallel granularity
    TK: int  # tile size for k (reduction) dimension, chosen for L1/L2 reuse
    VEC_K: int  # SIMD vector width along k (e.g., 8 for AVX2 double, 16 for AVX-512 float)
    UJ: int  # unroll factor for the j-loop (e.g., 2–8)


computation:
    # Semantics:
    #   For 0 <= j <= i < N:
    #     C[i, j] = beta * C[i, j] +
    #               alpha * sum_{k=0..M-1} ( A[j, k] * B[i, k] + B[j, k] * A[i, k] )
    #   For j > i, C[i, j] is left unchanged (upper triangle is not updated).
    #
    # Optimized formulation:
    #   For each row i of C, we:
    #     1. Precompute alphaA[k] = alpha * A[i, k] and alphaB[k] = alpha * B[i, k] once.
    #     2. For each j <= i, compute C[i, j] using these temporaries and accumulate over k.
    #
    # This reduces the number of multiplications by hoisting the alpha * A[i,k] and
    # alpha * B[i,k] products out of the (i, j, k) inner loops and improves locality.

    for i in [0, N):
        # Step 1: precompute scaled row i of A and B.
        # This loop has contiguous accesses to A[i, k] and B[i, k] (row-major).
        for k in [0, M):
            alphaA[k] = alpha * A[i, k]
            alphaB[k] = alpha * B[i, k]

        # Step 2: update only the lower triangle (j <= i) of C’s i-th row.
        # C[i, j] is read once and written once; all contributions along k are kept
        # in a register accumulator in the implementation.
        for j in [0, N):
            if j <= i:
                C[i, j] =
                    beta * C[i, j] +
                    sum(k in [0, M)) (
                        A[j, k] * alphaB[k] +
                        B[j, k] * alphaA[k]
                    )
            # For j > i, C[i, j] is unchanged, preserving original behavior.


optimization:
    #-------------------------------------------------------------
    # Parallelism
    #-------------------------------------------------------------
    # Each (i, j) pair in the lower triangle is independent, since C[i, j] is
    # only updated using A[*][*], B[*][*], and its own previous value.
    # We process rows (or row tiles) in parallel. The temporary buffers alphaA
    # and alphaB are treated as thread-private so that there are no races.
    #
    # Effective schedule:
    #   for I (row tiles), in parallel
    #     for i in tile I
    #       precompute alphaA, alphaB for row i
    #       for j <= i
    #         reduction over k
    block(i, I, TI)     # strip-mine i into tiles of size TI: i = I * TI + i_inner
    parallelize(I)      # distribute row tiles across threads
    hoist(I)            # make I (row-tile loop) outermost for coarse-grain parallelism

    #-------------------------------------------------------------
    # Blocking / tiling in the reduction dimension
    #-------------------------------------------------------------
    # Block k to improve cache reuse of:
    #   - A[j, k] and B[j, k] rows (for fixed j),
    #   - alphaA[k] and alphaB[k] (for fixed i),
    # while keeping k contiguous inside each tile for vectorization.
    #
    # Conceptual transformed reduction:
    #   for each (i, j with j <= i):
    #     acc = beta * C[i, j]
    #     for K in [0, M) step TK:
    #       for k in [K, min(K + TK, M)):
    #         acc += A[j, k] * alphaB[k] + B[j, k] * alphaA[k]
    #     C[i, j] = acc
    block(k, K, TK)     # k = K * TK + k_inner; TK tuned (e.g., 64–256) to fit L1/L2

    #-------------------------------------------------------------
    # Loop ordering / scheduling
    #-------------------------------------------------------------
    # Within each row tile I, the preferred loop nest is:
    #   for i in tile I:
    #     precompute alphaA/alphaB over full k
    #     for j in [0, i]:             # lower triangle per row
    #       for K:                     # k-tiles
    #         for k in tile K:         # inner-most reduction
    #           ...
    #
    # We keep k_inner as the innermost loop to enable efficient SIMD.
    # No additional interchange is strictly necessary if this order is used.

    #-------------------------------------------------------------
    # Vectorization
    #-------------------------------------------------------------
    # The inner k loop has four contiguous streams:
    #   A[j, k], B[j, k], alphaA[k], alphaB[k]
    # so it is naturally vectorizable. We explicitly request vectorization
    # along k with a tunable SIMD width VEC_K.
    vectorize(k, VEC_K)

    #-------------------------------------------------------------
    # Unrolling / register blocking
    #-------------------------------------------------------------
    # Unroll the j loop (over the lower triangle of row i) to keep several
    # C[i, j] values in registers simultaneously. This:
    #   - amortizes loads of alphaA/alphaB across multiple accumulators,
    #   - increases instruction-level parallelism (ILP).
    #
    # The triangular condition (j <= i) is handled either by restricting the
    # iteration bounds per row or by masking within the unrolled body.
    unroll(j, UJ)

    #-------------------------------------------------------------
    # Arithmetic simplification (comment, not a separate directive)
    #-------------------------------------------------------------
    # By using alphaA[k] = alpha * A[i, k] and alphaB[k] = alpha * B[i, k],
    # the inner update
    #     A[j, k] * alpha * B[i, k] + B[j, k] * alpha * A[i, k]
    # is evaluated as
    #     A[j, k] * alphaB[k] + B[j, k] * alphaA[k]
    # This reduces the number of multiplications from ~4 per (i, j, k) to
    # about 2 per (i, j, k) plus 2 per (i, k) for the precomputation,
    # significantly lowering arithmetic cost while preserving exact semantics.
--- END OF MODEL: syr2k-03 ---

    C[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j

    M: int           # problem size in the "K" dimension

    beta:  DATA_TYPE

    TJ: int          # tile size along j (columns of C, still only j <= i used)
    TK: int          # tile size along k (reduction dimension)
    VEC_WIDTH: int   # SIMD width used for vectorizing the k-loop
    UNROLL_K: int    # unrolling factor for the innermost k-loop

computation:
    # SYR2K on the lower triangle (UPLO = 'L', TRANS = 'N'):
    #   For all 0 <= j <= i < N:
    #     C[i, j] = beta * C[i, j]
    #               + alpha * sum_{k=0..M-1} ( A[j, k] * B[i, k] + B[j, k] * A[i, k] )
    #
    # Factoring alpha outside the sum reduces the number of multiplications by alpha
    # from O(N^2 * M) to O(N^2) and allows a single scalar multiply per C[i, j].
    for i in [0, N):
        for j in [0, i+1):         # lower-triangular domain: j <= i
            C[i, j] =
                beta * C[i, j]
                + alpha * sum(k in [0, M),
                               A[j, k] * B[i, k] +
                               B[j, k] * A[i, k])

optimization:
    # NOTE: All optimizations preserve the lower-triangular restriction j <= i.
    # After tiling, iterations with j > i inside a tile are not instantiated
    # (or are guarded by a j <= i condition in the generated code).

    # 1. Block the spatial (i, j) dimensions so that we work on C submatrices

    block(k, Kk, TK)        # Kk indexes tiles in the M dimension

    #    - Process tiles in (Ii, Jj) first (spatial blocking of C).
    #    - For each (Ii, Jj) tile, iterate over Kk tiles and then over the
    #      inner k within each Kk tile.
    #    This gives unit-stride access along k to A[*, k] and B[*, k] (row-major),
    #    and maximizes reuse of each A/B Kk-panel across all (i, j) in the tile.
    hoist(Ii)
    hoist(Jj)
    hoist(Kk)

    #    - Different Ii-tiles update disjoint sets of rows of C.
    #    - A and B are read-only, so there are no write–write or write–read hazards.
    parallelize(Ii)

    # 5. Vectorization and unrolling along the reduction dimension:
    #    - Vectorizing over k exploits contiguous row-major storage of A and B.

    vectorize(k, VEC_WIDTH)
    unroll(k, UNROLL_K)

parameters:

    # Symmetric rank-2k update on the lower triangular part of C.
    #
    # Original kernel (for 0 <= j <= i < N):
    #   C[i][j] *= beta;

    #       C[i][j] += A[j][k]*alpha*B[i][k] + B[j][k]*alpha*A[i][k];
    #

/* syr2k.c: this file is part of PolyBench/C */

#include <stdio.h>
#include <unistd.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <math.h>

/* Include polybench common header. */
#include <polybench.h>

/* Include benchmark-specific header. */
#include "syr2k.h"


/* Array initialization. */
static
void init_array(int n, int m,
		DATA_TYPE *alpha,
		DATA_TYPE *beta,
		DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(C,N,N,n,n),
		DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(A,N,M,n,m),
		DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(B,N,M,n,m))
{
  int i, j;

  *alpha = 1.5;
  *beta = 1.2;
  for (i = 0; i < n; i++)
    for (j = 0; j < m; j++) {
      A[i][j] = (DATA_TYPE) ((i*j+1)%n) / n;
      B[i][j] = (DATA_TYPE) ((i*j+2)%m) / m;
    }
  for (i = 0; i < n; i++)
    for (j = 0; j < n; j++) {
      C[i][j] = (DATA_TYPE) ((i*j+3)%n) / m;
    }
}


/* DCE code. Must scan the entire live-out data.
   Can be used also to check the correctness of the output. */
static
void print_array(int n,
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(C,N,N,n,n))
{
  int i, j;

  POLYBENCH_DUMP_START;
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_BEGIN("C");
  for (i = 0; i < n; i++)
    for (j = 0; j < n; j++) {
	if ((i * n + j) % 20 == 0) fprintf (POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, "\n");
	fprintf (POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, DATA_PRINTF_MODIFIER, C[i][j]);
    }
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_END("C");
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_FINISH;
}


/* Main computational kernel. The whole function will be timed,
   including the call and return. */
static
void kernel_syr2k[[gnu::flatten, gnu::noinline]](int n, int m,
		  DATA_TYPE alpha,
		  DATA_TYPE beta,
		  DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(C,N,N,n,n),
		  DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(A,N,M,n,m),
		  DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(B,N,M,n,m))
{
  int i, j, k;

//BLAS PARAMS
//UPLO  = 'L'
//TRANS = 'N'
//A is NxM
//B is NxM
//C is NxN
#pragma scop
  for (i = 0; i < _PB_N; i++) {
    for (j = 0; j <= i; j++)
      C[i][j] *= beta;
    for (k = 0; k < _PB_M; k++)
      for (j = 0; j <= i; j++)
	{
	  C[i][j] += A[j][k]*alpha*B[i][k] + B[j][k]*alpha*A[i][k];
	}
  }
#pragma endscop

}


int main(int argc, char** argv)
{
  /* Retrieve problem size. */
  int n = N;
  int m = M;

  /* Variable declaration/allocation. */
  DATA_TYPE alpha;
  DATA_TYPE beta;
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(C,DATA_TYPE,N,N,n,n);
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(A,DATA_TYPE,N,M,n,m);
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(B,DATA_TYPE,N,M,n,m);

  /* Initialize array(s). */
  init_array (n, m, &alpha, &beta,
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(C),
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A),
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(B));

  /* Start timer. */
  polybench_start_instruments;

  /* Run kernel. */
  kernel_syr2k (n, m,
		alpha, beta,
		POLYBENCH_ARRAY(C),
		POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A),
		POLYBENCH_ARRAY(B));

  /* Stop and print timer. */
  polybench_stop_instruments;
  polybench_print_instruments;

  /* Prevent dead-code elimination. All live-out data must be printed
     by the function call in argument. */
  polybench_prevent_dce(print_array(n, POLYBENCH_ARRAY(C)));

  /* Be clean. */
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(C);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(A);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(B);

  return 0;
}

    #-------------------------------------------------------------
    # Each (i, j) pair in the lower triangle is independent, since C[i, j] is
    # only updated using A[*][*], B[*][*], and its own previous value.
    # We process rows (or row tiles) in parallel. The temporary buffers alphaA
    # and alphaB are treated as thread-private so that there are no races.
    #
    # Effective schedule:
    #   for I (row tiles), in parallel
    #     for i in tile I
    #       precompute alphaA, alphaB for row i
    #       for j <= i
    #         reduction over k
    block(i, I, TI)     # strip-mine i into tiles of size TI: i = I * TI + i_inner
    parallelize(I)      # distribute row tiles across threads
    hoist(I)            # make I (row-tile loop) outermost for coarse-grain parallelism

    #-------------------------------------------------------------
    # Blocking / tiling in the reduction dimension
    #-------------------------------------------------------------
    # Block k to improve cache reuse of:
    #   - A[j, k] and B[j, k] rows (for fixed j),
    #   - alphaA[k] and alphaB[k] (for fixed i),
    # while keeping k contiguous inside each tile for vectorization.
    #
    # Conceptual transformed reduction:
    #   for each (i, j with j <= i):
    #     acc = beta * C[i, j]
    #     for K in [0, M) step TK:
    #       for k in [K, min(K + TK, M)):
    #         acc += A[j, k] * alphaB[k] + B[j, k] * alphaA[k]
    #     C[i, j] = acc
    block(k, K, TK)     # k = K * TK + k_inner; TK tuned (e.g., 64–256) to fit L1/L2

    #-------------------------------------------------------------
    # Loop ordering / scheduling
    #-------------------------------------------------------------
    # Within each row tile I, the preferred loop nest is:
    #   for i in tile I:
    #     precompute alphaA/alphaB over full k
    #     for j in [0, i]:             # lower triangle per row
    #       for K:                     # k-tiles
    #         for k in tile K:         # inner-most reduction
    #           ...
    #
    # We keep k_inner as the innermost loop to enable efficient SIMD.
    # No additional interchange is strictly necessary if this order is used.

    #-------------------------------------------------------------
    # Vectorization
    #-------------------------------------------------------------
    # The inner k loop has four contiguous streams:
    #   A[j, k], B[j, k], alphaA[k], alphaB[k]
    # so it is naturally vectorizable. We explicitly request vectorization
    # along k with a tunable SIMD width VEC_K.
    vectorize(k, VEC_K)

    #-------------------------------------------------------------
    # Unrolling / register blocking
    #-------------------------------------------------------------
    # Unroll the j loop (over the lower triangle of row i) to keep several
    # C[i, j] values in registers simultaneously. This:
    #   - amortizes loads of alphaA/alphaB across multiple accumulators,
    #   - increases instruction-level parallelism (ILP).
    #
    # The triangular condition (j <= i) is handled either by restricting the
    # iteration bounds per row or by masking within the unrolled body.
    unroll(j, UJ)

    #-------------------------------------------------------------
    # Arithmetic simplification (comment, not a separate directive)
    #-------------------------------------------------------------
    # By using alphaA[k] = alpha * A[i, k] and alphaB[k] = alpha * B[i, k],
    # the inner update
    #     A[j, k] * alpha * B[i, k] + B[j, k] * alpha * A[i, k]
    # is evaluated as
    #     A[j, k] * alphaB[k] + B[j, k] * alphaA[k]
    # This reduces the number of multiplications from ~4 per (i, j, k) to
    # about 2 per (i, j, k) plus 2 per (i, k) for the precomputation,
    # significantly lowering arithmetic cost while preserving exact semantics.
--- END OF MODEL: syr2k-03 ---

--- START OF MODEL: syr2k-04 ---
domain:
    i: dim in [0, N)
    j: dim in [0, N)
    k: dim in [0, M)

data:
    # A and B are N x M, row-major (same as in the C code)
    A[i, k]: in DATA_TYPE  = (i, k) -> i * M + k
    B[i, k]: in DATA_TYPE  = (i, k) -> i * M + k

    # C is N x N, row-major; only the lower triangle j <= i is updated.
    C[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j

parameters:
    N: int           # problem size in the symmetric dimension
    M: int           # problem size in the "K" dimension
    alpha: DATA_TYPE
    beta:  DATA_TYPE

    # Tunable blocking / vectorization parameters
    TI: int          # tile size along i (rows of C)
    TJ: int          # tile size along j (columns of C, still only j <= i used)
    TK: int          # tile size along k (reduction dimension)
    VEC_WIDTH: int   # SIMD width used for vectorizing the k-loop
    UNROLL_K: int    # unrolling factor for the innermost k-loop

computation:
    # SYR2K on the lower triangle (UPLO = 'L', TRANS = 'N'):
    #   For all 0 <= j <= i < N:
    #     C[i, j] = beta * C[i, j]
    #               + alpha * sum_{k=0..M-1} ( A[j, k] * B[i, k] + B[j, k] * A[i, k] )
    #
    # Factoring alpha outside the sum reduces the number of multiplications by alpha
    # from O(N^2 * M) to O(N^2) and allows a single scalar multiply per C[i, j].
    for i in [0, N):
        for j in [0, i+1):         # lower-triangular domain: j <= i
            C[i, j] =
                beta * C[i, j]
                + alpha * sum(k in [0, M),
                               A[j, k] * B[i, k] +
                               B[j, k] * A[i, k])

optimization:
    # NOTE: All optimizations preserve the lower-triangular restriction j <= i.
    # After tiling, iterations with j > i inside a tile are not instantiated
    # (or are guarded by a j <= i condition in the generated code).

    # 1. Block the spatial (i, j) dimensions so that we work on C submatrices
    #    that fit in cache and can reuse rows of A and B across multiple C[i, j].
    block(i, Ii, TI)        # Ii indexes tiles of rows of C/A/B
    block(j, Jj, TJ)        # Jj indexes tiles of columns of C (still only j <= i used)

    # 2. Block the reduction dimension k so that for each (Ii, Jj) C-tile we
    #    reuse the corresponding A/B panels across many updates to C.
    block(k, Kk, TK)        # Kk indexes tiles in the M dimension

    # 3. Loop ordering:
    #    - Process tiles in (Ii, Jj) first (spatial blocking of C).
    #    - For each (Ii, Jj) tile, iterate over Kk tiles and then over the
    #      inner k within each Kk tile.
    #    This gives unit-stride access along k to A[*, k] and B[*, k] (row-major),
    #    and maximizes reuse of each A/B Kk-panel across all (i, j) in the tile.
    hoist(Ii)
    hoist(Jj)
    hoist(Kk)

    # 4. Parallelization:
    #    - Different Ii-tiles update disjoint sets of rows of C.
    #    - A and B are read-only, so there are no write–write or write–read hazards.
    parallelize(Ii)

    # 5. Vectorization and unrolling along the reduction dimension:
    #    - Vectorizing over k exploits contiguous row-major storage of A and B.
    #    - The reduction over k is implemented by a vector reduction in registers.
    vectorize(k, VEC_WIDTH)
    unroll(k, UNROLL_K)

    # 6. Implicit arithmetic optimizations enabled by the formulation:
    #    - The sum(k, ...) construct means each C[i, j] is accumulated in a
    #      scalar (or a small set of vector) registers across all k in a tile,
    #      and C[i, j] is written back to memory only once.
    #    - The expression beta * C[i, j] + alpha * sum(k, ...) ensures that
    #      multiplication by alpha and beta is performed once per C[i, j],
    #      not once per (i, j, k) iteration.
    #    - Inside the innermost micro-kernel, the code generator can hoist
    #      A[i, k] and B[i, k] into scalar temporaries for a fixed (i, k) and
    #      reuse them across multiple j in the same (Ii, Jj, Kk) tile.
--- END OF MODEL: syr2k-04 ---

--- START OF MODEL: syr2k-05 ---
domain:
    # Matrix dimensions (N: order of C, N x M: shapes of A and B)
    i: dim in [0, N)        # row index of C, A, B
    j: dim in [0, N)        # column index of C (only j <= i updated)
    k: dim in [0, M)        # inner dimension

data:
    # Row-major layouts, matching PolyBench default macros
    A[i, k]: in DATA_TYPE = (i, k) -> i * M + k      # A is N x M
    B[i, k]: in DATA_TYPE = (i, k) -> i * M + k      # B is N x M
    C[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j   # C is N x N, full storage

parameters:
    alpha: DATA_TYPE
    beta: DATA_TYPE

    # Tunable optimization parameters (chosen for the target x64 machine)
    TI: int        # tile size for i (rows of C)
    TJ: int        # tile size for j (columns of C within a row block)
    TK: int        # tile size for k (reduction dimension)
    VEC_K: int     # SIMD width along k (e.g., 4 or 8 for AVX/AVX-512)
    UNROLL_K: int  # unroll factor along k inside each k-tile

computation:
    # Symmetric rank-2k update on the lower triangular part of C.
    #
    # Original kernel (for 0 <= j <= i < N):
    #   C[i][j] *= beta;
    #   for k in [0, M):
    #       C[i][j] += A[j][k]*alpha*B[i][k] + B[j][k]*alpha*A[i][k];
    #
    # Algebraically, this is:
    #   C_ij = beta * C_ij + sum_k alpha * (A_jk * B_ik + B_jk * A_ik)
    #        = beta * C_ij + alpha * sum_k (A_jk * B_ik + B_jk * A_ik)
    #
    # Upper-triangular entries j > i are left unchanged.
    UPDATE:
        for i in [0, N):
            for j in [0, i+1):      # 0 <= j <= i  (lower triangle only)
                C[i, j] = beta * C[i, j] +
                          alpha * sum(k in [0, M),
                                      A[j, k] * B[i, k] +
                                      B[j, k] * A[i, k])

optimization:
    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 1. Parallelism over independent rows (tiles of i)
    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Rows of C are independent in this formulation: each (i, j) with j <= i
    # depends only on:
    #   - its initial value C[i, j]
    #   - row i of A and B, and row j of A and B
    # There are no cross-row write-after-write or read-after-write hazards.
    #
    # Tile i first, then parallelize tiles across cores.
    block(i, I, TI)          # i = I * TI + i', with i' in [0, TI)
    parallelize(I)           # distribute i-tiles across threads

    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 2. Cache blocking in j (output band) and k (reduction dimension)
    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Work on small bands of the lower triangle of C to keep them in cache
    # while streaming through corresponding panels of A and B.
    block(j, J, TJ)          # j = J * TJ + j', j' in [0, TJ)
    # For each (I, i') we only admit those (J, j') such that j <= i
    # (i.e., tiles are clipped at the diagonal to stay in the lower triangle).

    # Tile the reduction dimension k to improve temporal locality on A and B
    # and to match L2/L3 cache sizes.
    block(k, K, TK)          # k = K * TK + k', k' in [0, TK)

    # Effective loop nesting from outermost to innermost becomes:
    #   I (parallel over row tiles)
    #     i' in [0, TI)
    #       J over j-tiles with j <= i
    #         j' in [0, TJ)   # still constrained by j <= i
    #           K in [0, ceil(M/TK))
    #             k' in [0, TK)
    #
    # For a fixed (i, j) within a tile, the full reduction over k is
    # implemented as a sum over K-tiles and their inner k', but the
    # mathematical result is unchanged.

    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 3. Scalar replacement / register accumulation for C
    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Instead of updating C[i, j] in memory at every k step (as in the
    # original code), hold the value in a scalar accumulator across the
    # entire k-reduction (over all K and k'), then write back once:
    #
    #   acc = beta * C[i, j]
    #   for K, k' in tiles:
    #       k = K * TK + k'
    #       acc += alpha * (A[j, k] * B[i, k] + B[j, k] * A[i, k])
    #   C[i, j] = acc
    #
    # This reduces C traffic from O(N^2 * M) loads/stores to O(N^2) and
    # matches the high-level assignment in UPDATE.
    # (Custom directive; semantics explained above.)
    #scalar_replacement(C[i, j])

    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 4. Algebraic simplification of the inner expression
    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    # The computation in UPDATE already reflects factoring alpha outside the
    # k-reduction:
    #   sum_k (A[j,k]*alpha*B[i,k] + B[j,k]*alpha*A[i,k])
    # = alpha * sum_k (A[j,k]*B[i,k] + B[j,k]*A[i,k])
    #
    # This turns two multiplications by alpha per (i, j, k) into a single
    # multiplication by alpha per (i, j), after the reduction, cutting the
    # number of FP multiplies in the inner loop roughly in half.
    #factor_out(alpha, k)     # conceptual directive, already applied in UPDATE

    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 5. SIMD and unrolling along k
    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    # After blocking, use the innermost k'-loop as the SIMD dimension. With
    # row-major storage and k varying fastest, accesses:
    #   A[j, k], B[j, k], A[i, k], B[i, k]
    # are unit-stride, well-suited for vector loads/stores.
    vectorize(k, VEC_K)      # generate vector code over k' within each TK-tile

    # Unroll the k'-loop inside each tile to increase ILP and hide FMA latency.
    unroll(k, UNROLL_K)

    # Optionally, lightly unroll j' inside each tile to reduce loop overhead
    # and help the compiler schedule multiple accumulators in parallel:
    #unroll(j, 2)
--- END OF MODEL: syr2k-05 ---

/**

/* syrk.c: this file is part of PolyBench/C */

#include <stdio.h>
#include <unistd.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <math.h>

/* Include polybench common header. */
#include <polybench.h>

/* Include benchmark-specific header. */
#include "syrk.h"


/* Array initialization. */
static
void init_array(int n, int m,
		DATA_TYPE *alpha,
		DATA_TYPE *beta,
		DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(C,N,N,n,n),
		DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(A,N,M,n,m))
{
  int i, j;

  *alpha = 1.5;
  *beta = 1.2;
  for (i = 0; i < n; i++)
    for (j = 0; j < m; j++)
      A[i][j] = (DATA_TYPE) ((i*j+1)%n) / n;
  for (i = 0; i < n; i++)
    for (j = 0; j < n; j++)
      C[i][j] = (DATA_TYPE) ((i*j+2)%m) / m;
}


/* DCE code. Must scan the entire live-out data.
   Can be used also to check the correctness of the output. */
static
void print_array(int n,
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(C,N,N,n,n))
{
  int i, j;

  POLYBENCH_DUMP_START;
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_BEGIN("C");
  for (i = 0; i < n; i++)
    for (j = 0; j < n; j++) {
	if ((i * n + j) % 20 == 0) fprintf (POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, "\n");
	fprintf (POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, DATA_PRINTF_MODIFIER, C[i][j]);
    }
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_END("C");
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_FINISH;
}


/* Main computational kernel. The whole function will be timed,
   including the call and return. */
static
void kernel_syrk[[gnu::flatten, gnu::noinline]](int n, int m,
		 DATA_TYPE alpha,
		 DATA_TYPE beta,
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(C,N,N,n,n),
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(A,N,M,n,m))
{
  int i, j, k;

//BLAS PARAMS
//TRANS = 'N'
//UPLO  = 'L'
// =>  Form  C := alpha*A*A**T + beta*C.
//A is NxM
//C is NxN
#pragma scop
  for (i = 0; i < _PB_N; i++) {
    for (j = 0; j <= i; j++)
      C[i][j] *= beta;
    for (k = 0; k < _PB_M; k++) {
      for (j = 0; j <= i; j++)
        C[i][j] += alpha * A[i][k] * A[j][k];
    }
  }
#pragma endscop

}


int main(int argc, char** argv)
{
  /* Retrieve problem size. */
  int n = N;
  int m = M;

  /* Variable declaration/allocation. */
  DATA_TYPE alpha;
  DATA_TYPE beta;
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(C,DATA_TYPE,N,N,n,n);
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(A,DATA_TYPE,N,M,n,m);

  /* Initialize array(s). */
  init_array (n, m, &alpha, &beta, POLYBENCH_ARRAY(C), POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A));

  /* Start timer. */
  polybench_start_instruments;

  /* Run kernel. */
  kernel_syrk (n, m, alpha, beta, POLYBENCH_ARRAY(C), POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A));

  /* Stop and print timer. */
  polybench_stop_instruments;
  polybench_print_instruments;

  /* Prevent dead-code elimination. All live-out data must be printed
     by the function call in argument. */
  polybench_prevent_dce(print_array(n, POLYBENCH_ARRAY(C)));

  /* Be clean. */
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(C);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(A);

  return 0;
}

domain:
    # Matrix dimensions (problem sizes)
    i: dim in [0, N)
    j: dim in [0, N)
    k: dim in [0, M)

data:
    # A is N x M, stored row-major: A[i][k]
    A[i, k]: in DATA_TYPE  = (i, k) -> i * M + k

    # C is N x N, stored row-major: C[i][j]
    # Only the lower triangle (j <= i) is updated by the kernel;
    # the upper triangle remains equal to its initialized values.
    C[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j

parameters:
    alpha: DATA_TYPE
    beta:  DATA_TYPE

    # Tunable blocking and vectorization parameters
    TI: int  # tile size along i (rows of C / A), e.g., 64
    TJ: int  # tile size along j (cols of C / rows of A), e.g., 64
    TK: int  # tile size along k (reduction dim / columns of A), e.g., 64
    VF: int  # vector length for k-dimension vectorization (e.g., 8 for AVX2 double)

computation:
    # SYRK semantics (BLAS: UPLO='L', TRANS='N'):
    #   C := alpha * A * A^T + beta * C
    # but only for the lower triangle j <= i.

    SCALE:
        # Scale only the lower triangular part by beta.
        # Upper triangle C[i,j] (j > i) is intentionally left unchanged,
        # matching the original kernel.
        for i in [0, N):
            for j in [0, i]:
                C[i, j] = beta * C[i, j]

    UPDATE:
        # Symmetric rank-k update on the lower triangle:
        #
        #   C[i,j] = C[i,j] + alpha * sum_k A[i,k] * A[j,k],  for j <= i
        #
        # Written as a per-(i,j) reduction so that the accumulation over k
        # can be kept in registers. This drastically reduces the number of
        # loads/stores of C compared to updating C[i,j] inside the k-loop.
        for i in [0, N):
            for j in [0, i]:
                C[i, j] += alpha * sum(k in [0, M), A[i, k] * A[j, k])

dependencies:
    # Each (i,j) entry must be scaled before it is updated.
    for i in [0, N), j in [0, i]:
        SCALE(i, j) -> UPDATE(i, j)

optimization:
    # ---------------------------
    # 1. Blocking / tiling
    # ---------------------------
    # Block i, j, and k to improve cache reuse:
    # - i, j blocking keeps a small C-tile in cache while it is updated.
    # - k blocking lets us sweep over columns of A in cache-sized chunks.
    #
    # Only (i,j) with j <= i are active; rectangular tiles are used, but
    # elements with j > i inside a tile are simply skipped.
    block(i, I, TI)   # I: tile index for rows of C / A
    block(j, J, TJ)   # J: tile index for columns of C / rows of A
    block(k, K, TK)   # K: tile index for reduction dimension

    # Make the tile loops outermost: for each (I,J) tile of C, accumulate
    # all contributions from K-tiles before moving on. This is the usual
    # blocked-SYRK/GEMM structure.
    hoist(I)
    hoist(J)
    hoist(K)

    # Within each (I,J) tile:
    #   - iterate over i, j in their tile ranges
    #   - enforce j <= i (skip j > i) to preserve lower-triangular semantics.

    # ---------------------------
    # 2. Parallelization
    # ---------------------------
    # Different (i,j) pairs are independent except for their own k-reduction.
    # Parallelizing over tiles of i (and optionally j) exposes coarse-grain
    # parallelism without violating dependencies.
    parallelize(I)
    # (Optionally, an implementation may also parallelize over J or use a
    # 2D (I,J) decomposition to improve load balance on many-core machines.)

    # ---------------------------
    # 3. Vectorization and unrolling
    # ---------------------------
    # In UPDATE, the inner reduction is a dot product over k:
    #   sum_k A[i,k] * A[j,k]
    # For fixed (i,j), A[i,*] and A[j,*] are both accessed with unit stride
    # in k when A is row-major, which is ideal for SIMD.
    #
    # Vectorize the k loop, and unroll for more ILP.
    vectorize(k, VF)
    unroll(k, 4)

    # ---------------------------
    # 4. Scalar hoisting inside innermost loops
    # ---------------------------
    # Within the innermost (i,j,k) loops, hoist the multiplication by alpha
    # and reuse A[i,k] across operations when possible.
    #
    # Conceptually, for each fixed (i,j) and k:
    #   t_i = A[i, k]
    #   t   = alpha * t_i
    #   C[i, j] += t * A[j, k]
    #
    # This reduces one multiply by alpha per iteration of k and encourages
    # the compiler to keep t_i and t in registers. It does not require
    # extra arrays, only scalar temporaries.

    # ---------------------------
    # 5. Register-level accumulation for C
    # ---------------------------
    # The use of sum(k, ...) already specifies a reduction. Implementations
    # should realize this as a scalar accumulator in registers:
    #
    #   s = 0
    #   for k in K-tile:
    #       s += A[i,k] * A[j,k]
    #   C[i,j] += alpha * s
    #
    # This minimizes memory traffic for C: each C[i,j] is loaded and stored
    # only once per full reduction over k, in contrast to updating it on
    # every k-iteration as in the original loop nest.

domain:
    i: dim in [0, N)          # row index of C and A
    j: dim in [0, N)          # column index of C, row index of A in second factor
    k: dim in [0, M)          # inner-product dimension over columns of A

data:
    # A is an N×M matrix, stored row-major.
    # Access pattern in the optimized kernel primarily walks along rows (varying k).
    A[i, k]: in DATA_TYPE = (i, k) -> i * M + k

    # C is an N×N matrix, stored row-major.
    # Only the lower triangle (j <= i) is updated; the upper triangle (j > i) is left unchanged.
    C[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j

parameters:
    N: int > 0                  # matrix size for C (N×N) and first dimension of A
    M: int > 0                  # second dimension of A (N×M)
    alpha: DATA_TYPE
    beta:  DATA_TYPE

    # Cache/blocking and vectorization tuning parameters (chosen per target machine)
    TI: int > 0                 # tile size along i (e.g., 64 or 128)
    TJ: int > 0                 # tile size along j (e.g., 64 or 128)
    TK: int > 0                 # tile size along k (e.g., 128 or 256)
    VLEN: int > 0               # SIMD vector length along k (e.g., 4 for AVX2 double, 8 for AVX2 float)
    UJ: int > 0                 # unroll factor along j (e.g., 2–4)
    UK: int > 0                 # unroll factor along k (e.g., 2–8)

computation:
    # SYRK (symmetric rank-k update) on the lower triangle:
    #   For all 0 <= i < N and 0 <= j <= i:
    #       C[i, j] = beta * C[i, j] + alpha * sum_{k=0..M-1} A[i, k] * A[j, k]
    #
    # Elements with j > i (upper triangle) are never modified by the kernel and
    # retain their initialization values.

    SCALE:
        for i in [0, N):
            for j in [0, i+1):              # 0 <= j <= i  (lower triangle only)
                C[i, j] = beta * C[i, j]

    UPDATE:
        for i in [0, N):
            for j in [0, i+1):              # 0 <= j <= i
                C[i, j] += alpha * sum(k in [0, M): A[i, k] * A[j, k])

dependencies:
    # For each (i, j) with 0 <= j <= i, SCALE(i, j) must complete before UPDATE(i, j).
    for i in [0, N), j in [0, i+1):
        SCALE(i, j) -> UPDATE(i, j)

    # Within UPDATE, the sum over k is a reduction:
    #   For fixed (i, j), iterations at different k contribute additively and can be
    #   reordered or vectorized as a canonical reduction, but must be completed
    #   before the final value of C[i, j] is committed.

optimization:
    #---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 1. Fuse scaling and update on C to reduce memory traffic
    #---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # fuse(X, Y): loop-fusion directive. Merge the loop nests of labeled
    # computations X and Y that share the same (i, j) domain, so that each
    # C[i, j] is loaded and stored only once.
    fuse(SCALE, UPDATE)

    # After fusion, the effective computation becomes, for 0 <= j <= i:
    #   tmp = beta * C[i, j]
    #   tmp += alpha * sum_k A[i, k] * A[j, k]
    #   C[i, j] = tmp

    #---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 2. Make k the innermost dimension to exploit row-contiguous access in A
    #---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # In the fused loop nest, interchange j and k so that the reduction over k
    # is innermost. This turns the inner kernel into a dot product:
    #
    #   for i:
    #     for j in [0, i+1):
    #       tmp = beta * C[i, j]
    #       for k in [0, M):
    #         tmp += alpha * A[i, k] * A[j, k]
    #       C[i, j] = tmp
    #
    # A[i, k] and A[j, k] are accessed with k varying fastest, so we traverse
    # contiguous rows in A, which is row-major.
    interchange(j, k)

    #---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 3. Cache blocking (tiling) in i, j, and k
    #---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # block(D, TD, T): split loop dimension D into an outer tile index TD and
    # an inner intra-tile index, with tile size T. The triangular condition
    # j <= i is preserved by applying it inside the innermost tile loops.
    #
    # Tiling improves temporal locality by reusing A rows and C tiles while they
    # reside in caches.

    block(i, I, TI)    # i = I * TI + ii
    block(j, J, TJ)    # j = J * TJ + jj
    block(k, K, TK)    # k = K * TK + kk

    # Execute tiles in i-major order (I outer), then j-major (J), then k-major (K).
    # Within each (I, J, K) tile, the innermost loops iterate over ii, jj, kk,
    # with a guard "if j <= i" for triangular correctness.
    hoist(I)
    hoist(J)
    hoist(K)

    #---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 4. Parallelization across i-tiles
    #---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Each C[i, j] (j <= i) is written exactly once and depends only on row i
    # and row j of A plus the initial C[i, j]; there are no cross-(i, j)
    # dependencies. Thus, tiles along the i-dimension can safely execute in
    # parallel.
    parallelize(I)

    # Note: A is read-only and shared; C tiles updated by distinct I tiles
    # do not overlap because i ranges in different I tiles are disjoint.

    #---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 5. Vectorization and unrolling
    #---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # With k as the innermost loop, the update for a fixed (i, j) is a dot
    # product of two contiguous length-M row segments of A:
    #
    #   tmp += alpha * A[i, k] * A[j, k]
    #
    # This is a canonical reduction and maps well to SIMD on k.

    vectorize(k, VLEN)   # vectorize the k-loop (dot-product reduction)
    unroll(k, UK)        # unroll k to increase ILP within each vectorized chunk

    # For additional throughput on C and partial reuse of A[j, :], unroll j
    # within each tile so that multiple C[i, j] accumulators live in registers
    # while streaming through a row of A[i, :].
    unroll(j, UJ)

    #---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 6. Scalar strength reduction for alpha
    #---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # The product alpha * A[i, k] is invariant with respect to j once i and k
    # are fixed. Within each (i, k) iteration, compute it once and reuse for all
    # j in the same tile.
    #
    # This does not require an additional N×M array; a per-(i, k) scalar is
    # sufficient and can live in a register:
    #
    #   a_ik = alpha * A[i, k]
    #   for j in tile with j <= i:
    #       tmp_j += a_ik * A[j, k]
    #
    # This reduces the number of multiplications by alpha by a factor of
    # approximately (i+1) per (i, k) and is naturally applied inside the
    # vectorized/unrolled innermost loops.
    #
    # (No explicit directive: this is a local algebraic optimization inside
    # the transformed inner kernel and keeps extra memory well below +50%.)
--- END OF MODEL: syrk-02 ---

--- START OF MODEL: syrk-03 ---
domain:
    i: dim in [0, N)
    j: dim in [0, N)
    k: dim in [0, M)

data:
    # A is N x M. We store it in column-major form so that each column A[*, k]
    # is contiguous in memory, matching a k-outer loop structure.
    A[i, k]: in DATA_TYPE = (i, k) -> i + k * N   # Column-major

    # C is N x N, stored full in row-major form. Only the lower triangle (j <= i)
    # is updated by the SYRK kernel; the upper triangle is left unchanged.
    C[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j  # Row-major

parameters:
    alpha: DATA_TYPE
    beta: DATA_TYPE

    # Tuning parameters (can be chosen based on cache sizes and SIMD width)
    TI: int  # tile size for i (rows of C / A)
    TK: int  # tile size for k (columns of A)
    VEC: int # SIMD width in elements along j

computation:
    # Phase 1: scale only the lower triangle of C by beta.
    SCALE:
        for i in [0, N):
            for j in [0, i]:
                C[i, j] = beta * C[i, j]

    # Phase 2: symmetric rank-k update on the lower triangle:
    #          C_lower := C_lower + alpha * A * A^T
    #
    # Mathematically, for all 0 <= j <= i < N:
    #   C[i, j] = C[i, j] + alpha * sum_{k=0..M-1} A[i, k] * A[j, k]
    UPDATE:
        for i in [0, N):
            for j in [0, i]:
                C[i, j] = C[i, j] + alpha * sum(k in [0, M), A[i, k] * A[j, k])

optimization:
    # --- High-level structure -------------------------------------------------
    # SCALE and UPDATE are executed in sequence. SCALE does not depend on A and
    # can be parallelized and vectorized independently. UPDATE is the main
    # compute-intensive part and is optimized aggressively below.

    # --- SCALE optimization ---------------------------------------------------
    # SCALE touches each C[i, j] (j <= i) exactly once. Rows are independent.
    parallelize(i)          # run different i-rows (or i-tiles) in parallel
    vectorize(j, VEC)       # vectorize along contiguous j within each row

    # --- UPDATE optimization --------------------------------------------------
    # 1. Treat UPDATE as a 3D loop nest over (i, j, k) with the triangular
    #    constraint j <= i. We'll perform loop transformations on this nest.

    # 2. Tile i and k to improve cache reuse:
    #    - i-tiling keeps a strip of rows of C and A in cache.
    #    - k-tiling reuses A-columns and C blocks across multiple k values.
    block(i, I, TI)         # i = I * TI + i_inner
    block(k, K, TK)         # k = K * TK + k_inner

    # 3. Hoist tile loops so we iterate over k-tiles outermost, then i-tiles:
    #    for K:
    #      for I:
    #        for i in tile I:
    #          for j in [0, i]:
    #            for k in tile K:
    #              C[i, j] += alpha * A[i, k] * A[j, k]
    #
    # This ordering:
    #   - Processes A by columns (k fixed) and rows (i, j varying),
    #   - Matches the column-major layout of A (A[*, k] contiguous),
    #   - Keeps C tiles hot in cache while accumulating over a k-tile.
    hoist(K)
    hoist(I)

    # 4. Parallelize across i-tiles: each (I, j<=i) block of C is independent
    #    for a fixed K, because each C[i, j] is updated by exactly one (i, j)
    #    pair and accumulates over k only.
    parallelize(I)

    # 5. Within each i-tile:
    #    - Keep j as the innermost loop for unit-stride access to C[i, j],
    #      which is stored row-major.
    #    - Vectorize j and unroll the inner k-loop to expose ILP and FMAs.
    vectorize(j, VEC)
    unroll(k, 4)

    # 6. Arithmetic strength reduction / scalar hoisting:
    #    For each fixed (i, k) inside an (I, K) tile, compute:
    #       t_ik = alpha * A[i, k]
    #    once and reuse it across all j in [0, i].
    #    This reduces the inner update to:
    #       C[i, j] += t_ik * A[j, k]
    #    cutting the number of multiplications roughly in half when i is large.
    #    The compiler can realize this via common-subexpression elimination.
    #    (No extra arrays are introduced; t_ik lives in a register.)
    #    #scalar-hoist(alpha * A[i, k], over=j)

    # 7. Triangular domain handling with tiling:
    #    Tiling is applied over the full i- and k-ranges, but all updates are
    #    guarded (either explicitly or by loop bounds) with j <= i to ensure
    #    that:
    #      - Only the lower triangle of C is updated,
    #      - The upper triangle C[i, j] for j > i remains equal to its
    #        initialized value, matching the original kernel semantics.
--- END OF MODEL: syrk-03 ---

--- START OF MODEL: syrk-04 ---
domain:
    i: dim in [0, N)
    j: dim in [0, N)
    k: dim in [0, M)

data:
    # A is an N×M matrix.
    # Store A in column-major order to make accesses A[j, k] contiguous when j varies:
    #   - layout: (i, k) ↦ k * N + i
    #   - this matches the use pattern A[j, k] with j as the inner loop index.
    A[i, k]: in DATA_TYPE = (i, k) -> k * N + i  # column-major

    # C is an N×N matrix, used only in its lower triangular part (j <= i).
    # Keep row-major to make C[i, j] contiguous when j varies:
    #   - layout: (i, j) ↦ i * N + j
    C[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j  # row-major, only j <= i updated

parameters:
    alpha: DATA_TYPE
    beta:  DATA_TYPE

    # Tunable tile sizes for cache blocking
    TI: int  # tile size along i (rows of C and A)
    TJ: int  # tile size along j (columns of C; rows of A in the second index)
    TK: int  # tile size along k (reduction dimension, columns of A)

    # Tunable SIMD vector width along j (depends on hardware, e.g., 8 for AVX2 doubles)
    VF: int

computation:
    # Symmetric rank-k update, lower triangle only:
    #   For 0 <= i < N, 0 <= j <= i:
    #     C[i, j] = beta * C[i, j] + alpha * sum_{k=0..M-1} A[i, k] * A[j, k]
    #
    # Entries with j > i are left unchanged, matching the original kernel.
    SYRK_UPDATE:
        for i in [0, N), j in [0, N):
            if j <= i:
                C[i, j] = beta * C[i, j] +
                          alpha * sum(k in [0, M), A[i, k] * A[j, k])

optimization:
    # --- 1. Triangular blocking over (i, j) and panel blocking over k -----------------
    # Tile i and j to operate on sub-blocks of C and the corresponding rows of A.
    # This improves reuse of A and C in caches.
    block(i, I, TI)          # I: tile index for rows of C and A
    block(j, J, TJ)          # J: tile index for columns of C (and row index j)
    block(k, K, TK)          # K: tile index for reduction dimension (columns of A)

    # Execute tiles in an order that keeps A panels and C tiles in cache:
    #   outer I → K → J
    # This lets each A[:, K] panel be reused across many (i, j) pairs
    # before moving to the next K.
    hoist(I)
    hoist(K)
    hoist(J)

    # Within each (I, J, K) tile:
    #   - i is outer (row of C),
    #   - k is middle (column “panel” of A),
    #   - j is innermost (column of C / row index into A).
    #
    # We keep the original j <= i triangular condition inside the tile,
    # so rectangular tiles that cross the diagonal are safely masked.
    #
    # Mathematically, this corresponds to interchanging the j and k loops
    # of the unblocked syrk update while preserving the reduction over k.
    interchange(j, k)

    # --- 2. Parallelization -----------------------------------------------------------
    # Different rows i of C (and their lower-triangular elements) are independent.
    # Parallelize at the tile level to amortize scheduling overhead:
    parallelize(I)

    # --- 3. Vectorization and unrolling ----------------------------------------------
    # With the chosen layouts:
    #   - C[i, j] is contiguous in j (row-major).
    #   - A[j, k] is contiguous in j (column-major).
    # After interchanging so that j is innermost, we get perfectly aligned,
    # unit-stride accesses to both C and A in the inner loop over j.
    #
    # Vectorize along j to exploit SIMD on:
    #   C[i, j] += alpha * A[i, k] * A[j, k]
    vectorize(j, VF)

    # Unroll the k-loop within each tile to increase ILP and utilize FMA units better.
    # The unroll factor is tunable; 4 is a reasonable default.
    unroll(k, 4)

    # --- 4. Scalar hoisting / strength reduction -------------------------------------
    # Within a fixed (i, k), the factor alpha * A[i, k] is reused for all j in the
    # current tile. Hoist this product out of the inner j-loop into a scalar
    # temporary (implemented during code generation, not as an extra array):
    #
    #   tmp_aik = alpha * A[i, k]
    #   for j in J-tile, j <= i:
    #       C[i, j] += tmp_aik * A[j, k]
    #
    # This reduces repeated multiplications of alpha * A[i, k] and keeps A[i, k]
    # in registers while streaming through A[j, k] and C[i, j].
    # (Expressed here as a comment-level optimization, applied inside the
    #   innermost generated loops.)
    # hoist alpha*A[i, k] into a scalar per (i, k) to avoid redundant work

    # --- 5. Notes on correctness and numerical behavior ------------------------------
    # - The j <= i guard preserves the original “UPLO = 'L'” semantics:
    #   only the lower triangle of C is updated; entries with j > i are unchanged.
    # - Reordering loops and blocking reorders floating-point additions in the
    #   reduction over k. This is mathematically equivalent to the original
    #   computation (modulo round-off), which matches the intended BLAS SYRK
    #   semantics.
--- END OF MODEL: syrk-04 ---

--- START OF MODEL: syrk-05 ---
domain:
    i: dim in [0, N)
    j: dim in [0, N)
    k: dim in [0, M)

data:
    # A is N x M, stored column-major so that A[*, k] is contiguous in memory.
    # This matches the outer-product–style syrk update that sweeps columns of A.
    A[i, k]: in DATA_TYPE = (i, k) -> k * N + i

    # C is N x N, stored row-major as in the original code.
    # Only the lower triangle (0 <= j <= i) is updated in the kernel;
    # entries with j > i retain their input values.
    C[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j

parameters:
    alpha: DATA_TYPE
    beta:  DATA_TYPE

    # Tunable optimization parameters (chosen to match cache and SIMD properties
    # of the target machine; example values are indicative, not mandatory).
    TI: int  # tile size for i (rows of C), e.g., 64
    TJ: int  # tile size for j (columns within a row / lower-triangular segment), e.g., 64
    TK: int  # tile size for k (columns of A), e.g., 256
    VEC: int # SIMD width (elements) along j, e.g., 8 for double on AVX-512
    UF:  int # unroll factor for innermost j loop, e.g., 4

computation:
    # SYRK semantics on the lower triangle:
    #   For all 0 <= j <= i < N:
    #     C[i,j] = beta * C[i,j] + alpha * sum_{k=0..M-1} A[i,k] * A[j,k]
    #
    # Elements with j > i are left unchanged (inout semantics).
    SYRK:
        for i in [0, N), j in [0, i]:
            C[i, j] = beta * C[i, j] + alpha * sum(k in [0, M): A[i, k] * A[j, k])

dependencies:
    # For each (i,j) with 0 <= j <= i, the only dependence is the reduction over k.
    # All (i,j) pairs are independent of each other.
    for i in [0, N), j in [0, i], k in [0, M):
        SYRK(i, j) -> SYRK(i, j)  # self-dependence along k models the reduction

optimization:
    # 1) Separate scaling from the rank-k update.
    #    This avoids mixing the beta scaling with the k-reduction and lets us keep
    #    C[i,j] resident in cache while performing multiple k-updates.
    #
    #    SCALE:
    #      for i, j with 0 <= j <= i: C[i,j] = beta * C[i,j]
    #    UPDATE:
    #      for i, j with 0 <= j <= i: C[i,j] += alpha * sum_k A[i,k] * A[j,k]
    split(SYRK) into (SCALE, UPDATE)

    # 2) Explicitly restrict both SCALE and UPDATE to the lower triangle to avoid
    #    any accidental work on the upper triangle.
    restrict_domain(SCALE,  condition = (0 <= j) and (j <= i))
    restrict_domain(UPDATE, condition = (0 <= j) and (j <= i))

    # 3) Implement UPDATE as a blocked outer-product over columns of A:
    #
    #    Mathematically:
    #      for k in [0, M):
    #        for i in [0, N):
    #          for j in [0, i]:
    #            C[i,j] += alpha * A[i,k] * A[j,k]
    #
    #    This is equivalent to the original sum over k for each (i,j), up to
    #    floating‑point reassociation. With A in column-major layout, accesses
    #    A[i,k] and A[j,k] are contiguous as i or j varies, improving locality.
    reorder(UPDATE, order = [k, i, j])

    # 4) Arithmetic optimization: precompute v_i = alpha * A[i,k] once per (i,k),
    #    reuse across all j for that (i,k), and do:
    #        C[i,j] += v_i * A[j,k]
    #    This saves one multiplication by alpha per inner iteration over j.
    #    v_i is a scalar temporary inside the (k,i) loops, not an additional array.
    precompute(v_i = alpha * A[i, k], scope = [k, i], reused_over = j)

    # 5) Blocking (tiling) for cache:
    #    Tile i, j, and k to keep working tiles of C and panels of A in cache.
    #
    #    Conceptual structure for UPDATE after tiling:
    #      for I in [0, N) step TI:                    # tile over rows of C
    #        for J in [0, I] step TJ:                  # tile over cols (lower triangle)
    #          for K in [0, M) step TK:                # tile over columns of A
    #            for k in K:
    #              for i in I:
    #                v_i = alpha * A[i, k]
    #                for j in J with j <= i:
    #                  C[i, j] += v_i * A[j, k]
    #
    #    The triangular condition j <= i is enforced inside the j-loop within each tile.
    block(i, I, TI)
    block(j, J, TJ)
    block(k, K, TK)

    # Hoist the tile loops to the outermost level so that:
    #   outer: I, J, K
    #   inner: k, i, j
    # This maximizes reuse of C[I,J] tiles and A[*,K] panels.
    hoist(I)
    hoist(J)
    hoist(K)

    # 6) Parallelization:
    #    - Parallelize across row tiles I for both SCALE and UPDATE.
    #    - Each C[i,j] (with j <= i) belongs to exactly one row i and thus to exactly
    #      one tile I, so there are no write conflicts between threads.
    #    - The reduction over k remains sequential within each (i,j), avoiding the
    #      need for atomics or per-thread partial sums.
    parallelize(I) on SCALE
    parallelize(I) on UPDATE

    # 7) Vectorization and unrolling:
    #    - C is row-major, so within a fixed i, the elements C[i,j] for increasing j
    #      are contiguous in memory.
    #    - Make j the innermost loop inside each tile, vectorize it, and unroll it.
    #      This exposes FMAs of the form C[i,j] += v_i * A[j,k] on x64.
    vectorize(j, VEC)
    unroll(j, UF)

    # 8) (Optional) Packed lower-triangular storage for C:
    #    - To further reduce working-set size, one can conceptually store only the
    #      lower triangle of C in a packed 1D array C_lower[p], with
    #          p = i * (i + 1) / 2 + j,  0 <= j <= i < N.
    #    - A preprocessing step copies C’s lower triangle into C_lower; a
    #      postprocessing step writes back into the full N x N C for printing.
    #    - This uses at most ~50% more memory than the original full C and A
    #      combined if both representations are kept, and improves cache locality
    #      for the actual computation, which then only touches C_lower.
    #
    #    Left disabled by default to keep the visible layout identical to the
    #    original row-major N x N matrix.
    #pack_lower_triangle(C, C_lower)  # disabled by default
--- END OF MODEL: syrk-05 ---

#include <stdio.h>
#include <unistd.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <math.h>

/* Include polybench common header. */
#include <polybench.h>

/* Include benchmark-specific header. */
#include "syrk.h"


/* Array initialization. */
static
void init_array(int n, int m,
		DATA_TYPE *alpha,
		DATA_TYPE *beta,
		DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(C,N,N,n,n),
		DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(A,N,M,n,m))
{
  int i, j;

  *alpha = 1.5;
  *beta = 1.2;
  for (i = 0; i < n; i++)
    for (j = 0; j < m; j++)
      A[i][j] = (DATA_TYPE) ((i*j+1)%n) / n;
  for (i = 0; i < n; i++)
    for (j = 0; j < n; j++)
      C[i][j] = (DATA_TYPE) ((i*j+2)%m) / m;
}


/* DCE code. Must scan the entire live-out data.
   Can be used also to check the correctness of the output. */
static
void print_array(int n,
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(C,N,N,n,n))
{
  int i, j;

  POLYBENCH_DUMP_START;
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_BEGIN("C");
  for (i = 0; i < n; i++)
    for (j = 0; j < n; j++) {
	if ((i * n + j) % 20 == 0) fprintf (POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, "\n");
	fprintf (POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, DATA_PRINTF_MODIFIER, C[i][j]);
    }
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_END("C");
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_FINISH;
}


/* Main computational kernel. The whole function will be timed,
   including the call and return. */
static
void kernel_syrk[[gnu::flatten, gnu::noinline]](int n, int m,
		 DATA_TYPE alpha,
		 DATA_TYPE beta,
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(C,N,N,n,n),
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(A,N,M,n,m))
{
  int i, j, k;

//BLAS PARAMS
//TRANS = 'N'
//UPLO  = 'L'
// =>  Form  C := alpha*A*A**T + beta*C.
//A is NxM
//C is NxN
#pragma scop
  for (i = 0; i < _PB_N; i++) {
    for (j = 0; j <= i; j++)
      C[i][j] *= beta;
    for (k = 0; k < _PB_M; k++) {
      for (j = 0; j <= i; j++)
        C[i][j] += alpha * A[i][k] * A[j][k];
    }
  }
#pragma endscop

}


int main(int argc, char** argv)
{
  /* Retrieve problem size. */
  int n = N;
  int m = M;

  /* Variable declaration/allocation. */
  DATA_TYPE alpha;
  DATA_TYPE beta;
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(C,DATA_TYPE,N,N,n,n);
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(A,DATA_TYPE,N,M,n,m);

  /* Initialize array(s). */
  init_array (n, m, &alpha, &beta, POLYBENCH_ARRAY(C), POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A));

  /* Start timer. */
  polybench_start_instruments;

  /* Run kernel. */
  kernel_syrk (n, m, alpha, beta, POLYBENCH_ARRAY(C), POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A));

  /* Stop and print timer. */
  polybench_stop_instruments;
  polybench_print_instruments;

  /* Prevent dead-code elimination. All live-out data must be printed
     by the function call in argument. */
  polybench_prevent_dce(print_array(n, POLYBENCH_ARRAY(C)));

  /* Be clean. */
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(C);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(A);

  return 0;
}

    # Matrix dimensions (problem sizes)
    i: dim in [0, N)
    j: dim in [0, N)
    k: dim in [0, M)

data:
    # A is N x M, stored row-major: A[i][k]
    A[i, k]: in DATA_TYPE  = (i, k) -> i * M + k

    # C is N x N, stored row-major: C[i][j]
    # Only the lower triangle (j <= i) is updated by the kernel;
    # the upper triangle remains equal to its initialized values.
    C[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j

parameters:
    alpha: DATA_TYPE
    beta:  DATA_TYPE

    # Tunable blocking and vectorization parameters
    TI: int  # tile size along i (rows of C / A), e.g., 64
    TJ: int  # tile size along j (cols of C / rows of A), e.g., 64
    TK: int  # tile size along k (reduction dim / columns of A), e.g., 64
    VF: int  # vector length for k-dimension vectorization (e.g., 8 for AVX2 double)

computation:
    # SYRK semantics (BLAS: UPLO='L', TRANS='N'):
    #   C := alpha * A * A^T + beta * C
    # but only for the lower triangle j <= i.

    SCALE:
        # Scale only the lower triangular part by beta.
        # Upper triangle C[i,j] (j > i) is intentionally left unchanged,
        # matching the original kernel.
        for i in [0, N):
            for j in [0, i]:
                C[i, j] = beta * C[i, j]

    UPDATE:
        # Symmetric rank-k update on the lower triangle:
        #
        #   C[i,j] = C[i,j] + alpha * sum_k A[i,k] * A[j,k],  for j <= i
        #
        # Written as a per-(i,j) reduction so that the accumulation over k
        # can be kept in registers. This drastically reduces the number of
        # loads/stores of C compared to updating C[i,j] inside the k-loop.
        for i in [0, N):
            for j in [0, i]:
                C[i, j] += alpha * sum(k in [0, M), A[i, k] * A[j, k])

dependencies:
    # Each (i,j) entry must be scaled before it is updated.
    for i in [0, N), j in [0, i]:
        SCALE(i, j) -> UPDATE(i, j)

optimization:
    # ---------------------------
    # 1. Blocking / tiling
    # ---------------------------
    # Block i, j, and k to improve cache reuse:
    # - i, j blocking keeps a small C-tile in cache while it is updated.
    # - k blocking lets us sweep over columns of A in cache-sized chunks.
    #
    # Only (i,j) with j <= i are active; rectangular tiles are used, but
    # elements with j > i inside a tile are simply skipped.
    block(i, I, TI)   # I: tile index for rows of C / A
    block(j, J, TJ)   # J: tile index for columns of C / rows of A
    block(k, K, TK)   # K: tile index for reduction dimension

    # Make the tile loops outermost: for each (I,J) tile of C, accumulate
    # all contributions from K-tiles before moving on. This is the usual
    # blocked-SYRK/GEMM structure.
    hoist(I)
    hoist(J)
    hoist(K)

    # Within each (I,J) tile:
    #   - iterate over i, j in their tile ranges
    #   - enforce j <= i (skip j > i) to preserve lower-triangular semantics.

    # ---------------------------
    # 2. Parallelization
    # ---------------------------
    # Different (i,j) pairs are independent except for their own k-reduction.
    # Parallelizing over tiles of i (and optionally j) exposes coarse-grain
    # parallelism without violating dependencies.
    parallelize(I)
    # (Optionally, an implementation may also parallelize over J or use a
    # 2D (I,J) decomposition to improve load balance on many-core machines.)

    # ---------------------------
    # 3. Vectorization and unrolling
    # ---------------------------
    # In UPDATE, the inner reduction is a dot product over k:
    #   sum_k A[i,k] * A[j,k]
    # For fixed (i,j), A[i,*] and A[j,*] are both accessed with unit stride
    # in k when A is row-major, which is ideal for SIMD.
    #
    # Vectorize the k loop, and unroll for more ILP.
    vectorize(k, VF)
    unroll(k, 4)

    # 4. Scalar hoisting inside innermost loops
    # ---------------------------
    # Within the innermost (i,j,k) loops, hoist the multiplication by alpha
    # and reuse A[i,k] across operations when possible.
    #
    # Conceptually, for each fixed (i,j) and k:
    #   t_i = A[i, k]
    #   t   = alpha * t_i
    #   C[i, j] += t * A[j, k]
    #
    # This reduces one multiply by alpha per iteration of k and encourages
    # the compiler to keep t_i and t in registers. It does not require
    # extra arrays, only scalar temporaries.

    # ---------------------------
    # 5. Register-level accumulation for C
    # ---------------------------
    # The use of sum(k, ...) already specifies a reduction. Implementations
    # should realize this as a scalar accumulator in registers:
    #
    #   s = 0
    #   for k in K-tile:
    #       s += A[i,k] * A[j,k]
    #   C[i,j] += alpha * s
    #
    # This minimizes memory traffic for C: each C[i,j] is loaded and stored
    # only once per full reduction over k, in contrast to updating it on
    # every k-iteration as in the original loop nest.
